forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Microsoft's FY2026 10-K reports revenue of $331,839m, operating income of $155,237m, other income net of $10,697m, pretax income of $165,934m, tax expense of $32,185m, net income of $133,749m, diluted EPS of $17.95, and 7,453m weighted-average diluted shares. Segment revenue/operating income was Productivity and Business Processes $139,996m/$83,879m, Intelligent Cloud $137,791m/$56,972m, and More Personal Computing $54,052m/$14,386m. Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 27% to $214.4b, Azure and other cloud services grew 41%, and commercial remaining performance obligation reached $678b. The filing also reports FY2026 interest and dividends income of $3,301m, total interest expense of $3,051m, finance-lease interest of $2,547m, finance-lease liabilities of $66,594m, finance-lease right-of-use assets added of $24,608m, cash additions to property and equipment of $115,948m, and $329.1b of additional primarily datacenter leases not yet commenced, expected to commence from FY2027 through FY2033 with terms of 1 to 20 years. REPORTED-TO-NORMALIZED BRIDGE: $331,839m revenue -> $155,237m operating income -> +$10,697m reported other income net -> $165,934m pretax -> -$32,185m tax -> $133,749m net income -> $17.95 diluted EPS on 7,453m diluted shares. Microsoft supplies FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.28 after removing $0.67 of OpenAI gains. Subtracting the separately disclosed aggregate Q4 $0.27 benefit produces only a provisional $17.01 reference because the release does not establish clean non-overlap or each component's after-tax contribution; $17.01 is not an input to any terminal expression. MODEL INFERENCE: Each terminal expression starts with FY2026 revenue and separately models operating income, ordinary-debt interest, existing finance-lease interest, incremental finance-lease interest tied to the disclosed uncommenced lease pipeline, tax, and diluted shares. Cash interest/dividend income, FX/other, and investment marks receive zero terminal credit. FY2026 ordinary-debt/other interest is provisionally inferred as $3,051m total interest expense less $2,547m finance-lease interest, or $504m; the subtraction and all outputs require independent verification. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Microsoft can beat QQQ if Azure/Copilot monetization converts backlog into low-teens revenue growth while software economics and datacenter utilization offset lease-funded infrastructure. The contrary case is that AI capacity commitments raise below-operating-line lease interest and depress margins faster than monetization, making diversified QQQ superior.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Microsoft has source-supported demand signals: FY2026 Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 27%, Azure and other cloud services grew 41%, and commercial RPO reached $678b, alongside broad productivity, cloud, developer, security, and consumer distribution. The counter-thesis is explicit: the Base capex-digestion and Bull index-catches-up cases let QQQ win when infrastructure returns lag or broader Nasdaq beneficiaries compound faster. Mechanical evaluation of the six authored joint states produces a 0.65 strict probability-to-beat from the 0.08, 0.12, 0.35, and 0.10 winning-state weights; that figure is a subjective research output, not a calibrated probability or portfolio approval.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply the Structural deceleration downside if either operating pre-breach trigger occurs: (1) Azure revenue growth is below 20% year over year in constant currency for two consecutive reported quarters, versus the FY2026 baseline of 41%; or (2) Microsoft Cloud gross margin is below 60% for two consecutive reported quarters while cash property-and-equipment additions plus finance-lease additions remain above 35% of revenue. FY2026 Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 66%, so trigger (2) was not breached, but its spending limb was already true: $115,948m cash additions plus $24,608m finance-lease additions equals $140,556m, or a model-computed 42.356685% of $331,839m revenue, subject to independent verification. A separate financing pre-breach trigger applies at the first reported 10-Q or 10-K showing any of: finance-lease liabilities at or above 25% of trailing revenue; annualized finance-lease interest at or above 1.0% of trailing revenue; or cash property-and-equipment additions plus finance-lease additions above 45% of trailing revenue for two consecutive reported quarters while Microsoft Cloud gross margin is below 63%. FY2026 model-computed baselines, requiring independent verification, were $66,594m/20.0682% for finance-lease liabilities/revenue, $2,547m/0.7675% for finance-lease interest/revenue, and 42.356685% for cash plus finance-lease additions/revenue. Consequence of either trigger: cap revenue CAGR at 8%, terminal operating margin at 42%, diluted-share growth at no less than 0.5%, and terminal P/E at 24x; give no cash-interest, FX, investment-mark, or buyback credit; set ordinary-debt and existing finance-lease interest no lower than their latest annualized disclosures; and calculate incremental lease interest as not-yet-commenced commitments multiplied by at least a 70% five-year activation share, 60% finance-lease classification share, and 5% imputed rate. Observation sources are subsequent earnings releases and 10-Q/10-K filings. These are author risk controls, not company guidance.

forecasts.theme: AI/cloud compounder: Azure, Copilot, developer tooling, security, and enterprise distribution
forecasts.limitations: GuruFocus summary, annual and quarterly financials, and key ratios were pulled. Its endpoint exposed FY2017-FY2026 plus TTM annual columns rather than 15 annual years, so no 15-year claim is made. GuruFocus segment retrieval failed response-schema validation; SEC XBRL segment figures are used instead. The 2026-10-07 close is GuruFocus's $529.76 price stamped 16:00 EDT and is corroborated by the dated summary/OHLC payload described in the source record. FY2026 is the latest reported annual/TTM period because no FY2027 quarter was public by the snapshot. The $17.01 reference is provisional and unused. The $329.1b pipeline is described as primarily datacenter leases, but the filing does not establish which future arrangements will be finance versus operating leases, exact commencement by fiscal year, or future imputed rates. Activation, finance-classification, and imputed-rate assumptions are Human judgment, not Source facts. Holding existing finance-lease interest at no less than FY2026's $2,547m while adding scenario pipeline interest is a conservative floor, not guidance. The model gives no terminal cash-interest/dividend income, FX/other, investment-mark, or buyback credit and does not claim those items will literally be zero. Dividends are omitted to match the shared price-only benchmark. Regulatory remedies, AI supply/power constraints, customer concentration, OpenAI dependence, cyber events, tax disputes, unknown acquisitions, and accounting reclassification remain material residual risks. The controller-supplied full-precision scenario outputs are populated; all model-computed ratios, expression outputs, strict wins, marginals, and the 0.65 probability-to-beat still require independent arithmetic and evidence review.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: The six joint probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated execution/QQQ judgments selected independently of old rankings. They total exactly 1: QQQ bear 0.08+0.12=0.20, QQQ base 0.20+0.35=0.55, and QQQ bull 0.15+0.10=0.25. Within Bear, resilient cloud receives more weight than structural deceleration because backlog and diversified distribution may remain durable. Within Base, durable AI conversion is judged more likely than a severe capex-digestion lag, while the latter remains material. Within Bull, a broad Nasdaq AI rally outrunning Microsoft is more likely than Microsoft sustaining the supercycle assumptions. Mechanical comparison shows MSFT strictly beats QQQ in four states with 0.65 aggregate weight and loses in two states with 0.35 aggregate weight; the result remains an uncalibrated author judgment, not investment approval.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001404655, NYSE symbol HUBS, and common stock, $0.001 par. GuruFocus' 2026-10-07 16:04 EDT quote was $220.27. HubSpot had 306,446 customers at 2026-06-30; Q2 revenue was $911.740m, +20% reported and approximately 17.5% constant-currency in management commentary; subscription was 98% of H1 revenue. Q2 NRR was 102%, customer dollar retention was in the high 80s, and average subscription revenue per customer was $11,800. AI adoption was measurable but not separately monetized: more than 55% of Pro+ customers used agents or Breeze Assistant; monthly agentic actions exceeded 3x the start-of-year level; Data Agent had more than 16,000 activations, Prospecting Agent almost 17,000, Customer Agent more than 10,000, and Customer Agent resolved 72% of tickets without human escalation. SOURCE HISTORY: GuruFocus exposed 2017-2025 plus TTM, not 15 years; revenue per share rose from $10.199 in 2017 to $58.865 in 2025 and $65.42 TTM, while current three-year revenue and FCF growth were 17.8% and 39.4%. HubSpot's IPO was in 2014, so no 15-year public history is claimed. SOURCE REPORTED BRIDGE, USD millions: TTM revenue is 3131.266-1475.003+1792.735; TTM GAAP operating income is 7.379-(-52.096)+71.263; TTM GAAP net income is 45.911-(-25.051)+75.892; GuruFocus reports TTM diluted EPS of $2.825. Q2 GAAP operating income was $43.319m and net income $43.338m; nonoperating income was $6.248m, including $9.412m interest income, $(0.395)m interest expense, and $(2.769)m other expense. H1 tax expense was $12.969m on $88.861m pretax income; a full U.S. valuation allowance remained, so that tax rate is not durable. NORMALIZATION/OWNER-ECONOMICS BRIDGE: no adjusted EPS is used. The terminal model starts from reported revenue and applies a GAAP operating margin retaining recurring SBC, AI inference/hosting, acquired-intangible amortization, capitalized-software amortization, and ordinary acquisition/integration expense. Strict TTM owner FCF per share before acquisitions, in USD millions and million shares, is (760.717-325.932+421.580-53.165+29.370-35.074-130.624+65.857-74.292-528.153+257.668-244.227)/50: reported CFO less PP&E, capitalized software, and SBC, divided by FY2026 guided diluted shares. This deliberately does not add back SBC or assume buybacks. October's $65m-$75m restructuring cash charge is not normalized away. MODEL INFERENCE: CRM context, distribution, and agent adoption can sustain low/mid-teens revenue growth and expand GAAP margin, but Q2 buying friction, AI costs, and pricing changes make that unproven. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the six cases use a direct GAAP common-EPS bridge, not management's non-GAAP EPS, and QQQ remains the default pending independent Evidence & Risk and North Star PM review.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: HubSpot can beat QQQ if its installed CRM context converts AI trials and agents into durable paid credit or seat expansion while unified-suite adoption and internal AI productivity raise GAAP operating margin. The $220.27 price and GuruFocus 3.31x P/S and 14.26x reported P/FCF were far below prior expectations, so successful stabilization plus GAAP margin conversion can outweigh multiple normalization. This is unproven: Q2 constant-currency growth slowed to about 17.5%, NRR was only 102%, budget scrutiny lengthened sales cycles, and gross margin faced hosting, AI inference, and capitalized-software amortization pressure. QQQ is superior if AI commoditizes CRM, consumption pricing cannibalizes seats, inference costs offset productivity, customer growth or NRR weakens, or SBC-funded dilution persists. Scenario weights are subjective and uncalibrated; no legacy rank, score, hurdle, or expected IRR was translated into probability.
forecasts.falsifier: Operating trigger: if two consecutive reported quarters through 2028-09-30 show both constant-currency revenue growth below 12% and GAAP operating margin below 5%, versus Q2 2026 at about 17.5% and 4.8%, cap the central model at 8% revenue growth and 10% terminal GAAP margin and move at least 15 percentage points from central/upside to downside. Retention trigger: if company-reported NRR is 95% or lower for two consecutive quarters through 2028-09-30, versus 102% in Q2 2026, remove the 14%-19% growth paths unless paid AI usage independently offsets churn. Dilution trigger: if weighted diluted shares exceed 52.0m for two consecutive quarters before 2028-09-30, versus 50.615m in Q2 2026 and 50.0m FY2026 guidance, use at least 2% annual share growth and no buyback credit. Cost trigger: if GAAP subscription gross margin is below 78% for two consecutive quarters before 2028-09-30, versus about 83.7% in Q2 from $894.025m subscription revenue and $145.957m subscription cost, cap terminal GAAP operating margin at 12%. Sources are each quarterly 10-Q or earnings exhibit; consequences apply at the next refresh. None was evidenced as breached at the model date.

forecasts.limitations: No AI-agent revenue, paid conversion, cohort retention, inference-cost, or agent gross-margin KPI was disclosed; activation and usage therefore cannot establish incremental economics. September 2026 Analyst Day materials were not retrievable in the bounded source pass; the Oct. 6 8-K only says longer-term margin targets were reaffirmed. GuruFocus annual financial history exposed 2017-2025 plus TTM rather than 15 years, and its segment endpoint failed validation; SEC establishes one operating segment and 2025 geographic revenue of Americas $1,872.171m, Europe $1,010.968m, and Asia Pacific $248.127m. TTM bridges use FY2025 plus H1 2026 less H1 2025; the controller-generated scenario outputs use the disclosed formulas and remain subject to independent reproduction. The model sets terminal net interest and other income to zero rather than capitalizing current cash interest, uses author-selected terminal tax rates because the valuation allowance can reverse, and does not model acquisition cash outflows. It gives no continuing buyback offset: 2026 repurchases consumed $742.880m in H1, only $257.1m remained under the February authorization at filing, and the new $1.0bn August authorization is discretionary, working-capital funded, and limited to 24 months. The $65m-$75m October restructuring cash charge, execution disruption, AWS and inference dependency, privacy and AI regulation, FX because 49% of Q2 revenue was international, one-year-or-less contracts, solution-partner concentration, and acquisitions remain material.
forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: common stock, $0.001 par, trades NYSE:HUBS; 49,866,201 shares were issued and outstanding at 2026-07-31. Q2 weighted diluted shares were 50.615m; H1 were 51.564m; FY2026 guidance assumed 50.0m. H1 SBC was $244.227m, including $227.852m of RSUs; FY2025 SBC was $528.153m. Capitalized software was $74.292m in H1 2026 and $130.624m in FY2025 and is treated as economic capex in the owner-FCF cross-check. At 2026-06-30, cash was $958.314m; cash plus short- and long-term investments was about $1.4bn. The 2025 converts were fully settled in June 2025; current and noncurrent funded debt were zero at 2026-06-30, and the secured revolver had no borrowings. Remaining contractual claims included $283.8m operating leases and $415.9m vendor commitments. H1 buybacks were 3.467m shares for $742.880m at a $214.25 average; $257.1m remained under the February program, then an additional discretionary $1.0bn, 24-month program was authorized in August from working capital. Futurepedia cost $19.1m cash net plus $8.6m employment-contingent consideration and was immaterial. MODEL TREATMENT: no preferred stock, NCI, ADR, or FX translation is needed; terminal earnings are common-available GAAP earnings. Starting 50m diluted shares are grown at nonnegative author assumptions, so the model never assumes an unfinanced repurchase offset. Because valuation is direct common EPS, cash and debt are not separately added or subtracted from terminal value.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: The shared QQQ masses are preserved exactly: bear 0.12+0.08=0.20, base 0.25+0.30=0.55, bull 0.15+0.10=0.25; total=1.00. Conditional execution weights are subjective, uncalibrated human judgments based on Q2 constant-currency growth of about 17.5%, 102% NRR, 14% reported billings growth, measurable AI adoption, improving GAAP margin, slowing customer additions, and material SBC. The largest single weight is a central recovery, not an upside case; 37% total probability is assigned to explicit operational-lag or bear paths where QQQ wins. No historical rank or hurdle set the weights. Every scenario uses TTM revenue of FY2025 less H1 2025 plus H1 2026, compounds author-selected revenue for five years, applies an SBC-inclusive GAAP operating margin, assumes zero terminal net interest and other income, subtracts author-selected tax, has no preferred or NCI claim, divides by 50m diluted shares grown at a nonnegative rate, and applies a terminal GAAP P/E. Controller-calculated outcomes show HUBS strictly beating its paired QQQ CAGR in four cases totaling 0.63 and not beating in two cases totaling 0.37; all outputs remain subject to independent reproduction.

scenarios.name: Demand break / restructuring drag

SOURCE ANCHORS: Q2 constant-currency growth about 17.5%, NRR 102%, customer adds below expectations, GAAP operating margin 4.8%, and October cash restructuring charge of $65m-$75m. Causal formula in USD millions and million shares: ((3131.266-1475.003+1792.735)*1.06^5*8%+zero nonoperating income)*(1-25% tax)/(50*1.02^5)*20x; direct common EPS means no separate cash/debt bridge.

Causal formula in USD millions and million shares: ((3131.266-1475.003+1792.735)*1.12^5*14%+zero nonoperating income)*(1-22% tax)/(50*1.01^5)*28x. No repurchase offset, cash/debt adjustment, or non-GAAP EPS is embedded.

Model inference: use a direct diluted-EPS framework, because interest, loan-loss provisions, taxes, funding costs and FX already pass through consolidated net income; operating cash flow is distorted by customer funds and financial receivables. Every scenario compounds total net income, divides by scenario share growth, and applies a terminal P/E. Human judgment: the ecosystem can sustain unusually high earnings growth if commerce, payments, advertising and credit cross-sell deepen, but the roughly 51x TTM starting valuation, deliberate margin reinvestment, credit losses and Latin American FX/regulation make multiple compression and earnings misses material.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MELI can beat QQQ if its underpenetrated regional commerce and financial-services flywheel compounds net income per diluted share in the low-to-mid 20s or better while the terminal P/E remains at least in the low 30s. Q2 2026 evidence supports the runway—commerce buyers +26%, Mercado Pago MAUs +30%, GMV +36% FX-neutral, and advertising +73% in USD—but does not prove owner-earnings conversion because operating margin fell to 6.7%. QQQ is the superior alternative if MELI's credit-card and consumer-loan growth causes provisions/funding to consume operating leverage, if free-shipping/1P investments fail to improve retention and monetization, if local-currency depreciation overwhelms unit growth, or if a still-premium terminal multiple is not earned. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: monday.com is a USD-reporting Israeli foreign private issuer whose FY2025 Form 20-F cover identifies ordinary shares, no par value, traded on Nasdaq as MNDY; it is not an ADR. GuruFocus supplied FY2019-FY2025 annual history rather than 15 years; reported revenue rose from $78.1m in 2019 to $1,232.0m in 2025, and its segment endpoint failed schema validation. The SEC/issuer TTM revenue bridge through 2026-06-30 is $316.900m+$333.878m+$351.265m+$364.621m=$1,366.664m. Q2 revenue was $364.6m, up 22%; cRPO was $750m, up 27%; total NDR was 109%; AI-product ARR doubled sequentially and represented 17% of net-new ARR; Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 17%; Q3 revenue guidance was 16%-17% growth. At June 30 the issuer reported 42.274119m ordinary shares, 2.604847m unvested RSUs, and 1.150320m options with a $68.12 weighted-average exercise price. On August 5 it issued 0.196829m Foundation shares. Its Foundation policy permits up to 1% of outstanding ordinary shares annually, with only up to 1% aggregate carryover, as part of an up-to-10%-over-about-ten-years intention. The August-approved executive compensation policy permits a Co-CEO award up to 0.50% of issued shares for no-exercise-price awards or 1.0% for awards with an exercise price, subject to a $13.65m on-target value cap. The 2021 plan permits an annual reserve increase of up to 5% of prior year-end shares, though reserve capacity is not actual issuance. MODEL INFERENCE: seats-plus-credits AI pricing, enterprise expansion, and post-restructuring leverage may sustain double-digit revenue growth and expand normalized margins, while 109% NDR and the Q3 deceleration make that contested. SBC is economically recurring: the terminal denominator uses full-count outstanding awards and positive future issuance rather than treating non-GAAP add-backs as free. HUMAN JUDGMENT: scenario growth, margins, multiples, FCF margins, cash yields, acquisition uses, issuance rates, and joint probabilities are explicit author assumptions, not issuer guidance.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MNDY can beat QQQ from $83.51 if cRPO and enterprise cohorts support durable double-digit growth, paid AI credits become meaningful usage, restructuring converts roughly 89% gross margins into operating leverage, and dilution stays within the modeled 3%-6% combined annual future issuance envelope. QQQ is the better default if Q3's 16%-17% guide marks structural deceleration, NDR stays near 109% or lower, AI economics constrain margins, recurring equity issuance exceeds the explicit envelope, or management consumes the $1.073bn opening liquidity without proportional operating value. Exact controller evaluation shows four of six joint paths strictly beat paired QQQ returns, for a subjective aggregate beat probability of 0.60; the 0.10 bear/weak and 0.30 base/lag paths do not beat QQQ.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001443646 and NYSE-traded Class A common stock BAH. GuruFocus recorded the 2026-10-07 16:00:02 EDT close at $68.69 and TTM reported EPS of $6.368. The SEC-filed Q1 FY2027 release reported $2,800m revenue, $279m operating income and $198m net income versus $2,924m, $257m and $271m a year earlier; Q1 revenue fell 4.2%, but adjusted EBITDA rose 7.4%, adjusted margin reached 11.9%, backlog was $39bn, and book-to-bill was 1.5x. MODEL INFERENCE: national-security demand, cyber/AI products and a low starting earnings multiple can outweigh Civil weakness if consolidated revenue resumes growth and margins hold near or above the TTM level. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the valuation is attractive enough to underwrite nine joint outcomes, but post-quarter acquisition debt and the absence of disclosed AI-product economics keep QQQ as the default in weak and merely adequate execution paths.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: BAH can beat QQQ if national-security awards, AI-native cyber products and Ultra Mission Solutions restore mid-single-digit growth while operating margin reaches roughly 10.5%-12.5%. The starting price is only about eleven times GuruFocus TTM reported EPS, so even moderate terminal multiples can create strong price returns. The counter-thesis is that federal procurement/shutdown pressure, Civil contraction, labor constraints, acquisition integration and higher interest expense suppress EPS while QQQ compounds at 10%-18%. Vellox is a concrete product suite, but no AI revenue, ARR, bookings or customer KPI was disclosed; it is optionality, not a modeled standalone revenue stream.
forecasts.falsifier: At each quarterly filing, calculate rolling-four-quarter revenue growth and operating margin from SEC GAAP statements, and read company backlog/book-to-bill disclosures. Re-underwrite immediately and assign zero weight to paths above 4% revenue growth or 11% terminal margin if either (a) rolling-four-quarter revenue growth is <=-3% at two consecutive quarter-ends, (b) rolling-four-quarter GAAP operating margin is <9% at two consecutive quarter-ends, or (c) quarterly book-to-bill is <0.9x twice within four quarters. From debt filings, also calculate post-Ultra net debt/LTM adjusted EBITDA; if it exceeds 4.0x at two consecutive quarter-ends, remove all terminal multiples above 15x until leverage returns below 3.5x. These are pre-breach relative to Q1's 1.5x book-to-bill, 11.9% adjusted margin and disclosed 2.7x June leverage; the latter predates the August financing/acquisition and therefore is not used as the post-close baseline.
forecasts.nextAction: Independent Evidence & Risk review must reperform the scenario arithmetic, verify the TTM tax normalization, post-August debt/cash bridge, Ultra purchase accounting and contribution, backlog/book-to-bill definitions, and whether any later filing disclosed Vellox economics. The North Star PM then decides ranking for both Core and AI sleeves; no roster, sizing or trade action is authorized here.

Q1 SBC expense was $21m and repurchases were $72m. The remaining authorization was $634m but may be suspended or ended, so every scenario uses 0% share-count growth and gives no buyback credit. On 2026-08-04 the company issued $700m 5.375% notes and $500m 5.900% notes; disclosed net proceeds were about $1,189m, used partly to repay the $714m A-1 term loan and partly for the $720m Ultra acquisition. The prospectus showed as-adjusted debt of $4,422m and cash of $1,015m before the acquisition; the source-based post-close bridge is cash=(1015-720) and net debt=4422-(1015-720), both USDm, but no post-close balance sheet had yet been filed. No preferred stock or noncontrolling-interest claim was identified. REPORTED-TO-NORMALIZED TTM BRIDGE, USDm except per share: revenue=(11217+2800-2924); operating income=(1033+279-257); reported net income=(205+200+175+198); pretax income=((205+21)+(200-13)+(175+58)+(198+53)); normalized net income=pretax*(1-0.215), using the midpoint of management's 20%-23% FY2027 tax guide. forecasts.probabilityRationale: The nine probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated; none comes from a legacy score, hurdle, rank or target return. Exact QQQ masses are 0.20 bear (0.08+0.08+0.04), 0.55 base (0.15+0.25+0.15), and 0.25 bull (0.08+0.10+0.07). Within each benchmark state, weights reflect separate judgments about federal demand, Civil stabilization, margin execution, Ultra integration and valuation. QQQ wins in the BAH fiscal-shock, execution-miss, index-outruns and solid-but-lag paths. All formulas use USD millions for revenue, operating income and interest, 120.185147 million diluted shares, no preferred/NCI deduction, zero assumed net share shrinkage, and terminal GAAP EPS times a P/E multiple. Interest scalars are author estimates that explicitly reflect the August debt refinancing and varying deleveraging; tax, margin, growth and multiple scalars are author assumptions, not source forecasts.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: AppFolio's 2026 Q2 10-Q identifies the Nasdaq-traded security as Class A common stock, reports Q2 revenue of $281.124 million (up 19% year over year), 9.6 million property-management units (up 8%), 22,751 property-management customers, and GAAP operating income of $52.977 million (18.8% margin). Value Added Services were $219.467 million of Q2 revenue versus $59.800 million of subscription revenue, so payments, screening, and risk-mitigation usage—not subscriptions alone—drives the model. The filing reports $217.401 million cash, no revolver borrowings, H1 operating cash flow of $121.902 million, and only $0.228 million H1 PP&E purchases; GuruFocus's source-provided TTM diluted EPS is $4.387. Model inference: start with $4.387 of TTM diluted EPS and model five-year net-income growth divided by explicit diluted-share growth, then apply a terminal P/E; this direct per-share framework avoids an irrelevant EV bridge but does not treat current net cash as incremental terminal value. Human judgment: durable system-of-record workflows, higher-value transaction adoption, and operating leverage can support mid-teens-or-better net-income growth, while payments concentration, regulation, AI competition, and multiple compression warrant severe lag cases.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: APPF can beat QQQ if unit growth plus deeper Value Added Services adoption sustains roughly 20% net-income growth in the central execution-win case while diluted-share growth stays near 0.5% and the terminal market still awards 35x earnings. Q2 2026 revenue grew 19%, units 8%, and GAAP operating income 31%, providing operating evidence for that path; however, the stock starts from a premium earnings multiple and QQQ is the better alternative whenever growth fades toward high single digits, dilution rises, or the terminal multiple falls into the mid-20s. The scenario weights are fresh subjective judgments, not calibrated frequencies or translations of any legacy score.
forecasts.falsifier: At each quarterly filing, test: (1) property-management units grow below 6% year over year for two consecutive quarters, or Value Added Services revenue grows below 12% year over year for two consecutive quarters—then remove the 20% central net-income-growth assumption and shift the base execution-win weight to the lag case; (2) GAAP operating margin is below 15% while revenue growth is below 15% for two consecutive quarters—then cap the central terminal multiple at 27x and re-underwrite; (3) diluted weighted-average shares grow above 2% year over year for two consecutive quarters absent a disclosed acquisition—then use at least 2% annual share growth in every case and recalculate; (4) a material payment-processor loss, adverse payments/tenant-screening regulation, or disclosed material cyber/chargeback loss occurs—then suspend the win cases pending quantified economics. Sources are the next two APPF 10-Q/10-K filings, especially revenue disaggregation, units, operating margin, EPS/share data, SBC, and repurchase notes. Consequence in every trigger is a full probability and valuation refresh, not an automatic trade.

In QQQ bull, weights are 0.13 win and 0.12 lag: APPF may monetize vertical AI and workflow depth, but beating an 18% QQQ CAGR requires both exceptional earnings compounding and sustained premium valuation, so the conditional win weight falls to 52%. The mechanically evaluated outcomes show that the three execution-win cases strictly beat their matched QQQ returns and the three lag cases do not, producing an authored strict-outperformance probability of 0.58. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Wix has one registered class of NIS 0.01 ordinary shares trading directly on Nasdaq as WIX; no ADR ratio applies. GuruFocus returned the split-adjusted 2026-10-07 close of $72.97. FY2025 raw FCF was $572.957m; H1 2025 and H1 2026 raw FCF were $290.106m and $127.615m, making the observed TTM bridge $572.957m-$290.106m+$127.615m=$410.466m. The 20-F reports $48.9m of 2025 deposit and investment income. The Q1 release says 2026 guidance reflects foregone interest on tender cash and interest on the $500m facility. Q2 reported $52.642m raw FCF and the fully drawn facility as current debt. MODEL INFERENCE: every scenario starts from $410.466m-$48.9m-(6%*$500m). Removing the entire FY2025 investment-income amount from a TTM containing only H2 2025 and imposing a full-year 6% facility charge are deliberately conservative; the latter may over-deduct because raw TTM FCF already includes some Q2 facility interest. Acquisition and restructuring cash costs remain in raw FCF. Cash-refinance paths grow this after-current-facility-interest base, subtract note refinancing interest once, and subtract only facility interest above 6%. The 41,849,511 May share base grows only for future grants; all 5,977,396 disclosed option/PSU/RSU shares are added separately at gross shares with no proceeds, forfeitures or net-settlement credit. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Wix beats QQQ only if core Wix and Base44 grow cash generation enough to absorb a harsh gross-award envelope and 2030 refinancing or conversion.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Wix can outperform QQQ if bookings and ARR convert into durable raw FCF growth, Base44 reaches sustainable unit economics, and Wix resolves the near-term facility and 2030 notes without sacrificing operating flexibility. The revised bridge removes old-liquidity income, imposes a full-year current-facility interest charge, gives no repurchase credit, separates disclosed award overhang from future grants, and gives no capped-call benefit. The counter-thesis is AI-native commoditization, persistent Partners weakness, structurally high Base44 inference/marketing cost, failed restructuring, punitive refinancing or dilution. QQQ remains the better default in disruption and core-plateau cases. This price-only comparison excludes QQQ distributions and therefore favors WIX.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply pre-breach consequences: (1) bookings growth below 6% year over year for two consecutive quarters caps modeled FCF growth at 3% until two quarters exceed 8%; (2) Base44 non-GAAP gross margin below 40% in Q4 2026 triggers the disruption path; (3) raw TTM FCF below $350m at two consecutive quarter-ends triggers no more than 8x, at least 2.5% future-grant growth and the gross award envelope; (4) beginning 2026-10-31 and monthly until facility refinancing, require unrestricted unencumbered liquidity plus unconditional committed refinancing to cover 1.25x all principal due within 24 months plus twelve months of cash needs, expressly including the $500m facility and excluding the pledged NIS 1bn bills and $120m deposit; one failure triggers disruption financing; and (5) beginning 2028-09-30 extend the same test through 2030-09-15 so it includes both facility and $1.15bn notes. At note maturity use all 5,463,535 gross shares and zero capped-call offset unless then-current filings permit exact reproduction. Thresholds are author judgments.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies SPS Commerce, Inc., CIK 0001092699, one Nasdaq-listed common share under SPSC. The GuruFocus 2026-10-07 historical-price payload returned $81, although its MCP wrapper raised a list-versus-dictionary structured-content error; that failure remains part of provenance. FY2025 revenue was $751.505m; H1-2026/H1-2025 revenue was $389.936m/$368.949m, so reported TTM revenue is $772.492m. SPS sold its 3P Revenue Recovery business on 2026-06-30. The issuer says FY2026 guidance incorporates an approximately $10.5m reduction to H2 revenue and that the sale should be neutral to H2 adjusted EBITDA. The model therefore removes twice that explicitly quantified half-year amount from reported TTM revenue: $772.492m - 2 x $10.5m = a $751.492m continuing-revenue proxy. This is a transparent sensitivity, not a claim that $21m is the exact divested TTM revenue. Q2 revenue was $197.815m, GAAP operating income was $8.413m, and the separately disclosed 3P sale loss was $23.454m. The starting normalized operating bridge is therefore ($8.413m + $23.454m) / $197.815m = 16.109496246492935%. Its consistent quarterly after-tax per-share bridge is ($8.413m + $23.454m) x (1-24%) / 36.577m Q2 diluted shares = $0.6621352215873364. This definition excludes only the separately identified sale loss; it retains recurring SBC, acquired-intangible amortization, depreciation, and all ordinary operating costs. H1 SBC was $36.769m and unrecognized SBC was $115.2m over a 2.7-year weighted-average recognition period. Before repurchases, disclosed H1 share activity added 340,825 shares from awards/ESPP net of withholding, equal to 0.9084490465836252% of the 2025 year-end count in six months; H1 repurchases used $98.358m. MODEL INFERENCE: every scenario begins from the $751.492m proxy and 36.000174m July shares. Terminal price = [$751.492m x (1+revenue growth)^5 x terminal normalized operating margin x (1-24% tax)] / [36.000174m x (1+annual share growth)^5] x terminal P/E. Price CAGR = (terminal price / $81)^(1/5)-1. Because the margin retains SBC and all amortization and annual shares grow 1.8%-2.0%, no repurchase cash or SBC add-back is double-counted. Cash is deliberately omitted from terminal equity value, so no terminal-cash benefit funds repurchases. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the $751.492m proxy is the least-assertive bridge available from the issuer's quantified guidance; 1.8%-2.0% annual share growth is anchored to the disclosed six-month pre-repurchase issuance pace rather than net shares after cash-funded repurchases. Network effects, 96% recurring revenue, low concentration, and operating leverage could expand the sale-loss-normalized 16.1% Q2 operating margin, but the required 26%-29% execution margins in winning base/bull paths are demanding because they continue to charge SBC and amortization.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SPSC strictly beats QQQ in this authored distribution only in the QQQ-bear/resilient, QQQ-base/central, and QQQ-bull/upside paths, totaling 57%. The central case beats QQQ only narrowly: 10.308337205582441% versus 10%, so small deterioration in growth, dilution, margin, or multiple makes QQQ superior. The credible counter-thesis is that post-divestiture growth remains low single digit, short-cancel contracts or competition weaken retention, MAX/AI spending does not restore growth, acquisitions keep amortization and SBC elevated, gross equity issuance exceeds the modeled range, or valuation normalizes. Stress, base-lag, and bull-lag explicitly select QQQ as the better alternative. The 57% is subjective and uncalibrated, not investment approval.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if issuer-reported revenue growth, adjusted only for a separately quantified divestiture comparison, is <=2% y/y for two consecutive quarters, or if (GAAP operating income plus only separately quantified one-time disposal losses) / revenue is <=15% for two consecutive quarters, move all growth/margin assumptions to stress or base-lag until two subsequent quarters cure the breach. Pre-breach equity-economics trigger: if trailing-twelve-month pre-repurchase share issuance from awards and ESPP net of withholding exceeds 2.25% of the beginning share count, or SBC is >=10% of revenue for two consecutive quarters, use at least 2.5% annual share growth and cap terminal P/E at 20x until two subsequent quarters cure the breach; repurchases cannot cure this metric. Pre-breach capital trigger: if quarter-end cash less disclosed interest-bearing current/noncurrent borrowings becomes negative, or gross interest-bearing borrowing exceeds $250m, without a separately disclosed acquisition bridge covering first-year revenue, interest, tax, shares, and financing, remove all upside paths and default to QQQ. June 2026 cash was $173.167m and the filing presented no interest-bearing borrowing line; leases remain tracked separately. These are monitoring triggers, not evidence that a breach has occurred.
forecasts.nextAction: At the next filing, replace the $751.492m proxy with an issuer-disclosed exact continuing-operations revenue bridge if one becomes available; update reported revenue growth, the sale-loss-normalized operating margin under the unchanged SBC-and-amortization-inclusive definition, cash, interest-bearing borrowings, leases, diluted shares, pre-repurchase award/ESPP issuance, SBC/revenue, and repurchase cash. Evidence & Risk must reproduce the six formulas, confirm strict inequalities and the 57% aggregate, and challenge the 26%-29% terminal margins. North Star PM must decide whether a narrowly positive base-case spread and subjective 57% strict-beat weight justify inclusion versus simply owning QQQ.
forecasts.theme: Recurring supply-chain network software; direct SBC-and-amortization-inclusive operating earnings per share versus QQQ
forecasts.limitations: GuruFocus summary, annual/quarterly financials, and key-ratio endpoints were queried. The visible annual payload exposed 2017-2025 plus TTM, not 15 full years, so no 15-year claim is made. The GuruFocus segment endpoint returned data but failed MCP structured-content validation because the provider payload was a list rather than a dictionary; no separately valued segment model is used. The $751.492m continuing-revenue figure is a sensitivity that annualizes the issuer's quantified H2 reduction, not an exact carve-out statement. The Q2 starting normalization does not claim an exact pro-forma continuing margin because the issuer disclosed H2 adjusted-EBITDA neutrality, not a complete GAAP operating-expense carve-out. The model retains SBC and all D&A/amortization, assumes a 24% cash tax, and omits cash, interest income, debt, dividends, and repurchase benefit. Dilution assumptions are human judgments anchored to disclosed pre-repurchase issuance, while award timing can vary. Terminal margins, P/E values, and probabilities are subjective; price returns exclude dividends; Q3-2026 had not been filed by the model snapshot. MathJS reproduced displayed arithmetic, but all arithmetic requires independent verification against exact canonical bytes before publication.
forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: at 2026-06-30 SPS had $173.167m cash, 36.194528m period-end shares, no presented interest-bearing borrowing line, and operating-lease liabilities of $1.540m current plus $4.766m noncurrent. The 10-Q cover reported 36.000174m shares on 2026-07-23. Preferred stock had zero shares issued/outstanding. Options outstanding were 0.365095m at a $102.30 weighted-average exercise price, and 1.685220m PSUs/RSUs/RSAs/DSUs were outstanding. H1 operating cash flow less capex was $105.921m while repurchase cash was $98.358m, so repurchases consumed most of that simple subtotal. MODEL POLICY: use 36.000174m starting shares and positive 1.8%-2.0% annual share growth; retain SBC in operating expense; credit no repurchase, authorization, net cash, interest income, or debt-funded acquisition. This avoids treating SBC as costless and avoids assuming buybacks without charging their cash cost.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: HUMAN JUDGMENT: common QQQ marginals remain 0.20/0.55/0.25. Within QQQ bear, 0.08 is SPSC stress and 0.12 resilient; within QQQ base, 0.20 is base-lag and 0.35 central execution; within QQQ bull, 0.15 is bull-lag and 0.10 upside. Mechanically, resilient 2.0470043907859115% exceeds -4%, central 10.308337205582441% strictly exceeds 10%, and upside 18.56207188643748% strictly exceeds 18%; their joint weights sum to 0.57. Stress, base-lag, and bull-lag lose. The former stress-path beat is removed after correcting the divested-revenue base and SBC/dilution policy. These probabilities are subjective, uncalibrated, and do not preserve the rejected rank.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: GuruFocus reports a USD53.49 consolidated regular-session close at 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT and TTM EPS of USD3.638 for the ADR. Tencent's 2026 interim report reports first-half revenue of RMB401.243 billion (+10% year over year), IFRS profit attributable to equity holders of RMB114.115 billion (+10%), diluted IFRS EPS of RMB12.417 (+12%), and Q2 gross margin of 58%. Q2 segment revenue growth was 8% for VAS, 22% for Marketing Services, and 9% for FinTech and Business Services. Model inference: Tencent can compound USD-translated attributable earnings through games, AI-improved ads, cloud and payments while repurchases partly offset awards/options, but elevated AI investment, China policy and currency/ADR risk warrant wide growth and terminal-P/E ranges. The model is direct source-provided TTM-EPS/P-E, not EV-derived; it therefore does not add investee value or net cash separately.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Tencent begins at about 14.7 times the source-provided USD3.638 TTM EPS versus the USD53.49 ADR price, while issuer evidence shows double-digit first-half revenue/profit growth, 22% Q2 Marketing Services growth, gross-margin expansion and ongoing repurchases. If AI-enhanced advertising, internally developed games and cloud sustain low-double-digit USD-translated attributable-profit growth and the diluted share base contracts, a mid-teens terminal P/E can produce price growth above the shared QQQ base case. QQQ remains the better default if AI capex suppresses cash conversion, China regulation/geopolitics or RMB depreciation imposes a lasting discount, or Tencent's earnings growth falls to mid-single digits while QQQ compounds at 10%-18%.
forecasts.falsifier: At each Tencent quarterly/interim/annual release, test: (1) if consolidated revenue growth is below 5% and non-IFRS operating margin is below 32% for two consecutive quarters, move base-case mass toward execution-lag and reduce operating-growth assumptions; (2) if both Marketing Services growth is below 10% and Domestic Games growth is below 5% for two consecutive quarters, remove the low-double-digit base growth premise; (3) if reported diluted weighted-average shares grow more than 2% year over year for two consecutive quarters despite repurchases, replace nonpositive share-count-growth assumptions with at least +2% and recalculate; (4) if period-end net cash is below zero or reported free cash flow remains negative for two consecutive half-years while capex exceeds 25% of revenue, reduce terminal multiples and reassess financing risk; and (5) any ADR ratio change, inability to convert/cancel the DR, trading restriction, sanctions exposure that impairs holders, or loss of reliable USD price evidence makes the row unrankable pending security reconciliation. Consequence: any one security/tradability event is an immediate hard gap; either operating pair triggers a re-underwrite rather than automatic removal.
forecasts.nextAction: The six outcomes already use the controller's full-precision deterministic results. Evidence & Risk must independently verify the USD53.49 close, GuruFocus USD3.638 TTM EPS translation against issuer RMB diluted EPS and applicable FX, the ADR ISIN and 1:1 terms across holder-relevant depositaries, current issued shares and the diluted option/award basis, debt/net cash, formula arithmetic and strict QQQ comparisons. North Star PM must judge China/VIE/geopolitical, RMB, AI-capex and unsponsored-ADR risks before any exact-hash publication; no portfolio action is authorized.
forecasts.theme: China internet platform and AI monetization
forecasts.limitations: Source facts: the GuruFocus annual/quarterly financial-data endpoint returned empty arrays for TCEHY and HKSE:00700 in this run, so it did not supply the requested 15-year table; the indicator endpoint exposed a 2003-2025 revenue series but failed schema validation before returning the complete series. GuruFocus segment retrieval also failed its response-schema adapter, while operating data supplied only a five-year advertising series. The primary 2025 annual and 2026 interim reports therefore anchor financial history and latest fundamentals. Model limitations: USD3.638 TTM EPS is a GuruFocus source-provided USD per-ADR calculation and must be independently reconciled to Tencent's RMB diluted EPS and the applicable period FX; all scenario operating growth rates mean USD-translated IFRS attributable-profit growth, thereby including RMB/USD movement. The unsponsored ADR can be issued by multiple depositaries; the latest September 2026 SEC F-6EF establishes one ADS equals one ordinary share for Deutsche Bank's program, and JPM's current program page maps TCEHY/CUSIP 88032Q109 to ISIN US88032Q1094 and 1:1, but the reviewer must confirm the holder's precise depositary terms and fees. No value is separately added for listed/unlisted investments or net cash; this forecloses an explicit SOTP/net-asset uplift but does not necessarily make terminal values conservative because the terminal P/E may implicitly reflect balance-sheet assets. Dividends and ADR fees are omitted, so the reported outcomes are price-only rather than total-shareholder-return estimates. China/VIE, capital-control, audit, sanctions, policy and OTC-liquidity risks are reflected through low multiples and outcome weights, not independently priced claims.
forecasts.capitalStructure: Source facts as of 2026-06-30: Tencent's interim report shows Q2 weighted-average basic shares of 9,025 million, 128 million potential dilutive options/awards and 9,153 million diluted shares; first-half equivalents were 9,029 million basic, 134 million potential dilution and 9,163 million diluted. Tencent repurchased about 37.4 million shares in Q2 for HKD16.9 billion. Q2 share-based compensation was RMB6.579 billion at operating-profit level and RMB7.756 billion in the attributable-profit non-IFRS reconciliation, so buybacks cannot be treated as pure per-share accretion without an award/option bound. Current issuer evidence: the 2026-10-07 next-day disclosure reports 9,092,605,595 issued ordinary shares excluding treasury shares, zero treasury shares and 238,000 shares repurchased that day for cancellation; the September monthly return reports 75,059,835 options outstanding and 49,004,981 ordinary shares issuable from exercisable outstanding options under the 2023 Share Option Scheme. Period-end total cash at 2026-06-30 was RMB511.2 billion, total debt RMB453.0 billion and net cash RMB58.2 billion; listed investee stakes had RMB487.2 billion fair value and unlisted stakes RMB387.9 billion carrying value, but none is added to this direct EPS model. Tencent completed US$2.45 billion and CNY15 billion note issuance in June 2026; debt and AI funding needs are captured in earnings growth, multiple and probability rather than an EV bridge. Security facts: the latest SEC F-6EF filed 2026-09-03 by Deutsche Bank registers ADSs, each representing one Tencent ordinary share; JPM identifies TCEHY as an active unsponsored OTC DR, CUSIP 88032Q109, DR ISIN US88032Q1094, underlying ticker 700, underlying ISIN KYG875721634 and ratio 1:1. Model assumptions bound annual share-count change from -2% in the strongest case to +1.5% in the impairment case; any sustained >2% growth triggers the stated re-underwrite.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: These are subjective conditional weights, not empirical or publisher-supplied probabilities and are not derived from a legacy rank. Within QQQ bear, 0.12 is assigned to Tencent execution-win and 0.08 to lag because Tencent's diversified franchises, net cash and repurchases can defend per-share earnings, while China/geopolitical impairment remains a fat tail. Within QQQ base, 0.32 goes to win and 0.23 to lag because first-half revenue/profit and Q2 ads/games/cloud evidence supports low-double-digit operating growth, but AI capex, SBC and policy risk can leave Tencent below a 10% QQQ hurdle. Within QQQ bull, 0.12 goes to win and 0.13 to lag because beating an 18% annual QQQ outcome requires both high-teens Tencent operating growth and a 20x terminal P/E despite China/ADR discount; strong company execution can still lose to a U.S. AI-led index boom. State totals are exactly 0.20, 0.55 and 0.25; total mass is 1.00. Human judgment remains required on whether these conditional weights adequately compensate for non-quantifiable China and unsponsored-ADR impairment risk.

Formula: terminal price = 3.638*((1+0.16)/(1-0.02))^5*20; CAGR = (terminal price/53.49)^(1/5)-1. Both operating execution and China-risk re-rating are required to beat the demanding QQQ bull hurdle.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Accenture's October 1, 2026 SEC-furnished FY2026 release reports $74.18 billion revenue (+6% USD, +5% local currency), $84.54 billion bookings (1.1 book-to-bill), 15.4% GAAP operating margin, $8.52 billion net income, $13.56 GAAP diluted EPS, and $11.62 billion free cash flow. Q4 growth was broad-based: both consulting and managed services grew 7% in local currency. FY2027 issuer guidance is 3%-6% local-currency revenue growth, 15.9%-16.1% operating margin, and $14.39-$14.81 GAAP diluted EPS. Model inference: Accenture can compound total net income at mid-single to low-double digits if enterprise reinvention, cloud/data modernization and AI implementation demand offsets AI-driven labor deflation and if delivery automation supports margins. Human judgment: the direct diluted-GAAP-EPS/P-E framework uses FY2026 $13.56 EPS as the starting per-share metric; scenario net-income growth, diluted-share change and terminal multiples are subjective five-year assumptions, not issuer guidance or calibrated forecasts.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: At $196.64, ACN begins at about 14.5 times FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS before dividends, while the issuer guides FY2027 GAAP EPS growth of 6%-9% and plans at least $9.5 billion of cash returns. That starting valuation plus resilient managed-services demand and buyback-supported per-share growth can beat QQQ in the bear and successful base cases without requiring QQQ-like growth. The QQQ alternative is superior if AI shifts economics to software/platform vendors, compresses billable labor faster than Accenture monetizes reinvention, or if QQQ compounds at the 18% bull hurdle while ACN remains a mid-single-digit grower. Dividends are deliberately excluded because the shared comparison is price-only.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Meta's 2026 Q2 filing identifies Nasdaq-traded Class A common stock as META and reports $60.801bn quarterly revenue (+28% year over year), 3.60bn Family daily active people (+3%), ad impressions +14%, average price per ad +12%, and Family of Apps operating income of $23.394bn, offset by a $4.619bn Reality Labs operating loss. The filing reports $6.18 diluted Q2 EPS; GuruFocus reports $26.548 TTM diluted GAAP EPS at the 2026-10-07 close. Primary-source normalization facts: Meta's Q3 2025 results say a one-time $15.93bn non-cash tax charge reduced diluted EPS by $6.20; Q1 2026 results say an $8.03bn tax benefit, which partially offset that charge, increased diluted EPS by $3.13; Q2 2026 results include $2.40bn of legal charges and $1.18bn of severance expense. Model inference: recommendation and advertising AI can sustain low-double-digit operating-earnings growth, but the $130bn-$145bn 2026 capex program, Reality Labs losses, no H1 2026 share repurchases, and very large disclosed infrastructure commitments make conversion to per-share value uncertain. Human judgment: the direct framework starts from reported TTM diluted GAAP EPS of 26.548. The normalization pressure test is starting EPS = 26.548 + 6.20 - 3.13 + 0.00 legal adjustment + 0.00 severance adjustment. The two issuer-quantified per-share tax effects are reversed in opposite directions. Legal and severance charges remain fully in the normalized denominator because the issuer did not publish item-specific after-tax per-share effects, legal exposure remains active, restructuring may recur, and assuming deductibility or nonrecurrence would be unsupported. No tax shield is imputed to either retained item.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Source facts: Q2 advertising volume and pricing both grew double digits while Family of Apps remained highly profitable, giving Meta a company-specific AI monetization path rather than only broad AI beta. Model inference: META beats QQQ only if net income compounds materially faster than the index while net share count becomes flat-to-down and the terminal P/E remains at least in the low-to-mid 20s despite the infrastructure obligation load. Counter-thesis and QQQ alternative: QQQ is preferable if Meta's infrastructure and Reality Labs spending absorb owner cash, regulation weakens targeting, SBC drives dilution, or the stock's reported-EPS valuation compresses; QQQ then diversifies AI upside across semiconductors, software, cloud and other platforms instead of relying on one ad-funded capital program. The normalized sensitivity removes only the issuer-quantified one-time Q3 tax charge and offsetting Q1 tax benefit; it is not used to erase legal or severance costs. Scenario weights are subjective conditional judgments, not calibrated frequencies or publisher targets.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: HKEX/issuer materials identify Cayman-incorporated ENN Energy Holdings Limited ordinary shares, stock code 2688; Hang Seng Indexes maps 2688 to ISIN KYG3066L1014. GuruFocus maps HKSE:02688 to the same issuer; its key-ratio response identifies Ordinary Shares, HKD market currency and CNY reporting currency, while its historical-price response exposed a 2026-10-07 split-adjusted close of HKD49.44 despite response-validation failure. OFX showed 1 HKD=USD0.127118 on 2026-10-07, giving the working USD close of 49.44*0.127118=6.284714 rounded. FY2025 revenue was RMB111,905m, attributable profit RMB5,904m, core profit RMB6,741m and basic EPS RMB5.31. H1 2026 revenue was RMB57,021m, attributable profit RMB2,667m, core profit RMB3,175m and basic EPS RMB2.40; H1 2025 comparatives were RMB55,673m, RMB2,429m and RMB3,223m. Thus the disclosed TTM bridge is revenue 111905-55673+57021=RMB113,253m; reported common profit 5904-2429+2667=RMB6,142m; company-defined core profit 6741-3223+3175=RMB6,693m. Core profit excludes other gains/losses except realised commodity-derivative settlements and compensation, plus related tax on unrealised derivatives; retained realised hedging is recurring resource-matching economics but volatile. MODEL INFERENCE: low-single-digit revenue, pass-through, integrated-energy mix and smart-home monetisation can sustain common earnings, but a price-only framework needs both execution and a non-distressed terminal multiple. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the low starting valuation creates credible QQQ-beating paths, offset by China utility regulation, gas-demand weakness, FX and controlling-shareholder/governance risk.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: H1 2026 retail gas volume rose 0.8%, retail-gas gross profit rose 10.4%, electricity sales rose 40.5%, gross margin reached 11.7%, operating cash flow was RMB3,078m and net gearing improved to 19.1%; management guided 2026 retail gas volume to flat/slight growth, capex about RMB6.0bn, FCF broadly flat and dividend at least HKD3.00. MODEL INFERENCE: pass-through and mix can grow common earnings faster than revenue while a single-digit-to-low-teens P/E offers rerating. HUMAN JUDGMENT: ENN beats QQQ only if durable common earnings and valuation recovery overcome RMB/HKD-to-USD drag; QQQ is superior when volume/margin execution remains weak or its AI-led bull case persists.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach tests from the 2026-10-07 baseline: (1) company-defined rolling-12-month core profit below RMB5.5bn in two consecutive interim/annual reports (baseline RMB6.693bn) moves all paths to the weak/drawdown economics; (2) net gearing above 30% or interest-bearing debt above RMB26bn at two consecutive reporting dates (baseline 19.1% and RMB18.944bn at 2026-06-30) applies at least +0.5% annual share growth and a maximum 8x terminal multiple; (3) retail gas volume declines more than 3% YoY while residential pass-through falls below 70% in either annual report (baseline H1 volume +0.8%, disclosed cumulative pass-through 74.8%) removes the margin-expansion paths; (4) diluted or issued share count rises more than 1% annualised over two reporting dates, excluding trustee-held awards already reflected, replaces the relevant share path with observed dilution. Sources are the next issuer interim/annual report and monthly return; consequence is explicit scenario demotion, not a narrative warning.

forecasts.thesis: Fiserv is a leveraged payments and financial-technology reset trading at a distressed price after organic contraction and margin compression. The underwriting uses the low end of 2026 adjusted EPS guidance as a cash-like per-share anchor, assumes no buyback benefit, and requires recurring revenue stabilization plus margin repair for outperformance. Clover, issuer processing and core-account relationships create recovery optionality, but the thesis fails if Financial Solutions erosion and transformation spending are structural.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: At $45.31, the starting valuation is low relative to the issuer's $7.20 low-end adjusted-EPS outlook. A 3%-6% revenue recovery, margins returning only to 33%-37%, stable financing costs and no share-count decline can compound common-available earnings enough for multiple stabilization to outperform QQQ. The advantage is valuation-recovery asymmetry, not a claim that Fiserv has QQQ-like secular growth. QQQ wins when revenue stays flat/down, margins remain below 30%, debt absorbs cash, or strong index growth is not matched by Fiserv execution.
forecasts.falsifier: Forward, pre-breach tests start with Q3 2026. If both of any two consecutive reported quarters through Q2 2027 show organic revenue at or below -3% and adjusted operating margin below 30%, remove every recovery/upside path and cap common-earnings growth at 0% and exit multiple at 8x. If GAAP operating income/net interest expense is below 2.0x in any two quarters through Q2 2027, or current plus long-term debt exceeds $30bn without offsetting unrestricted cash/FCF, use the distress financing case. If diluted shares exceed 540m before 2027-12-31 absent disclosed EPS-accretive M&A, set share-count growth to at least 1.5%. Sources are future 10-Q/8-K earnings filings, measured against the Q2 2026 10-Q baseline.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: JPX identifies BeeX Inc., code 4270, ISIN JP3799690007; the issuer identifies one Tokyo Growth common share class. FY2026 revenue was JPY10,626.073m and operating income JPY592.601m. FY2027 Q1 revenue rose to JPY3,002.198m, but operating income fell to JPY122.294m as external development resources, hiring and sales investment increased. License-resale revenue grew 31.9%, while cloud integration and MSP fell 3.3% and 3.4%; the issuer reports one cloud-solutions segment. Model inference: the low starting price can produce QQQ-beating USD returns if recurring resale/MSP scale, integration recovers, and operating margin expands, but resale mix alone can raise revenue while depressing margins. Human judgment: retain only conditional, uncalibrated execution cases; no legacy score or rank informs probability.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: BeeX combines SAP/cloud-migration demand with growing monthly license resale and MSP revenue; recurring sales were 77.0% of FY2026 revenue and Q1 license resale grew 31.9%. The JPY1,890 price represents a modest multiple of prior-FY JPY202.78 basic and JPY182.60 diluted EPS, so execution plus margin recovery could outrun QQQ despite yen translation. Counter-thesis: Q1 already showed revenue growth with lower profit; integration and MSP contracted, options dilute owners, TerraSky controls the company, liquidity is thin, and a weaker yen can erase local gains. QQQ is the default in lag cases.
forecasts.falsifier: Use discrete quarters, not issuer-reported cumulative periods, for both two-quarter tests. Q2 discrete revenue, operating income, integration revenue and MSP revenue equal H1 cumulative amounts less Q1; Q3 discrete amounts equal 9M cumulative amounts less H1. Compare each discrete category total with the same discrete prior-year quarter, applying the same subtraction rule. Operating trigger: if discrete operating income/discrete revenue is below 0.035 in both Q2 and Q3, move all execution-case weight to corresponding lag cases and exclude from Top 50 pending reset; Q1 was 4.073482% and is not a breach. Quality trigger: if discrete integration-plus-MSP revenue is nonpositive year over year in both Q2 and Q3, apply the same consequence. If BeeX omits the category data needed for subtraction, treat the test as unmeasurable and require re-underwriting rather than assuming a pass. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: ASML identifies its Nasdaq security as registered ordinary shares, ticker ASML, ISIN USN070592100, traded in USD; the SEC cover identifies ordinary shares, nominal value EUR0.09, ticker ASML. GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT close at USD1,804.96. Issuer US-GAAP diluted EPS was EUR5.48 in Q3 2025, EUR7.34 in Q4 2025, EUR7.15 in Q1 2026 and EUR7.58 in Q2 2026, totaling EUR27.55 TTM. The ECB EXR observation for 2026-10-07 is 1.1177 USD per EUR, described as the 2:15 p.m. CET ECB reference rate. REPRODUCIBLE STARTING BRIDGE: selected USD TTM diluted EPS is (5.48+7.34+7.15+7.58)*1.1177. This deliberately applies one dated spot convention to all four issuer-reported EUR quarters; it does not claim to reproduce GuruFocus's undocumented USD32.121 conversion or transaction-period FX. No tax, SBC, seasonality or one-off normalization is made. ASML reported 2025 sales EUR32.7bn, gross margin 52.8% and net income EUR9.6bn; H1 2026 US-GAAP sales were EUR18.0934bn, net income EUR5.6743bn and diluted EPS EUR14.73. The July 2026 6-K raised 2026 net-sales guidance to EUR43bn-EUR45bn and gross margin to 54%-56%. MODEL INFERENCE: EUV/High-NA leadership and installed-base service can sustain high earnings growth, but the USD outcome also embeds EUR/USD translation and the current price requires durable AI capex plus a high terminal multiple. HUMAN JUDGMENT: use the explicit issuer-EPS/ECB-spot bridge, aggregate USD net-income growth and separately modeled share growth; price-only returns exclude dividends. The authorized controller evaluation of the selected-start expression produced the full-precision scenario outputs reported below, including a breakout CAGR of 0.18047244059739453 versus the independently derived USD30.7310662133 starting-EPS break-even for an 18% QQQ CAGR; independent review must reproduce that narrow strict-win result.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: ASML can beat QQQ if AI-led advanced Logic and Memory capacity, EUV/High-NA adoption, upgrades and installed-base service convert the 2026 acceleration into roughly 18%-20% USD net-income compounding while terminal P/E remains 44x-54x. QQQ is the better default if export controls, customer cyclicality, High-NA economics, supplier constraints, FX or valuation compression slow ASML. The joint paths deliberately include ASML losses to QQQ in the severe bear, base de-rating and QQQ-bull/company-lag states. The authorized controller arithmetic classifies the breakout outcome as a strict win by a narrow margin and the total probabilityBeatQqq as 0.50; those results remain subject to independent arithmetic and evidence review rather than portfolio approval.
forecasts.falsifier: Exact metric/threshold/window/source/consequence contract: (1) At each of the next two quarterly 6-K reports, calculate TTM issuer-reported EUR diluted EPS multiplied by that report date's ECB USD-per-EUR reference rate. If the result is below USD30 for two consecutive reports, transfer all higher-execution mass to the lag path within each QQQ state: bear/resilient 0.12 to bear/severe, base/strong 0.25 to base/reset, and bull/breakout 0.13 to bull/lag; benchmark marginals remain 0.20/0.55/0.25 and no ASML-over-QQQ base case remains pending re-underwrite. (2) Using the next two quarterly 6-Ks, if both quarterly gross margin is below 50% and installed-base-management sales growth is below 10% year over year for two consecutive reports, apply the same exact transfer. (3) In any quarterly 6-K or annual report through 2027-12-31, if ASML quantifies that a newly imposed export rule eliminates, blocks or delays at least EUR4.4bn of then-forecast annual net sales or booked demand, apply the same transfer immediately. EUR4.4bn is the author-set 10% threshold based on the midpoint of the cited EUR43bn-EUR45bn 2026 guidance, not an issuer materiality definition. (4) If ASML withdraws its announced 2027 NXE/NXT capacity expansion in a release or filing through 2027-12-31, apply the same transfer. Primary observations are ASML's furnished US-GAAP earnings releases/financial statements and the ECB EXR daily series.

forecasts.thesis: LULU is a direct common-equity earnings turnaround: a globally recognized premium athletic-apparel brand trades at a depressed valuation after material Americas traffic, conversion and product-relevance deterioration. FY2025 revenue was $11.103bn, with Americas 71% and declining 1%, while China grew 28.9% and Rest of World 15.6%. The upside requires restored full-price product resonance, low/mid-single-digit consolidated growth and recovery from refund-normalized margin pressure; it does not require continued buybacks. forecasts.whyBeatQqq: At $91.88, even partial recovery toward high-teens operating margin can produce attractive per-share earnings without relying on net share shrinkage, while international growth supplies a second engine. The counter-case is decisive: if Americas erosion is structural, QQQ wins through diversification and superior secular growth. The joint distribution therefore includes both turnaround wins and three explicit QQQ-win states; the controller-computed strict outperformance probability, not narrative conviction, determines rank.

FY2025 issuer results were revenue $6,791m, reported operating profit $797m, net income $888m and diluted EPS $1.59; management non-IFRS values were operating profit $1,066m, net income $965m and EPS $1.72. Q1/Q2 2025 reported revenue was $1,585m/$1,688m, operating profit $151m/$196m, net income $211m/$228m and EPS $0.38/$0.41; non-IFRS operating profit was $213m/$258m, net income $189m/$234m and EPS $0.34/$0.42. MODEL INFERENCE: the TTM bridge is FY2025-Q1'25-Q2'25+Q1'26+Q2'26: reported revenue 6791-1585-1688+1634+1786=6938; reported operating profit 797-151-196+180+174=804; reported net income 888-211-228+104+167=720; reported EPS 1.59-0.38-0.41+0.18+0.30=1.28, corroborating GuruFocus TTM EPS 1.281. I do not use the $1.82 as normalized economic EPS: SBC is recurring and dilutive, and acquisition amortization, integration and structural-optimization costs may recur as GF expands. The terminal model therefore starts from the $6,938m reported TTM revenue bridge and uses IFRS operating margins that retain SBC, then explicitly applies net finance/other, tax, NCI, diluted-share growth and a P/E. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the opportunity is specialty foundry mix and utilization improvement, with silicon photonics/SiGe for AI optical networking, power delivery and technology-services/IP raising growth and margin; it is not a leading-edge GPU thesis.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: GFS can beat QQQ only if specialty demand changes its low-growth earnings profile: Q2 2026 revenue rose 6% YoY, non-IFRS operating margin reached 16.7%, and management highlighted optical networking in AI data centers. Q2 cash generation and $3.3b cash/marketable securities support investment, while the June ARC acquisition and July Photeon IVR acquisition broaden Physical-AI and data-center power offerings. The high cases require sustained 10%-14% revenue growth, 20%-22% IFRS operating margin and 27x-30x terminal P/E; these are author assumptions, not guidance. QQQ remains superior if handset/cycle weakness, utilization, China capacity, tariffs, grants, customer concentration, integration, recurring SBC or financial-reporting control weaknesses constrain GFS to 5%-6% growth and 14%-17% margins. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Zoetis' 2026 Q2 10-Q identifies one NYSE-listed class, Common Stock, $0.01 par value, ticker ZTS, and CIK 0001555280; GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 close as $71.55 USD. The 2025 10-K reports revenue of $9,467m, operating profit before interest/other/tax of $3,546m (revenue less the disclosed operating costs), net income of $2,673m and diluted EPS of $6.02; SEC history shows revenue rising from about $4.2bn in 2011 to $9.467bn in 2025, although the provider financial response exposed a shorter visible window and no claim is made that every GuruFocus field spans 15 years. The Q2 2026 10-Q reports $4,730m H1 2026 revenue and recasts H1 2025 revenue to $4,672m, while expressly stating that the 2025 annual statements will be recast only when presented as future comparatives. MODEL INFERENCE: the scenario revenue base of $9,525m is the arithmetic $9,467m FY2025 - $4,672m recast H1 2025 + $4,730m H1 2026. It is a mixed-accounting-basis LTM proxy, not company-reported LTM revenue and not fully comparable because FY2025 remains unrecast at the snapshot. Reported LTM net income using the same mixed-basis bridge is $2,673m - $1,328m + $1,292m. Reported diluted EPS by quarter is $1.63 Q3 2025 + $1.37 Q4 2025 + $1.42 Q1 2026 + $1.65 Q2 2026, consistent with GuruFocus TTM EPS 6.079 subject to rounding. Management-adjusted EPS over the same quarters is $1.70+$1.48+$1.53+$1.87. The scenario model does not simply capitalize management-adjusted EPS. Purchase-accounting amortization is recurring for an acquisitive company, acquisition costs recur intermittently, and SBC is a recurring compensation cost; all stay economically represented through scenario operating margins and share counts. The raw-to-adjusted gap is disclosed only to show normalization sensitivity. Q2's $0.22 adjusted-EPS addback comprised $0.06 purchase accounting, approximately zero acquisition/divestiture cost and $0.16 significant items; H1 addbacks were $0.11, approximately zero and $0.21. Restructuring/productivity and impairment items are plausibly nonrecurring individually but recurring as a class, so no blanket addback is made. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the low price creates recovery optionality, but the sharp 2026 U.S. companion-animal slowdown, leverage-funded 2025-26 buyback and mixed-basis revenue proxy make this a balanced, not high-confidence, QQQ challenger.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Zoetis can beat QQQ if companion-animal demand stabilizes, its dermatology/parasiticide franchises and pipeline restore 5%-8% revenue growth, and operating leverage lifts the terminal operating margin to 33%-35%. The counter-thesis is concrete: Q2 U.S. revenue fell 7%, U.S. companion-animal sales fell 11%, full-year 2026 organic operational revenue guidance was cut to negative 3% to negative 1%, and adjusted EPS guidance to $6.15-$6.25. Competition, pet-owner price sensitivity, veterinary-visit softness and elevated debt can leave QQQ superior. The joint cases deliberately give QQQ wins in severe bear, slow base and normal bull paths.

At 2026-07-31, 413,223,602 shares were outstanding. H1 operating cash flow was $1,056m, capex $227m, dividends declared $436m, cash repurchases including excise taxes $1,190m and SBC $51m. The 2025 10-K records a major capital change: long-term debt rose from about $5.22bn to $9.04bn after $2.0bn of 0.25% convertible notes due 2029 plus senior notes; 2025 repurchases were $3.2bn, and 2026 H1 repurchases reduced year-end shares from 424.93m to 414.15m. The convertible's initial conversion price was about $148.20 and capped calls mitigate but do not eliminate settlement/refinancing risk. Each terminal bridge begins from 414.154m and uses 0% to +1% annual share growth, absorbing SBC/awards and possible convert dilution rather than assuming repurchases. There is no preferred dividend; disclosed NCI was zero, so post-tax income is common-available. Interest is scenario-bounded at $220m-$300m annually versus H1 2026 reported net interest of $123m.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: Subjective, uncalibrated joint weights are assigned independently of any legacy rank: QQQ bear 0.20 = severe 0.12 + recovery 0.08; QQQ base 0.55 = slow 0.30 + execution 0.25; QQQ bull 0.25 = normal 0.10 + innovation 0.15. Each terminal price uses USD millions: the explicitly disclosed mixed-basis revenue proxy (9467-4672+4730), five-year revenue growth, terminal operating margin, annual net interest, tax, terminal diluted shares from 414.154m and P/E. Stock CAGR is (terminal price / $71.55)^(1/5)-1. No aggregate EPS CAGR or buyback offset is hidden.

forecasts.thesis: Synopsys combines mission-critical EDA, silicon IP and Ansys simulation into a silicon-to-systems engineering platform positioned to monetize rising chip and physical-system complexity. The upside requires durable low-to-mid-teens organic revenue growth, cross-selling, after-SBC margin expansion and disciplined debt reduction; acquisition-driven reported growth and management non-GAAP EPS are not accepted at face value.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SNPS can beat QQQ if EDA remains a toll road for custom silicon and AI compute, Design IP recovers, Ansys expands the addressable market, and the combined company converts revenue growth into after-SBC margins above the FY2027 economic baseline while paying down acquisition debt. The concentrated economics create more upside than QQQ only if these company-specific execution steps occur; QQQ is superior in integration, export-control, customer-concentration and valuation-compression states.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating triggers measured from primary 10-Q/10-K or issuer results: (1) if FY2027 revenue guidance or actual revenue falls below $10.6b, cap subsequent modeled revenue CAGR at 7% and terminal P/E at 22; (2) if after-SBC operating margin, computed as GAAP operating margin plus acquired-intangible amortization plus restructuring but not SBC, is below 32% for two consecutive fiscal quarters through FY2028, cap terminal economic margin at 34%; (3) if current plus noncurrent debt exceeds $12b at two quarter-ends through FY2028 absent a separately underwritten acquisition, set terminal interest/other expense to at least $0.65b, prohibit negative share growth and move affected outcomes to lag; (4) if Design IP grows below 8% or S&A below 5% in two consecutive fiscal years through FY2029, cap consolidated revenue CAGR at 9%; (5) if annual SBC exceeds 10% of revenue in FY2028 or FY2029, use at least +1% share CAGR unless cash-funded repurchases fully cover issuance after debt service. Sources: SEC filings and Synopsys Investor Day/results pages in evidenceUrls.
