forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Amazon's Q2 2026 10-Q identifies the traded security as AMZN common stock, reports 10.7863 billion shares outstanding on July 22, 2026, and shows Q2 net sales of $200.606 billion, operating income of $27.461 billion, and diluted shares of 10.903 billion. GuruFocus marks the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT price at $259.92 and exposes annual/quarterly statements, key ratios and operating data; its financial endpoint exposed 2017-2025 plus TTM in the returned annual array, while its longer indicator history call returned a malformed-list validation error, so this draft does not claim a clean 15-year numeric panel. MODEL INFERENCE: the direct per-share framework excludes volatile investment marks and values recurring consolidated after-tax operating earnings after debt interest, with no value separately assigned to Anthropic, OpenAI, warrants, cash, or Globalstar synergies. Five-year revenue growth, terminal operating margin, net interest, tax, dilution and P/E are independently varied. HUMAN JUDGMENT: AWS/AI, advertising and higher-service mix can expand consolidated margin, but debt-funded AI infrastructure, OpenAI funding, Globalstar consideration, competition and valuation make QQQ the better default in three of six paths.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: AMZN beats QQQ only if high-margin AWS/AI and advertising scale faster than retail and infrastructure costs while consolidated operating margin rises materially above the sourced TTM baseline. The model assigns beat outcomes to a resilient QQQ-bear path, the strong QQQ-base execution path, and the exceptional QQQ-bull path; the subjective joint mass is 0.43. It deliberately lets QQQ win when revenue remains strong but margin, financing cost or terminal valuation disappoint, including a credible strong-company/strong-index lag state.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if reported consolidated net-sales growth is below 8% year over year AND operating margin is below 10% in each of two consecutive quarters, move all strong/exceptional execution mass to lag/impaired paths until two quarters recover; Q2 2026 was $200.606B versus $167.702B and $27.461B operating income, so this conjunction was not breached at model date. Pre-breach financing trigger: if reported long-term debt exceeds $200B while trailing operating income is below $100B for two consecutive quarters, cap terminal P/E at 20 and use at least $10B terminal net interest; June 30 debt was $128.894B before the documented July $24.867B net USD and September £4.235B net sterling offerings, so the $200B threshold was not evidenced as breached. Dilution trigger: if quarterly diluted weighted-average shares rise more than 2% year over year for two quarters, use at least 2% annual share growth in every path; Q2 was 10.903B versus 10.806B. Sources: Q2 10-Q and July/September financing 8-Ks.
forecasts.nextAction: Evidence & Risk should independently recompute every terminal price and five-year CAGR from the disclosed scenario inputs, verify grouped probabilities, and check the TTM bridge, post-quarter debt/interest baseline, Globalstar closing dilution, and treatment of Anthropic/OpenAI marks before North Star PM review. forecasts.limitations: SOURCE LIMITS: GuruFocus summary/financial/key-ratio packs were retrieved, but large payloads were persisted outside this tool's readable surface; the clean annual array visible in-tool ran 2017-2025 plus TTM, and the longer indicator and segment endpoints failed schema validation. GuruFocus segment data therefore was not relied on; SEC filings supplied segment and operating evidence. The Q2 release exhibit was image-heavy, so the 10-Q controls. NORMALIZATION: reported TTM net income of $135.281B and GuruFocus TTM EPS of $12.433 are not recurring earnings: the 10-Q cash-flow reconciliation identifies $79.818B of TTM non-operating income, and private-investment/warrant marks flow through other income. The model instead starts with sourced TTM revenue and operating income, retains recurring SBC expense, applies explicit interest and tax, then divides by diluted shares. It does not credit investment assets or future marks. Residual risks include exact post-quarter FX translation of sterling debt, floating-rate coupons, unknown future AI funding, Globalstar election/closing mechanics, antitrust/regulatory remedies, tariffs, capex useful lives, and terminal multiple sensitivity. Full-precision scenario outputs are mechanically computed from the disclosed revenue-growth, margin, net-interest, tax, diluted-share-growth and terminal-P/E assumptions and remain subject to independent arithmetic verification.
forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: June 30, 2026 cash plus marketable securities were $78.213B plus $44.775B; long-term debt was $128.894B, versus $65.648B at year-end. July 9 added $24.867B net proceeds across floating and 4.6%-6.25% notes; September 14 added £4.235B net proceeds across 5.2%-6.65% notes. A $17.5B delayed-draw term facility existed, with SOFR plus 0.625%-0.875% if drawn; the filing did not establish a draw in the retrieved evidence. Q2/H1 interest expense was $1.314B/$2.114B. Preferred stock: none issued or outstanding; no separate preferred/NCI deduction is modeled. Common shares were 10.7863B outstanding July 22; Q2/H1 diluted weighted averages were 10.903B/10.889B. Globalstar had 128,598,125 shares cited in the S-4/A; each stock election receives up to 0.3210 AMZN share, cash elections are capped at 40%, and closing is expected in 2027, so exact issuance equals 0.3210 times eligible stock-election shares subject to adjustments/cancellations. Scenario annual share growth of 0.5%-1.5% bounds ongoing awards plus acquisition dilution without assuming buybacks. OpenAI's remaining $21.3B commitment was funded after June 30; its gains are excluded from modeled earnings.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: The six joint probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated, not translated from any legacy rank, score, hurdle or IRR. QQQ marginal masses exactly equal 0.20 bear (0.12+0.08), 0.55 base (0.30+0.25), and 0.25 bull (0.15+0.10); total is 1.00. Conditional execution weights reflect evidence that Q2 revenue and operating income were growing rapidly, countered by more than $60B of first-half long-term debt proceeds, further July/September issuance, heavy capex, OpenAI funding and acquisition dilution. The computed strict beat mass is 0.43: 0.08 resilient/bear, 0.25 scale/base and 0.10 exceptional/bull. The other 0.57 explicitly allows QQQ to win.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Credo's FY2026 10-K identifies Nasdaq-traded ordinary shares (not an ADR), describes copper and optical interconnect products spanning AECs, retimers, DSPs, chiplets and IP, and reports FY2026 revenue of $1.335 billion, GAAP net income of $472.279 million and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.51. The filing says the top ten customers represented about 90% of revenue and end-customer B, D and E represented 32%, 33% and 19%, respectively. The Q1 FY2027 10-Q reports $479.003 million revenue, 64.5% GAAP gross margin, $129.425 million GAAP net income and $0.67 GAAP diluted EPS; the issuer's Q1 results release guided Q2 revenue to $525-$535 million. Model inference: the direct per-share framework starts with FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.51 and values five-year terminal GAAP EPS after explicit net-income growth and diluted-share growth at a scenario P/E. The thesis requires Credo's low-power connectivity content to expand with AI cluster density while new optical products broaden the revenue base. Human judgment: the terminal multiples and outcome probabilities are subjective research assumptions, not issuer guidance or calibrated probabilities.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Credo beats QQQ only if unusually strong per-share earnings growth outruns dilution and offsets substantial valuation compression. The base execution-win case requires 32% annual net-income growth, 2% annual diluted-share growth and a 45x terminal P/E from $2.51 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS. The QQQ alternative is preferable if customer concentration, optical integration or competition reduces net-income growth to the 16% base-lag assumption while dilution reaches 4% and the terminal P/E contracts to 35x. Source facts support exceptional recent growth but do not establish its durability: Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 114.7% year over year, while FY2026 top-ten customer concentration was about 90%. This is price-only research, not a portfolio or trade instruction.
forecasts.falsifier: Review each 10-Q and 10-K through FY2029. Metric/threshold/window/source/consequence: (1) if year-over-year revenue growth is below 25% for two consecutive quarters, move probability from each execution-win branch to its paired lag branch and recompute; (2) if GAAP gross margin is below 60% for two consecutive quarters, cap the terminal P/E at 30x pending a new model; (3) if basic ordinary shares exceed 210 million by the FY2028 year end or quarterly diluted weighted-average shares exceed 225 million, replace all share-growth assumptions with the observed higher rate; (4) if rolling-four-quarter GAAP diluted EPS growth is below 20% in two consecutive reports, treat QQQ as the preferred default until re-underwritten; and (5) if top-ten customer concentration remains at least 80% in FY2028 and any disclosed at-least-10% end customer's annual revenue share falls by at least 20 percentage points year over year, mark the row temporarily unrankable. Use the issuer's quarterly and annual filings for revenue, margin, EPS, shares and customer concentration.

Reported basis: 186,477,898 ordinary shares were outstanding on June 8, 2026; the Q1 10-Q reports 187.768 million issued and outstanding on August 1, 2026 and 187,951,918 outstanding on August 25, 2026. Q1 diluted weighted-average shares were 194.378 million, versus 186.007 million basic; FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares were 188.232 million. The August 1 10-Q reports 8.3 million RSUs and 3.1 million PSUs expected to vest plus 1.7 million options expected to vest or already exercisable; Q1 SBC was $87.979 million versus $129.425 million GAAP net income, making dilution material. forecasts.probabilityRationale: These are fresh subjective conditional weights, not empirical or legacy-score translations. The bear state places most mass on execution lag because a $220.01 starting price against $2.51 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS leaves little tolerance for customer loss or multiple compression; only the smaller bear-win branch assumes sufficient earnings growth to offset contraction. The base state is also tilted to lag because FY2026 top-ten concentration was about 90%, Q1 SBC was large relative to GAAP income, and DustPhotonics introduces integration and contingent-share risk, despite reported Q1 revenue growth of 114.7% and Q2 revenue guidance of $525-$535 million. The bull state tilts to execution win because broad AI infrastructure spending, AEC and IC ramps and the issuer's greater-than-$500 million FY2027 optical-revenue expectation could create sustained operating leverage. The paired weights exactly reproduce the required QQQ marginals: 0.04+0.16 for bear, 0.24+0.31 for base, and 0.15+0.10 for bull. Using the supplied deterministic outputs, the strict-beat branches are bear/execution wins, base/execution wins and bull/execution wins, for a subjective 0.43 total probability of beating QQQ.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001835632 as Marvell Technology, Inc., with common stock trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under MRVL. GuruFocus' 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT quote is $284.68 USD. Q2 FY2027 revenue was $2.7393B, up 37% YoY; data-center revenue was about $2.17B/79% of total and up 46% YoY. Q2 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.33 and issuer-adjusted diluted EPS $0.94. Q3 guidance was $3.15B revenue +/-5%, 921M diluted shares, $0.53 GAAP EPS +/-$0.05 and $1.10 non-GAAP EPS +/-$0.05. The Q3 bridge excludes $0.34/share SBC, $0.21 acquired-intangible amortization and $0.05 other, partly offset by a $0.03 tax adjustment; the non-GAAP tax assumption is 11%. MODEL INFERENCE: use $4.40 normalized forward diluted EPS/share, the $1.10 Q3 midpoint annualized, rather than raw TTM GAAP EPS. This is a run-rate convention, not issuer FY guidance, and it is generous because SBC is recurring. Five-year outcomes grow total normalized earnings 10%-50% annually, separately apply 2%-3% annual diluted-share growth, then apply 24x-38x terminal P/E. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Marvell can beat QQQ only if AI custom silicon, optics, switching and scale-up connectivity sustain unusually high earnings growth; the price already requires substantial execution. Counter-thesis: hyperscaler concentration, discretionary Google purchase milestones, TSMC/supply dependence, integration risk and recurring excluded costs produce slower growth and multiple compression, making diversified QQQ the superior default.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MODEL INFERENCE: MRVL has more operating leverage to AI infrastructure than QQQ if data-center revenue remains broad across electro-optics, switching, storage and custom silicon and if current growth converts to normalized earnings faster than diluted shares rise. The base-execution and exceptional paths require 40% and 50% annual total normalized-earnings growth, respectively, while diluted shares grow 2.5%-3%; they do not assume buybacks. QQQ wins in the demand-setback, base-deceleration and bull-valuation-reset paths because MRVL's $284.68 starting price and adjusted-EPS exclusions leave little margin for merely good execution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: upside is concentrated, not QQQ-like; accepting this as a core candidate requires belief that Marvell's customer programs are durable enough to offset single-customer, dilution and valuation risk.
forecasts.falsifier: Observe the next two issuer earnings releases and 10-Qs through Q4 FY2027. If data-center revenue growth is below 25% YoY in both quarters, or issuer-adjusted diluted EPS is below $1.10 for two consecutive quarters despite at least $3.15B quarterly revenue, cap total normalized-earnings growth at 20% and terminal P/E at 28x in every path. Separately, if SEC-reported diluted weighted-average shares exceed 960M before FY2028 without a commensurate per-share earnings increase, use at least 3% annual share growth. Sources: exact SEC 10-Q/8-K earnings exhibits and issuer reconciliations listed in evidenceUrls. These thresholds are author judgments, not company guidance.
forecasts.nextAction: Evidence & Risk should independently reconcile the recurring SBC/intangible exclusions, test whether the 2%-3% annual dilution range bounds the NVIDIA preferred conversion, Google warrant, awards and acquisition issuance, and page-check Investor Day deck pages 38-40 and 142-143. Exact PM judgment remains required on whether adjusted EPS is an acceptable starting metric and whether MRVL's concentrated upside merits inclusion versus QQQ; this research authorizes no rank, size or trade.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: HUMAN JUDGMENT: probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated; none comes from a legacy score, rank, IRR or hurdle. QQQ masses are fixed at 0.20/0.55/0.25. Within QQQ bear, 0.12 goes to a customer/demand setback and 0.08 to resilient AI execution. Within QQQ base, 0.30 goes to deceleration and 0.25 to broad execution. Within QQQ bull, 0.15 goes to participation with valuation reset and 0.10 to exceptional execution. The heavier lag weights reflect the high starting price, adjusted-EPS exclusions, hyperscaler concentration and dilution instruments. The upside weights reflect verified 37% company and 46% data-center Q2 growth, Q3 acceleration guidance and broad product exposure. QQQ is explicitly preferred in credible lag states. The resulting strict five-year price-outperformance probability is 0.43.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus historical-price output returns the Nasdaq Class A close at $237.15 on 2026-10-07, and its key-ratio payload is timestamped 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT. Nebius's Q2 2026 SEC-furnished results report revenue of $582.3m, +454% YoY; Nebius AI cloud supplied $574.9m and reached $3.0bn annualized run-rate revenue (last-month revenue x12). Q2 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $236.2m, but GAAP operating loss was $175.9m and GAAP continuing net loss was $190.4m, or $0.68 per diluted share. Q2 cost of revenue $133.6m + product development $191.0m + SG&A $173.9m + D&A $259.7m = $758.2m total operating costs versus $582.3m revenue; SBC was $102.5m. This is not normalized profitability: D&A, SBC and financing costs are economically material. The reported-to-model revenue bridge is Q3 2025 $146.1m + Q4 2025 $227.7m + Q1 2026 $399.0m + Q2 2026 $582.3m = $1,355.1m TTM; the model instead starts from $3.2bn FY2026E, the midpoint of issuer guidance of $3.0bn-$3.4bn, because capacity and contracted deployments make TTM revenue stale. MODEL INFERENCE: value the still-GAAP-loss-making company as enterprise value/revenue, then deduct terminal net debt and divide by a fully diluted share denominator. Five-year terminal revenue equals $3.2bn times the stated scenario growth for five years; terminal enterprise value equals terminal revenue times the stated EV/revenue multiple. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the current valuation embeds substantial execution; only paths with roughly 35%-50% five-year revenue growth and sustained 9x-13x terminal EV/revenue produce attractive per-share outcomes after financing dilution.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Nebius can beat QQQ if its $37.5bn of reported remaining performance obligations at June 30, Microsoft/Meta deployments, higher ACV per MW, customer prepayments and expanding power footprint convert into sustained revenue growth while AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA economics remain strong. Q2 management reported four landmark deals averaging >$1bn, 70% of deals with prepayments covering 50%-60% of related capex, a 1-year-10-month estimated payback for Q2 deals, and a 5 GW year-end contracted-power target. The counter-thesis is that $237.15 already prices a large share of this success: GAAP operating profit and FCF remain negative after D&A and capex, customer concentration is high, capacity requires repeated debt/equity issuance, and terminal multiple compression can overwhelm revenue growth. QQQ is the better default in the 59% joint probability assigned to the three lag paths; modeled beat probability is 41%, an uncalibrated author judgment.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: when FY2026 results are filed, revenue below $3.0bn OR year-end Nebius AI-cloud ARR below $6.5bn (versus issuer guidance $3.0bn-$3.4bn revenue and $7bn-$9bn ARR) moves all win paths to their same-benchmark lag path and caps any rerun terminal EV/revenue multiple at 6x. Pre-breach financing trigger: at each quarterly/annual filing through 2027, gross funded debt above $18bn before reported Nebius AI-cloud ARR reaches $7bn, or an economic diluted-share sensitivity above 440m before ARR reaches $7bn, forces at least the base-lag denominator/net-debt assumptions and removes the bull-win path. Quality trigger: two consecutive quarters with Nebius AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin below 30% after ARR exceeds $4bn forces revenue growth assumptions down by at least 10 percentage points. Sources are the issuer's SEC-furnished results, debt filings and outstanding-share/equity-award disclosures. None of these forward windows was observable as breached at 2026-10-07; Q2 ARR was $3.0bn, Q2 AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin was 49.7%, and disclosed debt components remained below the $18bn trigger. Consequence is an explicit probability/model reset, not an automatic trade.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: Uncalibrated subjective joint weights are independent of any legacy rank, conviction score or hurdle. QQQ bear mass 0.20 splits 0.08 failure / 0.12 recovery because weak capital markets hurt funding but a lower QQQ hurdle lets a modest positive NBIS CAGR outperform. QQQ base mass 0.55 splits 0.33 lag / 0.22 win because the current valuation requires exceptional growth and valuation durability. QQQ bull mass 0.25 splits 0.18 lag / 0.07 win because broad AI prosperity benefits Nebius demand but makes QQQ's 18% hurdle difficult; only the extreme scale/valuation path wins. Total lag mass is 0.59 and beat mass is 0.41. All revenue growth, terminal multiples, terminal net debt and share counts are author-selected scenario assumptions, not issuer forecasts except the common $3.2bn starting midpoint.

The result is $356.888838095238 and an 8.51804652888215% five-year price CAGR, below QQQ's deliberately difficult 18% hurdle; sector growth alone does not establish relative outperformance.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: TTM IFRS revenue is $19,339.757m and pretax income is $4,384.603m; Q2 had 138.9m customers, $17.1 ARPAC, 12.4% risk-adjusted NIM and 33% managerial ROE. The H1 SEC tax reconciliation starts from a 42.5% combined Brazilian rate, which Nu says is not materially different from the average effective rate across its jurisdictions before reconciling permanent items and jurisdiction effects. On $2,190.619m H1 pretax income, theoretical tax was $931.013m; disclosed reductions included $280.789m from different subsidiary/parent rates, $108.793m interest on capital, $28.405m from rate changes and $253.617m other amounts, mainly foreign tax credits, tax-exempt sovereign-bond interest, incentives and non-taxable interest on tax recoverables. Reported H1 tax was $258.099m, comprising $1,249.145m current expense and a $991.046m deferred benefit. Model inference: reported tax is not a recurring earnings rate because deferred-tax formation and realization are timing items, while neither recurring permanent exclusions nor country mix is sufficiently bounded to support the rejected 35% normalization. The revised direct per-share model therefore uses a 40%-42.5% normalized IFRS range, with 42.5% in every bear/base path and 40% only in the bull execution path; 40% is the filing's H1-2025 theoretical comparator, not guidance. Human judgment: customer/ARPAC growth and low service cost can compound USD revenue, but the valuation retains funding, ECL, operating expense, SBC, FX, capital and dilution risk.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: NU beats QQQ only in the 0.30 base-scaled and 0.11 bull-platform paths, for 0.41 strict-win probability after tax remediation. The former requires 18% USD revenue CAGR, 43% gross margin after funding/transaction/ECL cost, 16% opex/revenue, 42.5% normalized IFRS tax, 0.8% annual share growth and 20x terminal P/E; the latter requires 23%, 46%, 14%, 40%, 0.5% and 23x, respectively. QQQ is superior in the remaining 0.59 probability. In particular, applying 42.5% rather than rejected 35% tax to bear-resilient execution changes its terminal value by 0.575/0.65 and flips that 0.11 path from a strict win to a lag versus QQQ bear. This explicitly reduces strict-win mass from 0.52 to 0.41 rather than hiding the sensitivity. If cash less debt falls below $75m, annualized total economic-unit growth exceeds 5%, or equity is issued outside the modeled LTIP award stack for financing or acquisitions, suspend all beat classifications at the next refresh until an explicit funding and fully diluted unit bridge is rebuilt. forecasts.thesis: Source facts: the audited FY2025 20-F reports revenue RMB431.845713bn, operating profit RMB93.102131bn, and net income attributable to ordinary shareholders RMB97.842539bn. The earlier unaudited release reported operating profit RMB94.624061bn and net income RMB99.364469bn, so both profit figures were reduced by RMB1.521930bn in the audited filing; this model uses the audited values. The Q2 2026 exhibit reports H1 2026/H1 2025 revenue RMB218.587bn/RMB199.657bn, operating profit RMB47.330bn/RMB41.879bn, and net income RMB39.729bn/RMB45.496bn. Therefore the issuer-period TTM bridges are revenue 431.845713+218.587-199.657=RMB450.775713bn, operating profit 93.102131+47.330-41.879=RMB98.553131bn, and net income 97.842539+39.729-45.496=RMB92.075539bn. The audited FY2025 diluted EPS was RMB16.50 per ordinary share; four ordinary shares equal one ADS; H1 2026/H1 2025 diluted EPADS were RMB26.90/RMB30.69. TTM diluted EPADS is therefore 16.50*4+26.90-30.69=RMB62.21. Using the 20-F's explicit 2025-12-31 convenience rate of RMB6.9931/USD gives USD8.895911684374598 per ADS and a USD78.50 starting P/E of 8.824278251085035x. GuruFocus reports USD9.015 TTM EPS, USD0.11908831562540279 or 1.3386859025880151% higher; its exact FX/period convention was not exposed, so the difference is disclosed rather than forced away. Model inference: the low starting multiple can beat QQQ if commerce revenue compounds at least high single digits, GAAP operating margin remains near the high teens or better, and trade/regulatory costs do not strand cash or destroy Temu economics. Counter-thesis: Q2 growth slowed to 8%, management is increasing ecosystem and supply-chain investment, non-operating income is volatile, and ADS/VIE, cash-access, tariff, consumer-protection, product-safety, dilution, and delisting risks can permanently impair value.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: At USD78.50 and issuer-convention TTM diluted EPADS of USD8.895911684374598, PDD starts at 8.824278251085035x earnings, far below the multiples normally associated with durable double-digit growth. The favorable paths require explicit revenue growth, GAAP margins, diluted-equivalent share growth, tax, FX, and terminal P/E assumptions; no terminal net-cash add or buyback benefit is used. The revised joint-outcome probability of strictly beating the paired QQQ return is 0.40: durable execution 0.25, solid compounding 0.10, and global upside 0.05. QQQ remains the better default in the other 0.60 because PDD's VIE enforceability, Cayman-holder rights, China cash access, tariff/de-minimis, governance, and platform-investment risks are issuer-specific. The 5% VIE-loss scenario explicitly permits a near-total ADS impairment rather than treating intact consolidated earnings as a floor.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach facts: Q1/Q2 2026 revenue growth was 11%/8%; Q1/Q2 GAAP operating margin was about 18%/25%; June cash plus cash equivalents and short-term investments was RMB456.4bn; H1 basic/diluted weighted-average ordinary shares were 5.622bn/5.907bn. At the first reporting date on which any trigger is observable, falsify every favorable scenario if (a) revenue growth is below 3% for two consecutive quarters, (b) GAAP operating margin is below 12% for two consecutive quarters, (c) cash plus cash equivalents and short-term investments is below RMB300bn at quarter-end without an equal clearly distributable asset, or (d) diluted weighted-average ordinary shares exceed 6.25bn for two consecutive reported periods. Also trigger immediately, before any trading prohibition takes effect, upon an official notice or company disclosure that VIE arrangements may no longer be used, consolidation/economic benefits cannot be received, or an HFCA/PCAOB trading prohibition is pending. Deterministic rerun: set durable execution 0.25, solid compounding 0.10, and global upside 0.05 to zero; transfer 0.25 to base lag, raising it from 0.30 to 0.55, and transfer 0.15 to bull regulatory lag, raising it from 0.05 to 0.20. Leave bear severe/rebuild and VIE-loss weights unchanged. Post-trigger weights are severe 0.12, rebuild 0.08, base lag 0.55, durable 0, VIE loss 0.05, bull lag 0.20, solid 0, and global 0; they total 1.00, preserve QQQ marginals 0.20/0.55/0.25, and reduce probabilityBeatQqq to 0.00.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: Human judgment: joint probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated, not translations of a prior rank, score, conviction, or expected return. QQQ marginals remain fixed at 0.20 bear, 0.55 base, and 0.25 bull. Bear paths are severe impairment 0.12 and rebuild 0.08. Base paths are lag 0.30 and durable execution 0.25. forecasts.thesis: Source facts: FormFactor supplies probe cards and test/measurement systems across the semiconductor lifecycle. Its filed Q2 2026 release reported $258.242 million revenue, 50.7% GAAP gross margin, $0.71 GAAP diluted EPS and $0.82 non-GAAP diluted EPS; H1 revenue was $484.386 million, with Probe Cards $407.952 million and Systems $76.434 million. The 10-Q attributes Foundry & Logic growth to networking/high-performance-compute demand and DRAM growth primarily to HBM demand. Model inference: $2.20 starting normalized annual diluted EPS is not a reported metric or guidance; it lies between the annual implications of H1 GAAP diluted EPS of $0.96 and H1 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.38, credits only part of the restructuring-related normalization and continues to burden recurring SBC. Human judgment: FORM can compound this baseline rapidly only if HBM, advanced-logic and co-packaged-optics demand persists, factory changes hold margins, and customer-specific wins broaden. The $139.80 price already requires strong execution and leaves substantial multiple-compression risk.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: FORM has a narrower but potentially faster earnings vector than QQQ: probe-card complexity and test intensity can rise with HBM generations, high-performance-compute CPUs/custom ASICs, advanced packaging and co-packaged optics. Filed H1 2026 revenue grew strongly year over year and Q2 gross margin reached 50.7%, demonstrating operating leverage when mix and volume align. The stock can beat only in stronger execution paths where normalized EPS-pool growth and a premium terminal P/E overcome a uniform 2.0% annual increase in the forward GAAP diluted weighted-average share denominator. QQQ is the better alternative when customer concentration, semiconductor cyclicality, competition, export controls, mix reversal, execution or valuation compression prevents that combination.
forecasts.falsifier: Measure from each filed 10-Q/10-K and earnings exhibit. Before a full thesis breach, move all scenarios to a dilution review if the next filed quarter's diluted weighted-average shares exceed the prior-year quarter by more than 2%, or if newly granted/issued equity plus the remaining plan reserve indicates the 2.0% annual denominator assumption is underbounded; give no buyback offset unless repurchases have actually occurred. Falsify the above-base execution thesis if, in any two consecutive reported quarters, (a) total revenue year-over-year growth is 5% or less and GAAP gross margin is below 42%, or (b) combined DRAM plus Foundry & Logic revenue declines at least 10% year over year. Forecast consequence: constrain EPS-pool growth to 8% or less, use share growth of at least the observed diluted-share rate, cap terminal P/E at 25x, rerun the direct per-share bridge, and default to QQQ. These are author thresholds, not issuer guidance.
forecasts.nextAction: After the 2026 Q3 10-Q is filed, reconcile GAAP EPS, restructuring, SBC, basic and diluted weighted-average shares, RSU/ESPP activity, plan-reserve usage, segment revenue and gross margin to the $2.20 starting EPS and 2.0% forward diluted-share assumption. Confirm whether Q3 guidance of $270 million revenue and $0.75 GAAP diluted EPS was achieved, rerun all outcomes if evidence changes the model, and obtain new exact-byte author confirmation, independent Evidence & Risk review and North Star PM judgment before persistence or ranking.

Model inference: the $2.20 starting EPS is already on a diluted-share basis, so every scenario starts from the H1 GAAP diluted weighted-average denominator of 79.546 million and grows that same denominator by 2.0% annually. forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Micron's September 30, 2026 8-K identifies the listed security as $0.10-par common stock trading as MU on Nasdaq Global Select Market. Its attached FY2026 release reports $133.188 billion revenue, $84.969 billion GAAP net income, $74.33 diluted EPS on 1.143 billion weighted-average diluted shares, $89.68 billion operating cash flow, $27.37 billion net capital expenditures, and $62.31 billion adjusted free cash flow; Q4 revenue was $54.229 billion and GAAP diluted EPS was $32.87. The issuer's Q4 prepared remarks say the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bit supply is covered by agreements at significant year-over-year price increases, while the Q3 10-Q describes multi-year take-or-pay strategic customer agreements and also warns that DRAM and NAND selling prices have historically been extremely volatile. Model inference: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33 is the common direct-per-share starting metric; five-year aggregate net-income growth, dilution/buyback bounds, and terminal P/E—not a selected stock CAGR—determine every outcome. Human judgment: the contracts and HBM mix may improve durability, but 80.7% FY2026 GAAP gross margin and a $1,088 starting price embed an extraordinary shortage cycle, so most probability remains on execution-lag outcomes.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MU beats QQQ only if contracted supply, HBM leadership, and disciplined industry capacity let aggregate earnings remain durable or compound from the record FY2026 base while dilution stays controlled. At $1,088, the trailing GAAP P/E implied by issuer EPS is not itself the hard problem; the hard problem is whether record shortage-era EPS persists through 2031. The modeled base-win path requires 12% annual aggregate net-income growth, 0.5% annual share shrinkage, and a 14x terminal P/E. The QQQ alternative is superior in the three execution-lag paths because it diversifies away Micron's memory-pricing, customer, technology-transition, capex, and China risks and does not require one producer's record margin to persist.
forecasts.falsifier: Move probability from each execution-win path to its paired lag path if either (1) Micron reports GAAP gross margin below 60% for two consecutive quarters within the next eight reported quarters, using 10-Q/10-K statements; (2) disclosed SCA remaining performance obligations or covered-volume expectations fall more than 20% year over year without an explained conversion to recognized revenue, using issuer prepared remarks/filings; (3) calendar-2027/2028 HBM qualification or shipment commitments are delayed by two quarters or more, using issuer releases/filings; or (4) diluted weighted-average shares rise more than 1% year over year for two consecutive fiscal years absent demonstrably accretive M&A, using 10-K EPS footnotes. If FY2028 GAAP diluted EPS is below $74.33 despite the issuer's FY2027 supply commentary, retire the positive aggregate-growth assumptions and re-underwrite from normalized trough earnings. Conversely, two fiscal years with gross margin above 65%, no material SCA cancellations, and diluted shares flat/down would support retaining—not automatically increasing—the win weights.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT close at $386.05 and identifies the security as Ordinary Shares-Class A; SEC CIK 0000877212 and the Q2 2026 10-Q identify NASDAQ-traded Class A common stock. SEC arithmetic for the TTM ended 2026-07-04 is revenue $5,847m = $5,396m FY2025 - $2,601m H1 2025 + $3,052m H1 2026; GAAP operating income $858m = $700m-$378m+$536m; GAAP net income $539m = $419m-$248m+$368m; and summed diluted EPS $10.91 = $8.18-$4.81+$7.54. NORMALIZATION/MODEL INFERENCE: add back H2 2025 exit/restructuring $76m and acquisition/integration $17m, H1 2026 purchase-accounting $5m, acquisition/integration $3m and exit costs $16m; subtract Q2's nonrecurring $73m tariff-refund benefit. That yields normalized operating income about $902m. Below operating income, add back only H1 investment losses net of sale/other gains ($15m-$5m-$3m=$7m), while retaining interest, FX and debt-issuance costs. Applying a 19% tax assumption to the $51m pretax adjustment gives normalized net income about $580m = $539m + $51m*(1-0.19), or about $12.1 per diluted share on the 48.0m model base; the SEC-reported Q2 diluted weighted-average count was 48.129m. All bridge arithmetic is author-calculated and requires independent verification. SBC and intangible amortization are retained because equity compensation recurs and acquisitions/intangible consumption are part of Zebra's operating model; company non-GAAP TTM EPS of $19.29 (FY2025 $15.84 less H1 2025 $7.63 plus H1 2026 $11.08) is therefore not used as economic EPS. HUMAN JUDGMENT: durable AIDC leadership, machine vision, RFID and AI-assisted frontline workflows can compound, but the $386.05 price demands substantial growth and margin expansion relative to this conservative earnings base.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Zebra can beat QQQ only if organic growth remains mid/high single digit or better, Elo integration and machine-vision/frontline-AI products lift consolidated margins, and cash generation reduces refinancing risk without relying on buybacks. Q2 organic sales grew 9.2% (CF 7.5%, AVA 11.4%); management guided FY2026 reported growth of 14%-16%, including about 8 points from acquisitions/dispositions/FX, 23.5%-24.0% adjusted EBITDA margin, $20.75-$21.25 non-GAAP EPS and greater than $1bn FCF. Those are source facts, not forecast assumptions. The counter-thesis is that recent growth is acquisition/FX-assisted, Q2 margin includes a $73m tariff refund, services/software grew only 1.3% in Q2, Elo increased debt and goodwill, and machine-vision/AI revenue and attach rates are undisclosed. At conservative normalized EPS near $12.1, valuation is demanding; QQQ is the better default in the central and lag paths unless Zebra achieves durable revenue/margin upside.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Vertiv's cited 2025 Form 10-K identifies the NYSE-listed Class A common stock and reports $10,229.9 million of 2025 sales and $15.0 billion of year-end backlog versus $7.2 billion one year earlier, while warning that orders can be cancelled or deferred. The June 2026 10-Q reports H1 sales of $5,923.8 million, operating profit of $1,078.0 million, net income of $887.9 million and diluted EPS of $2.26; Q2 gross profit was $1,234.9 million on $3,274.3 million of sales, or 37.7%. H1 growth included $226.3 million of acquisition-related sales and $92.6 million of favorable FX. GuruFocus summary, annual/quarterly financials and key ratios were pulled before valuation; its financial history runs from 2017 but pre-2020 per-share history is zero/non-comparable, and its segment endpoint failed response-schema validation, so the SEC filing is the segment source. REPORTED-TO-SELECTED STARTING-EPS BRIDGE: FY2025 diluted GAAP EPS $3.41 minus H1 2025 diluted GAAP EPS $1.25 plus H1 2026 diluted GAAP EPS $2.26 equals selected TTM diluted GAAP EPS $4.42; GuruFocus reports $4.419 TTM. The model deliberately makes no non-GAAP add-back. The TTM includes acquisition intangible amortization of $269.9 million, calculated from source amounts as FY2025 $211.5 million minus H1 2025 $92.9 million plus H1 2026 $151.3 million; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes the H1 2026 $62.0 million contingent-consideration fair-value loss; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes H1 2026 $29.6 million of swap-related interest income; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes the $6.2 million debt-extinguishment loss; selected adjustment $0.00. It also retains reported taxes: the filing gives a 16.1% H1 2026 effective rate versus 28.8% in H1 2025, with H1 2026 affected by stock-compensation benefits and the swap settlement; selected tax adjustment $0.00. This is a causal GAAP base, not a normalized claim. COMPUTED SENSITIVITY CONTRACT: using 392.511287 million H1 diluted shares, the conservative lower-start formula 4.42-(29.6/392.511287)-(((1058.3*0.235)-170.4)/392.511287) equals $4.145102172666948, removing all H1 swap income and recasting H1 tax to the 2025 full-year 23.5% effective rate. The operating-adjusted upper-start formula 4.42+((62.0*(1-0.235))/392.511287)+((269.9*(1-0.235))/392.511287)-((29.6*(1-0.235))/392.511287)-(((1058.3*0.235)-170.4)/392.511287) equals $4.809693252311493. These are author calculations, not source-reported EPS. Substituting the lower start in the three authored winning branches produces five-year price CAGRs of -0.03290734056665845 in bear/resilient, 0.12499771003852023 in base/strong and 0.18572187973668375 in bull/strong; each remains strictly above its respective -0.04, 0.10 and 0.18 QQQ return. Therefore all three main-case win classifications and the 0.36 strict-win mass survive the conservative lower-start sensitivity. MODEL INFERENCE: AI and high-density compute can sustain unusually high demand for power, cooling and deployment infrastructure, but a direct GAAP-EPS model must absorb acquisition amortization, financing, cyclicality and dilution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: retain reported $4.42 rather than claim a normalized result; use aggregate post-financing, post-amortization GAAP earnings growth and terminal P/E, with no buyback benefit.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Vertiv can beat QQQ only if power-density, liquid-cooling, service and modular-deployment demand converts backlog into earnings growth far above aggregate Nasdaq-100 earnings while margins remain structurally higher. The cited filing supplies current evidence for that possibility: H1 2026 sales grew 26.7%, operating profit 47.0% and net income 81.7%, with strong Americas and APAC operating leverage. The offset is severe starting-valuation risk: $246.49 divided by selected SEC-derived $4.42 trailing diluted GAAP EPS is 55.76696832579186x. QQQ is the better default in the lag branches, where growth normalizes, acquisitions dilute GAAP earnings or terminal P/E compresses to 20x-32x. The deterministic main-case results show strict VRT wins only in bear/resilient, base/strong and bull/strong, for authored aggregate outperformance probability 0.36; the economic assumptions were selected independently rather than reverse-engineered from a desired rank. The computed lower-start sensitivity preserves those classifications, but its bull/strong CAGR of 0.18572187973668375 remains only narrowly above the 0.18 QQQ bull assumption.
forecasts.falsifier: Exact metric/threshold/window/source/consequence contract: (1) At each of the next two quarterly filings, if reported year-over-year net-sales growth is below 10% for two consecutive quarters or consolidated gross margin is below 34% for two consecutive quarters, remove all resilient/strong mass and transfer it to the lag branch in the same QQQ state: bear/resilient 0.08 moves to bear/lag, making bear 0.00/0.20; base/strong 0.20 moves to base/lag, making base 0.00/0.55; bull/strong 0.08 moves to bull/lag, making bull 0.00/0.25. (2) At the next Form 10-K, if backlog is below $12.0 billion, the same exact within-state transfer applies. (3) At every quarterly filing through December 31, 2027, compare actual common shares outstanding and diluted weighted-average shares with 384,988,173 and 392,511,287; if either grows more than 1.5% year over year absent a disclosed share-funded acquisition that is demonstrably accretive to GAAP EPS, replace every lower dilution input with 1.5% and recalculate all outcomes. (4) Utility Innovation closing funding is tested in the closing 8-K and first 10-Q after close: if upfront cash consideration after contractual adjustments exceeds $1.595 billion, exactly 10% above the disclosed approximately $1.45 billion, or if total Utility Innovation contingent cash paid or recognized as payable exceeds the contractual $1.15 billion ceiling, apply the same within-state mass transfer and cap terminal P/E at the corresponding lag multiple: 20x in QQQ bear, 28x in QQQ base and 32x in QQQ bull. (5) At every quarter-end through December 31, 2027, if issuer-reported consolidated net debt/adjusted EBITDA exceeds 3.0x, apply that same transfer and lag-multiple cap until the ratio is below 3.0x for two consecutive quarters. (6) King consideration is undisclosed. In the closing 8-K and first 10-Q after close, if total cash plus fair value of contingent/share consideration exceeds the model's $250 million author reserve, apply the same transfer and multiple cap. These are pre-declared reproducible consequences, not monitoring-only language.
forecasts.nextAction: After the next VRT 10-Q or acquisition-closing filing, refresh the four-quarter diluted GAAP EPS base and rerun the same per-share formulas after verifying Q3 sales, gross margin, orders/backlog, Utility Innovation and King purchase prices, funding, purchase-price allocations, amortization, contingent-consideration remeasurement/payment, debt, interest income/expense, diluted shares, SBC and any repurchases. Any changed forecast requires new canonical bytes/hash, exact-byte author confirmation, independent Evidence & Risk review and North Star PM decision; this draft is not publication, sizing or trade approval.
forecasts.theme: AI power, liquid cooling and critical digital infrastructure
forecasts.limitations: SOURCE LIMITS: Latest filed financial statements available at the October 7 model date cover June 30, 2026; no Q3 2026 10-Q was available. Starting $4.42 is constructed from rounded SEC per-share figures; GuruFocus's $4.419 TTM corroborates it, but rounding can move the start by about $0.001. Vertiv has been public only since February 2020, so a clean 15-year public-company history is unavailable; the GuruFocus pull begins in 2017 and pre-2020 per-share history is zero/non-comparable. The GuruFocus segment call failed response-schema validation, so SEC Americas/APAC/EMEA and product/services disclosures are used. MODEL LIMITS: The $4.42 base is reported GAAP, not normalized. The computed $4.145102172666948 lower and $4.809693252311493 upper starts intentionally expose rather than hide judgment: $269.9 million TTM amortization is source-derived, while applying a 23.5% tax rate and deciding which items to remove are author choices. Utility Innovation has not closed. Its approximately $1.45 billion upfront cash, customary adjustments and maximum $1.15 billion contingent cash are disclosed, but purchase-price allocation, amortization, exact funding mix, fees, earnout timing and tax effects are unknown. King consideration is undisclosed; $250 million is an author reserve and falsifier, not a source fact. Dividends are excluded because ranking is price-only. Terminal multiples, funding-rate bounds and probabilities are human judgment, not issuer guidance or calibrated frequencies. HUMAN DECISION STILL REQUIRED: after independent Evidence & Risk review, the North Star PM must decide whether the narrow lower-start bull/strong margin and authored 0.36 probability are decision-useful versus QQQ; no portfolio action is authorized.
forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: The June 2026 10-Q reports 384,936,985 Class A shares outstanding at June 30 and 384,988,173 at July 27; H1 diluted weighted-average shares were 392,511,287. It reports 8.8 million dilutive equity awards, another 0.5 million anti-dilutive awards, $30.8 million H1 SBC, no 2026 repurchases and $2.4 billion remaining authorization. Actual shares rose from 382,553,680 at December 2025 to 384,936,985 at June 2026. At June 30, cash was $2,810.6 million, short-term investments $300.0 million and long-term debt $2,939.8 million, yielding the source-based static $170.8 million net-cash bridge. The 10-Q reports $2,483.6 million of revolver availability and a 4.0x maximum consolidated-net-debt/EBITDA covenant, temporarily electable to 4.5x after a qualifying acquisition. The September 1 agreement requires approximately $1.45 billion upfront cash, subject to customary adjustments, plus up to $1.15 billion contingent cash and says existing resources will fund it. Static post-upfront net debt is approximately $1,279.2 million; if the full $1.15 billion earnout were also paid without intervening cash generation, static net debt would be approximately $2,429.2 million, before fees, King, taxes, working capital or new borrowing. Existing contingent-consideration liabilities were $234.6 million at June 30. MODEL INFERENCE AND HUMAN-JUDGMENT FINANCING BOUNDS: Every 12%-29% aggregate earnings-growth input is after lost interest income, incremental interest, GAAP acquisition amortization, transaction/integration fees, earnout remeasurement and King; none is an unfinanced operating-growth rate. For the $1.45 billion upfront payment, resilient/strong branches assume a 4%-6% annual pretax cash/debt opportunity-cost range and lag branches 6%-8%. At a 23.5% tax rate and 392.511287 million diluted shares, the computed annual after-tax EPS costs are $0.11304133529286255-$0.16956200293929385 for 4%-6% and $0.16956200293929385-$0.2260826705857251 for 6%-8%. If the full $1.15 billion earnout is paid, cumulative use becomes $2.60 billion and the computed annual after-tax EPS costs are $0.20269480811133975-$0.3040422121670096 for 4%-6% and $0.3040422121670096-$0.4053896162226795 for 6%-8%. The model assumes the full earnout is paid in resilient/strong branches by the end of 2029 and zero earnout in lag branches when targets are missed; any fair-value remeasurement still flows through GAAP earnings. Because Utility Innovation's purchase-price allocation is unavailable, the model uses an author sensitivity, not a fact: allocating 40%-60% of the $1.45 billion upfront price to finite-lived intangibles over 8-10 years produces $58.0-$108.75 million of annual pretax amortization. Year-one transaction-fee sensitivity of 1%-2% of $1.45 billion equals $14.5-$29.0 million. King has a $250 million all-cash author reserve, zero assumed incremental earnings and the stated falsifier. No repurchase benefit, new share-funded deal or financing from negative share growth is assumed.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: These are subjective joint probabilities, not empirical or publisher-supplied odds. Each QQQ state's pair exactly preserves the shared 0.20/0.55/0.25 marginal. In QQQ bear, 0.08 goes to resilient execution because backlog and service demand may cushion a downturn, versus 0.12 to a simultaneous capex, integration and valuation shock. In QQQ base, 0.20 goes to strong execution because current sales, profit and margin evidence is exceptional, but 0.35 goes to lag because the starting mid-50s GAAP P/E leaves little room for merely good growth. In QQQ bull, 0.08 goes to execution strong enough to clear an 18% QQQ hurdle and 0.17 to company lag because broad AI prosperity can still favor the diversified index while VRT's multiple compresses. Main-case deterministic arithmetic identifies bear/resilient, base/strong and bull/strong as strict wins; aggregate authored mass is 0.36. The computed conservative lower-start sensitivity preserves all three classifications and 0.36 mass. Reweighting is exact if any sales/margin/backlog/acquisition-funding/leverage/King trigger trips: transfer 0.08 bear/resilient to bear/lag, 0.20 base/strong to base/lag and 0.08 bull/strong to bull/lag, preserving benchmark marginals and reducing strict-win mass from 0.36 to 0.00.

Formula: $4.42*((1.12)/(1.01))^5*30 = $222.34469325016028 terminal price; CAGR = ($222.34469325016028/$246.49)^(1/5)-1 = -0.020407406760310387. forecasts.thesis: Veeva is the life-sciences industry-cloud leader with recurring subscriptions, deeply embedded regulated workflows, expanding R&D/Quality exposure and a large cash-funded balance sheet. The source case is not that AI revenue is already proven; it is that Vault CRM, Vault AI and Falcon can use Veeva's domain data, applications and compliance position to sustain low-to-high-teens revenue growth while GAAP margins remain strong. Starting valuation is demanding, so only the breakout paths beat a strong QQQ outcome.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: VEEV beats QQQ only if durable product expansion, Vault CRM migration and monetizable agentic workflows keep total revenue compounding near the high teens, GAAP operating margin reaches the mid-30s, dilution stays contained and the terminal multiple remains premium. A resilient Veeva path can beat a QQQ bear case; a 17% growth breakout can beat the QQQ base case; only a 20% category-creator path beats the QQQ bull case. Central execution at lower growth or with multiple compression loses to QQQ, preserving the benchmark opportunity cost.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply, do not merely observe, these pre-breach triggers using SEC/issuer quarterly reports: (1) if TTM total-revenue growth or subscription growth is below 10% for two consecutive reported quarters, cap remaining revenue CAGR at 8% and terminal P/E at 25x; latest Q2 growth was 18%/16%, so not breached. (2) If GAAP operating margin is below 25% for two consecutive quarters, use no more than 25% terminal operating margin; latest Q2 was 29.6%. (3) If diluted weighted-average shares grow above 2% YoY for two consecutive quarters, set forecast share growth to at least 2%; Q2 diluted shares fell to 165.057m from 167.685m. (4) Q2 disclosed one top-20 biopharma production deployment of Agentic Call Report. If by FY2028 Veeva has neither disclosed production AI deployment at at least three customers nor provided measurable AI-linked revenue, attach, or retention evidence, remove the 17%-20% AI breakout paths and reassign their mass to lag states. (5) A material security/privacy failure, failed Vault CRM migration causing disclosed customer losses, or funded debt above 1x TTM GAAP operating income forces a fresh model before use.
forecasts.nextAction: Independent Evidence & Risk review must inspect the 2026 10-K, 2026-07-31 10-Q, Q2 8-K exhibit, share authorization and GuruFocus payload; confirm the TTM revenue/share bridge, cash and investments, lease versus funded-debt classification, share ledger, Copli and Ostro acquisition terms, formula-derived scenario outputs, and whether any public post-Q2 event through 2026-10-07 changes the model. PM then decides ranking; Dustin retains final authority.
forecasts.theme: Core; AI-regime vertical applications, regulated data/workflows and governance
forecasts.limitations: The GuruFocus segment endpoint failed wrapper validation, although SEC product-area disclosures were retrieved. GuruFocus broad financial payloads were too large for inline inspection, so only fields surfaced by the tool and SEC corroboration are used. AI economics are not separately disclosed. Copli purchase consideration was not established from reviewed primary evidence; Q2 characterized Copli's financial impact as immaterial, but future acquisition cadence remains uncertain. The FY2027 non-GAAP outlook cannot be reconciled to GAAP because Veeva says SBC and other excluded items cannot be reasonably predicted; this model therefore uses GAAP margins and treats SBC as economic. Interest income is scenario-bounded as a percent of revenue rather than assuming today's cash yield persists. Scenario outputs are formula-derived estimates, not source facts or calibrated probabilities.

At 2026-07-31: 161.835m common shares outstanding; Q2 diluted weighted-average shares 165.057m; cash $1.812bn; short-term investments $5.431bn; no funded debt identified; operating lease liabilities $14.635m current plus $137.060m noncurrent; no preferred or NCI claim identified. The discretionary $2bn/two-year repurchase authorization had about $1.4bn remaining, but forecast share growth is 0% to +1%, not an assumed five-year buyback. Goodwill/intangibles and acquisition risk remain in GAAP margins.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: Joint probabilities are subjective, uncalibrated judgments, not translations of a legacy rank, score, hurdle or expected return. Each QQQ marginal is exact: bear 0.08+0.12=0.20; base 0.20+0.20+0.15=0.55; bull 0.17+0.08=0.25; total=1.00. The weights allow QQQ to win in Veeva disruption, base lag, base execution and bull lag paths. Veeva wins only in bear resilience, base breakout and bull category-creator paths. High cash and current execution support resilience; valuation, concentration, CRM migration and unproven AI monetization keep most mass out of breakout cases.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus identifies the quoted instrument as Mobileye Global Class A and supplied the $7.15 regular-session close at 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT. The Q2 2026 SEC filing identifies two operating segments: Mobileye is reportable and Moovit is within Other; Mentee Robotics is allocated to Mobileye. TTM consolidated GAAP revenue is $2,016m, operating loss is $4,175m, pretax loss is $4,116m and net loss is $4,062m; operating loss includes a $3,788m non-cash goodwill impairment in Q1 2026. Issuer Q3-2025/Q4-2025/Q1-2026/Q2-2026 adjusted operating income was $74m/$41m/$95m/$155m, totaling $365m; adjusted net income was $76m/$45m/$96m/$155m, totaling $372m; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.09/$0.06/$0.12/$0.19, totaling $0.46. Adjustments remove acquired-intangible amortization, SBC, goodwill impairment, acquisition expense and tax effects; Q2 also removes the R&D-law grant related to ordinary income from sold RSUs. Q2 customer concentration was 28%/16%/15%/14% and H1 was 27%/16%/16%/15%; China was $122m of Q2's $508m revenue. Mobileye purchases every EyeQ SoC from one supplier and describes substantial reliance on STMicroelectronics and Quanta. Mentee was a related-party acquisition: CEO Amnon Shashua was chairman, co-founder and a significant shareholder and received 37.83% of consideration, about $341m; CTO Shai Shalev-Shwartz was a co-founder and significant shareholder and received 13.07%, about $118m. Shashua's son and son-in-law were Mentee employees and received option consideration. Shashua recused himself; a four-member disinterested committee recommended the transaction, the Board approved it, and the Audit Committee approved it under the Related Persons Transaction Policy. MODEL INFERENCE: amortization and goodwill impairment are non-cash acquisition-accounting items, but SBC and Mentee retention consideration are recurring economic dilution, so scenarios do not treat adjusted EPS as distributable owner earnings and explicitly grow shares. The R&D-law benefit is only partly recurring because Q2 recognition covered H1. Concentration increases the chance that an OEM production change, ordering reset, China weakness or component constraint interrupts operating leverage. The Mentee conflict does not change disclosed cash/share arithmetic but weakens the capital-allocation prior and lowers Mentee-dependent breakout weight. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Mobileye beats QQQ only if higher-content Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur, Drive and robotaxi programs convert its installed base and nonbinding $24.5bn eight-year expected automotive pipeline into revenue growth and operating leverage; Mentee remains optionality, not required base revenue.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Mobileye starts from a depressed $7.15 price while retaining a scaled edge-AI platform: more than 258m vehicles had deployed its SoCs by 2026-06-27, it works with more than 50 OEMs, and it shipped 20.9m systems in H1 2026 versus 18.1m a year earlier. EyeQ volume growth, content per vehicle and production scaling of Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur and Drive could compound revenue faster than QQQ. Counter-thesis: four customers represented 73% of Q2 revenue and 74% of H1 revenue; China represented $122m of Q2 revenue; every EyeQ SoC came from one supplier; STMicroelectronics and Quanta are important dependencies; design wins are not purchase commitments; Q4-2025 revenue fell 9%; Q2-2026 revenue was approximately flat; high-content launches can slip; Intel controls voting power; and SBC/Mentee dilution can consume operating progress. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Spotify's 2025 Form 20-F identifies Luxembourg-incorporated Spotify Technology S.A., CIK 0001639920, and one NYSE-listed class of ordinary shares under SPOT. GuruFocus returned the 2026-10-07 16:00:02 EDT USD close of $512.92. The issuer's Q2 deck reports 777m MAUs, 300m Premium subscribers, EUR4,777m revenue, 33.4% gross margin, EUR655m operating income, EUR797m quarterly FCF and EUR3.3bn rounded LTM FCF. Its detailed LTM FCF reconciliation reports EUR3,337m operating cash flow, EUR(79)m capital expenditures, EUR3m change in restricted cash and EUR3,261m FCF. 2025 revenue was EUR17,186m, operating income EUR2,198m and FCF EUR2,874m. MODEL INFERENCE: Spotify can compound per-share FCF if subscriber/ARPU growth, ad automation and marketplace economics lift revenue and margins faster than cash taxes, working capital and product reinvestment. HUMAN JUDGMENT: a direct issuer-reported FCF-per-share framework is preferable to reported EPS because 2025-26 net income contains volatile Exchangeable Note fair-value finance effects, taxes and share-price-linked social charges. No normalization is claimed: the raw LTM FCF base is retained, with its working-capital, restricted-cash and cash-tax timing limitations handled through scenario growth, dilution and valuation bounds.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: Q2 reported 15% constant-currency revenue growth, 33.4% gross margin, 13.7% operating margin and EUR3.3bn rounded LTM FCF; management's prepared remarks describe 2030 objectives of mid-teens revenue growth, 35%-40% gross margin and operating margin above 20%, not guidance guaranteed to occur. MODEL INFERENCE: SPOT beats QQQ only if pricing, Premium subscriber growth, ad automation and newer products produce durable low/mid-teens FCF growth while the terminal FCF multiple remains at least in the mid-20s. HUMAN JUDGMENT/QQQ ALTERNATIVE: at $512.92 the valuation already discounts meaningful execution. QQQ is the better default if label/publisher bargaining power, platform competition, FX, regulation, taxes or reinvestment hold FCF growth near the bear path. The corrected joint scenarios put QQQ ahead in all SPOT-bear paths and in SPOT-base paired with QQQ base or bull; SPOT wins the base/QQQ-bear path and every bull path, for a subjective 31% beat probability.
forecasts.falsifier: PRE-BREACH OPERATING TRIGGER: starting with the next reported quarter after 2026-10-07, if Spotify reports BOTH constant-currency total-revenue growth below 8% and Premium-subscriber growth below 6% year over year in two consecutive quarterly shareholder decks, cap the underwriting at the 4% FCF-growth/18x bear path and rerun. PRE-BREACH CASH/MARGIN TRIGGER: if reported LTM FCF falls below EUR2.8bn or operating margin falls below 12% in two consecutive quarterly reports through 2028 while revenue remains positive, use the bear path until two consecutive quarters recover above both thresholds. FINANCING TRIGGER: if net debt excluding lease liabilities exceeds EUR2bn or net issued shares less treasury shares increase more than 3% year over year, rerun with at least 2% annual share growth and explicitly model the new claims. Sources are the issuer quarterly deck and SEC 6-K/20-F. These thresholds were not breached at Q2 2026: reported LTM FCF was EUR3.3bn rounded, operating margin 13.7%, constant-currency revenue growth 15%, subscriber growth 9%, and management said no debt other than leases.

Agi owns Banco Agibank and serves Brazilian retail borrowers, principally through payroll- and benefit-linked credit. At June 30, 2026, reviewed IFRS statements reported R$37.076bn gross loans and R$4.799bn equity. The management earnings release separately reported Agi Inc capital adequacy of 18.7%, expanded adequacy of 18.2%, and Tier I of 17.6%, explicitly incorporating IPO proceeds; the reviewed statements separately reported Banco Agibank PR/RWA of 13.89% and PR/(RWA+RBAN) of 13.52%. GuruFocus supplied USD5.80 June BVPS, 159.93m shares and the USD6.51 October 7 close. MODEL INFERENCE: A direct price-to-book model avoids capitalizing the abnormal 2Q tax benefit. Five-year USD value starts with USD5.80 BVPS, compounds retained book by scenario ROE, translates BRL to USD, explicitly dilutes for both registered S-8 pools, and applies terminal P/B. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the stock merits a QQQ-relative slot only if post-credit-cost ROE remains adequate and both holding-company and regulated-bank capital retain pre-breach cushions; Dustin must decide whether Brazil, INSS, funding, controller and dilution risks merit the assigned probabilities.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: Q2 loans grew 21.2% year over year, 88% of the portfolio was secured, INSS payroll share reached 9.6%, and Agi Inc management-reported capital adequacy was 18.7%. The October filing added R$2.1bn of 132-month FIDC funding at CDI plus 1.05%, backed by INSS payroll loans. June BVPS was USD5.80 versus the USD6.51 entry price. MODEL INFERENCE: if mid-teens ROE, high retention and controlled credit losses overcome BRL depreciation and the full gross S-8 capacity, book can compound faster than QQQ without assuming a large P/B re-rating. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the prospective edge is valuation plus book compounding, not persistence of 2025's 35.8% ROE or the 2026 tax benefit. QQQ is superior if risk-adjusted margin, bank capital, FX or dilution prevents USD BVPS compounding.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach capital tests from SEC-filed quarterly materials are entity-specific: suspend the positive thesis and re-underwrite before the next quarterly close if, in any quarter, (1) Agi Inc management-reported RE/RWA CAR is below 15.0% or RE/(RWA+RBAN) is below 14.5%, versus 18.7% and 18.2% at 2Q26 and a disclosed 10.5% CAR limit; or (2) Banco Agibank reviewed-statement PR/RWA is below 12.5% or PR/(RWA+RBAN) below 12.0%, versus 13.89% and 13.52%. If the applicable regulatory minimum changes, reset these tests to preserve at least a 200bp cushion. Also re-underwrite if NPL over 90 days exceeds 5.0%, LTM cost of risk exceeds 8.0%, LTM NIM after provisions falls below 5.0%, or institutional funding exceeds 70% with loans/deposits above 100%, in each case for two consecutive quarters. An INSS suspension over 30 days, a capital-restoration equity raise larger or more discounted than the bear formula, or verified material misconduct immediately voids the positive thesis.

forecasts.limitations: SOURCE COVERAGE: GuruFocus summary, annual and quarterly financials, key ratios and price were retrieved in the source pack; its segment endpoint failed schema validation and the public segment page was empty. Only 2023-2025 annual history was exposed, not 15 years, and AGBK began public trading in February 2026. SEC evidence supplies the 2025 20-F, F-1, 2Q26 reviewed statements and earnings release, October funding filing, and both S-8s. DILUTION: the April S-8 registered 9,775,805 Class A shares for the Omnibus Plan; the plan permits awards funded with authorized-unissued or treasury shares and lets the board adjust capacity. The September standalone Partnership Program reserves up to 7,100,000 Class A shares, may use new or treasury shares, and requires purchase at book net equity per share. Public filings available by the model date do not quantify grants, exercises, settlements, cancellations, treasury use, shares already included in the 159,930,070 basis, or economic overlap. The model therefore makes no unsupported reconciliation claim: every scenario adds both gross pools to the June base, assumes zero proceeds, and may double-count already issued or treasury-funded shares; this intentionally adverse treatment bounds known gross capacity. Bear also models a 10% capital raise at 0.70x contemporaneous pre-raise BVPS and credits the proceeds. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE: Arista couples a single EOS/NetDL software architecture with high-speed Ethernet platforms spanning AI, cloud, enterprise campus and routing. Q2-2026 revenue grew 37.7% YoY to $3.0357bn with 45.4% GAAP operating margin; TTM revenue was $10.5408bn and GuruFocus shows 24.1% 10-year per-share revenue growth and 33.5% EBIT growth. MODEL: open Ethernet can take share in AI scale-out and eventually scale-up while software/services and campus broaden the base. COUNTER-THESIS: the frozen $215.83 price is about 68x GAAP TTM EPS, two customers were 42% of FY2025 sales, Broadcom is the predominant silicon vendor, and $9.7bn of commitments leave little room for an AI digestion cycle. HUMAN JUDGMENT: quality is exceptional but valuation requires sustained growth; this is not portfolio approval.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: ANET beats QQQ only in the leader paths: revenue compounds 25%-27%, GAAP operating margin reaches 44%-45%, dilution stays below 0.7% annually and a 48x-55x terminal GAAP P/E remains defensible. Those assumptions require Ethernet to gain in AI fabrics, EOS/NetDL to preserve pricing and campus/services to diversify hyperscaler demand. QQQ is superior if revenue slows toward 20% or below, margins retreat, or the terminal multiple compresses toward 38x-40x; the model deliberately gives those lag paths most probability mass.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating falsifiers, observed from each subsequent 10-Q/10-K through 2031-10-07: (1) two consecutive quarters of YoY revenue growth below 15% (Q2-2026: 37.7%) removes all 20%+ growth paths and caps terminal P/E at 30x; (2) TTM GAAP operating margin below 38% for two consecutive quarter-ends (GuruFocus TTM: 43.14%) forces the downside margin/multiple; (3) any single customer above 35% of annual revenue (FY2025 max: 26%) plus annual growth below 15% forces concentration downside; (4) non-cancellable commitments above 100% of TTM revenue while inventory grows above 30% YoY and revenue below 15% (current commitments $9.7bn versus TTM revenue $10.5408bn; inventory condition not evidenced) forces the 8% growth/25x case. Sources: latest SEC 10-Q/10-K and GuruFocus ratios. Consequence is model reset, not an automatic trade.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Microsoft's FY2026 10-K reports revenue of $331,839m, operating income of $155,237m, other income net of $10,697m, pretax income of $165,934m, tax expense of $32,185m, net income of $133,749m, diluted EPS of $17.95, and 7,453m weighted-average diluted shares. Segment revenue/operating income was Productivity and Business Processes $139,996m/$83,879m, Intelligent Cloud $137,791m/$56,972m, and More Personal Computing $54,052m/$14,386m. Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 27% to $214.4b, Azure and other cloud services grew 41%, and commercial remaining performance obligation reached $678b. The filing also reports FY2026 interest and dividends income of $3,301m, total interest expense of $3,051m, finance-lease interest of $2,547m, finance-lease liabilities of $66,594m, finance-lease right-of-use assets added of $24,608m, cash additions to property and equipment of $115,948m, and $329.1b of additional primarily datacenter leases not yet commenced, expected to commence from FY2027 through FY2033 with terms of 1 to 20 years. REPORTED-TO-NORMALIZED BRIDGE: $331,839m revenue -> $155,237m operating income -> +$10,697m reported other income net -> $165,934m pretax -> -$32,185m tax -> $133,749m net income -> $17.95 diluted EPS on 7,453m diluted shares. Microsoft supplies FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.28 after removing $0.67 of OpenAI gains. Subtracting the separately disclosed aggregate Q4 $0.27 benefit produces only a provisional $17.01 reference because the release does not establish clean non-overlap or each component's after-tax contribution; $17.01 is not an input to any terminal expression. MODEL INFERENCE: Each terminal expression starts with FY2026 revenue and separately models operating income, ordinary-debt interest, existing finance-lease interest, incremental finance-lease interest tied to the disclosed uncommenced lease pipeline, tax, and diluted shares. Cash interest/dividend income, FX/other, and investment marks receive zero terminal credit. FY2026 ordinary-debt/other interest is provisionally inferred as $3,051m total interest expense less $2,547m finance-lease interest, or $504m; the subtraction and all outputs require independent verification. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Microsoft can beat QQQ if Azure/Copilot monetization converts backlog into low-teens revenue growth while software economics and datacenter utilization offset lease-funded infrastructure. The contrary case is that AI capacity commitments raise below-operating-line lease interest and depress margins faster than monetization, making diversified QQQ superior.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Microsoft has source-supported demand signals: FY2026 Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 27%, Azure and other cloud services grew 41%, and commercial RPO reached $678b, alongside broad productivity, cloud, developer, security, and consumer distribution. The counter-thesis is explicit: the Base capex-digestion and Bull index-catches-up cases let QQQ win when infrastructure returns lag or broader Nasdaq beneficiaries compound faster. Mechanical evaluation of the six authored joint states produces a 0.65 strict probability-to-beat from the 0.08, 0.12, 0.35, and 0.10 winning-state weights; that figure is a subjective research output, not a calibrated probability or portfolio approval.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply the Structural deceleration downside if either operating pre-breach trigger occurs: (1) Azure revenue growth is below 20% year over year in constant currency for two consecutive reported quarters, versus the FY2026 baseline of 41%; or (2) Microsoft Cloud gross margin is below 60% for two consecutive reported quarters while cash property-and-equipment additions plus finance-lease additions remain above 35% of revenue. FY2026 Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 66%, so trigger (2) was not breached, but its spending limb was already true: $115,948m cash additions plus $24,608m finance-lease additions equals $140,556m, or a model-computed 42.356685% of $331,839m revenue, subject to independent verification. A separate financing pre-breach trigger applies at the first reported 10-Q or 10-K showing any of: finance-lease liabilities at or above 25% of trailing revenue; annualized finance-lease interest at or above 1.0% of trailing revenue; or cash property-and-equipment additions plus finance-lease additions above 45% of trailing revenue for two consecutive reported quarters while Microsoft Cloud gross margin is below 63%. FY2026 model-computed baselines, requiring independent verification, were $66,594m/20.0682% for finance-lease liabilities/revenue, $2,547m/0.7675% for finance-lease interest/revenue, and 42.356685% for cash plus finance-lease additions/revenue. Consequence of either trigger: cap revenue CAGR at 8%, terminal operating margin at 42%, diluted-share growth at no less than 0.5%, and terminal P/E at 24x; give no cash-interest, FX, investment-mark, or buyback credit; set ordinary-debt and existing finance-lease interest no lower than their latest annualized disclosures; and calculate incremental lease interest as not-yet-commenced commitments multiplied by at least a 70% five-year activation share, 60% finance-lease classification share, and 5% imputed rate. Observation sources are subsequent earnings releases and 10-Q/10-K filings. These are author risk controls, not company guidance.

forecasts.limitations: GuruFocus summary, annual and quarterly financials, and key ratios were pulled. Its endpoint exposed FY2017-FY2026 plus TTM annual columns rather than 15 annual years, so no 15-year claim is made. GuruFocus segment retrieval failed response-schema validation; SEC XBRL segment figures are used instead. The 2026-10-07 close is GuruFocus's $529.76 price stamped 16:00 EDT and is corroborated by the dated summary/OHLC payload described in the source record. FY2026 is the latest reported annual/TTM period because no FY2027 quarter was public by the snapshot. The $17.01 reference is provisional and unused. The $329.1b pipeline is described as primarily datacenter leases, but the filing does not establish which future arrangements will be finance versus operating leases, exact commencement by fiscal year, or future imputed rates. Activation, finance-classification, and imputed-rate assumptions are Human judgment, not Source facts. Holding existing finance-lease interest at no less than FY2026's $2,547m while adding scenario pipeline interest is a conservative floor, not guidance. The model gives no terminal cash-interest/dividend income, FX/other, investment-mark, or buyback credit and does not claim those items will literally be zero. Dividends are omitted to match the shared price-only benchmark. Regulatory remedies, AI supply/power constraints, customer concentration, OpenAI dependence, cyber events, tax disputes, unknown acquisitions, and accounting reclassification remain material residual risks. The controller-supplied full-precision scenario outputs are populated; all model-computed ratios, expression outputs, strict wins, marginals, and the 0.65 probability-to-beat still require independent arithmetic and evidence review.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: The six joint probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated execution/QQQ judgments selected independently of old rankings. They total exactly 1: QQQ bear 0.08+0.12=0.20, QQQ base 0.20+0.35=0.55, and QQQ bull 0.15+0.10=0.25. Within Bear, resilient cloud receives more weight than structural deceleration because backlog and diversified distribution may remain durable. Within Base, durable AI conversion is judged more likely than a severe capex-digestion lag, while the latter remains material. Within Bull, a broad Nasdaq AI rally outrunning Microsoft is more likely than Microsoft sustaining the supercycle assumptions. Mechanical comparison shows MSFT strictly beats QQQ in four states with 0.65 aggregate weight and loses in two states with 0.35 aggregate weight; the result remains an uncalibrated author judgment, not investment approval.
