forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001404655, NYSE symbol HUBS, and common stock, $0.001 par. GuruFocus' 2026-10-07 16:04 EDT quote was $220.27. HubSpot had 306,446 customers at 2026-06-30; Q2 revenue was $911.740m, +20% reported and approximately 17.5% constant-currency in management commentary; subscription was 98% of H1 revenue. Q2 NRR was 102%, customer dollar retention was in the high 80s, and average subscription revenue per customer was $11,800. AI adoption was measurable but not separately monetized: more than 55% of Pro+ customers used agents or Breeze Assistant; monthly agentic actions exceeded 3x the start-of-year level; Data Agent had more than 16,000 activations, Prospecting Agent almost 17,000, Customer Agent more than 10,000, and Customer Agent resolved 72% of tickets without human escalation. SOURCE HISTORY: GuruFocus exposed 2017-2025 plus TTM, not 15 years; revenue per share rose from $10.199 in 2017 to $58.865 in 2025 and $65.42 TTM, while current three-year revenue and FCF growth were 17.8% and 39.4%. HubSpot's IPO was in 2014, so no 15-year public history is claimed. SOURCE REPORTED BRIDGE, USD millions: TTM revenue is 3131.266-1475.003+1792.735; TTM GAAP operating income is 7.379-(-52.096)+71.263; TTM GAAP net income is 45.911-(-25.051)+75.892; GuruFocus reports TTM diluted EPS of $2.825. Q2 GAAP operating income was $43.319m and net income $43.338m; nonoperating income was $6.248m, including $9.412m interest income, $(0.395)m interest expense, and $(2.769)m other expense. H1 tax expense was $12.969m on $88.861m pretax income; a full U.S. valuation allowance remained, so that tax rate is not durable. NORMALIZATION/OWNER-ECONOMICS BRIDGE: no adjusted EPS is used. The terminal model starts from reported revenue and applies a GAAP operating margin retaining recurring SBC, AI inference/hosting, acquired-intangible amortization, capitalized-software amortization, and ordinary acquisition/integration expense. Strict TTM owner FCF per share before acquisitions, in USD millions and million shares, is (760.717-325.932+421.580-53.165+29.370-35.074-130.624+65.857-74.292-528.153+257.668-244.227)/50: reported CFO less PP&E, capitalized software, and SBC, divided by FY2026 guided diluted shares. This deliberately does not add back SBC or assume buybacks. October's $65m-$75m restructuring cash charge is not normalized away. MODEL INFERENCE: CRM context, distribution, and agent adoption can sustain low/mid-teens revenue growth and expand GAAP margin, but Q2 buying friction, AI costs, and pricing changes make that unproven. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the six cases use a direct GAAP common-EPS bridge, not management's non-GAAP EPS, and QQQ remains the default pending independent Evidence & Risk and North Star PM review.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: HubSpot can beat QQQ if its installed CRM context converts AI trials and agents into durable paid credit or seat expansion while unified-suite adoption and internal AI productivity raise GAAP operating margin. The $220.27 price and GuruFocus 3.31x P/S and 14.26x reported P/FCF were far below prior expectations, so successful stabilization plus GAAP margin conversion can outweigh multiple normalization. This is unproven: Q2 constant-currency growth slowed to about 17.5%, NRR was only 102%, budget scrutiny lengthened sales cycles, and gross margin faced hosting, AI inference, and capitalized-software amortization pressure. QQQ is superior if AI commoditizes CRM, consumption pricing cannibalizes seats, inference costs offset productivity, customer growth or NRR weakens, or SBC-funded dilution persists. Scenario weights are subjective and uncalibrated; no legacy rank, score, hurdle, or expected IRR was translated into probability.
forecasts.falsifier: Operating trigger: if two consecutive reported quarters through 2028-09-30 show both constant-currency revenue growth below 12% and GAAP operating margin below 5%, versus Q2 2026 at about 17.5% and 4.8%, cap the central model at 8% revenue growth and 10% terminal GAAP margin and move at least 15 percentage points from central/upside to downside. Retention trigger: if company-reported NRR is 95% or lower for two consecutive quarters through 2028-09-30, versus 102% in Q2 2026, remove the 14%-19% growth paths unless paid AI usage independently offsets churn. Dilution trigger: if weighted diluted shares exceed 52.0m for two consecutive quarters before 2028-09-30, versus 50.615m in Q2 2026 and 50.0m FY2026 guidance, use at least 2% annual share growth and no buyback credit. Cost trigger: if GAAP subscription gross margin is below 78% for two consecutive quarters before 2028-09-30, versus about 83.7% in Q2 from $894.025m subscription revenue and $145.957m subscription cost, cap terminal GAAP operating margin at 12%. Sources are each quarterly 10-Q or earnings exhibit; consequences apply at the next refresh. None was evidenced as breached at the model date.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: The shared QQQ masses are preserved exactly: bear 0.12+0.08=0.20, base 0.25+0.30=0.55, bull 0.15+0.10=0.25; total=1.00. No historical rank or hurdle set the weights. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: monday.com is a USD-reporting Israeli foreign private issuer whose FY2025 Form 20-F cover identifies ordinary shares, no par value, traded on Nasdaq as MNDY; it is not an ADR. GuruFocus supplied FY2019-FY2025 annual history rather than 15 years; reported revenue rose from $78.1m in 2019 to $1,232.0m in 2025, and its segment endpoint failed schema validation. The SEC/issuer TTM revenue bridge through 2026-06-30 is $316.900m+$333.878m+$351.265m+$364.621m=$1,366.664m. Q2 revenue was $364.6m, up 22%; cRPO was $750m, up 27%; total NDR was 109%; AI-product ARR doubled sequentially and represented 17% of net-new ARR; Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 17%; Q3 revenue guidance was 16%-17% growth. At June 30 the issuer reported 42.274119m ordinary shares, 2.604847m unvested RSUs, and 1.150320m options with a $68.12 weighted-average exercise price. On August 5 it issued 0.196829m Foundation shares. Its Foundation policy permits up to 1% of outstanding ordinary shares annually, with only up to 1% aggregate carryover, as part of an up-to-10%-over-about-ten-years intention. The August-approved executive compensation policy permits a Co-CEO award up to 0.50% of issued shares for no-exercise-price awards or 1.0% for awards with an exercise price, subject to a $13.65m on-target value cap. The 2021 plan permits an annual reserve increase of up to 5% of prior year-end shares, though reserve capacity is not actual issuance. MODEL INFERENCE: seats-plus-credits AI pricing, enterprise expansion, and post-restructuring leverage may sustain double-digit revenue growth and expand normalized margins, while 109% NDR and the Q3 deceleration make that contested. SBC is economically recurring: the terminal denominator uses full-count outstanding awards and positive future issuance rather than treating non-GAAP add-backs as free. HUMAN JUDGMENT: scenario growth, margins, multiples, FCF margins, cash yields, acquisition uses, issuance rates, and joint probabilities are explicit author assumptions, not issuer guidance.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MNDY can beat QQQ from $83.51 if cRPO and enterprise cohorts support durable double-digit growth, paid AI credits become meaningful usage, restructuring converts roughly 89% gross margins into operating leverage, and dilution stays within the modeled 3%-6% combined annual future issuance envelope. QQQ is the better default if Q3's 16%-17% guide marks structural deceleration, NDR stays near 109% or lower, AI economics constrain margins, recurring equity issuance exceeds the explicit envelope, or management consumes the $1.073bn opening liquidity without proportional operating value. Exact controller evaluation shows four of six joint paths strictly beat paired QQQ returns, for a subjective aggregate beat probability of 0.60; the 0.10 bear/weak and 0.30 base/lag paths do not beat QQQ.
forecasts.falsifier: PRE-BREACH DEFINITIONS: baseline fully diluted units at 2026-08-06 equal 42.274119m June basic shares + 2.604847m unvested RSUs + 1.150320m options counted in full + 0.196829m executed Foundation shares + a conservative Co-CEO reserve equal to 1.0% of June basic shares. Period-end fully diluted units use the same full-count definition and add all later issued shares, unvested awards, announced-but-unissued awards, and Foundation commitments; no treasury offset is used. A single quarter triggers review; two consecutive reported quarters trigger mandatory re-underwrite. (1) If cRPO growth is below 15% AND total NDR below 105%, cap every revenue CAGR above 8% at 8%, move 0.10 probability from base/AI to base/lag and 0.05 each from bull/solid and bull/breakout to bear/weak, then recalculate. (2) If AI products are below 10% of net-new ARR, or a substantially comparable AI monetization metric is absent for two consecutive reports, replace base/AI inputs with 10% revenue CAGR, 18% margin, and 24x; bull/solid with 12%, 20%, and 26x; bull/breakout with 14%, 22%, and 30x; move 0.05 from each bull path to base/lag, then recalculate. (3) If non-GAAP operating margin excluding separately disclosed restructuring is below 12%, cap every terminal operating margin at 15% and multiple at 20x; move 0.10 from base/AI and 0.05 from each bull path to bear/weak, then recalculate. (4) If defined fully diluted units grow above 6% annualized for two consecutive quarter-ends absent acquisition-issued shares with separately disclosed acquired revenue, use at least the observed annualized employee issuance rate, move 0.05 from base/AI and 0.05 from bull/solid to base/lag, then recalculate. If multiple rules fire, perform a fresh six-path re-underwrite rather than stack reallocations mechanically.
forecasts.nextAction: Independent Evidence & Risk must verify the FY2025 20-F, Q2 2026 6-K Exhibits 99.1-99.3, July restructuring 6-K, August proxy/approval, 2021 plan, Foundation pledge and executed contribution; reproduce all six terminal prices/CAGRs; verify the 0.60 strict beat probability and exact 0.20/0.55/0.25 QQQ marginals; and confirm no post-Q2 debt, new repurchase authorization, or material acquisition before the snapshot. forecasts.limitations: Primary filing coverage is strong from FY2025 through Q2 2026, but GuruFocus exposed only seven annual periods and its segment call failed output-schema validation. The Co-CEO policy gives ceilings, not the final award form; the model uses the more conservative 1% full-count reserve although a no-price award is capped at 0.5% and on-target value at $13.65m. The Foundation pledge is an intention and annual ceiling, not a binding forecast; every path nevertheless uses the 1% annual maximum for five future years. The plan's 5% annual reserve increase is capacity, not issuance; bear and base-lag paths model 5% annual employee issuance plus 1% Foundation issuance, while stronger paths assume less employee issuance. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001443646 and NYSE-traded Class A common stock BAH. GuruFocus recorded the 2026-10-07 16:00:02 EDT close at $68.69 and TTM reported EPS of $6.368. The SEC-filed Q1 FY2027 release reported $2,800m revenue, $279m operating income and $198m net income versus $2,924m, $257m and $271m a year earlier; Q1 revenue fell 4.2%, but adjusted EBITDA rose 7.4%, adjusted margin reached 11.9%, backlog was $39bn, and book-to-bill was 1.5x. MODEL INFERENCE: national-security demand, cyber/AI products and a low starting earnings multiple can outweigh Civil weakness if consolidated revenue resumes growth and margins hold near or above the TTM level. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the valuation is attractive enough to underwrite nine joint outcomes, but post-quarter acquisition debt and the absence of disclosed AI-product economics keep QQQ as the default in weak and merely adequate execution paths.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: BAH can beat QQQ if national-security awards, AI-native cyber products and Ultra Mission Solutions restore mid-single-digit growth while operating margin reaches roughly 10.5%-12.5%. The starting price is only about eleven times GuruFocus TTM reported EPS, so even moderate terminal multiples can create strong price returns. The counter-thesis is that federal procurement/shutdown pressure, Civil contraction, labor constraints, acquisition integration and higher interest expense suppress EPS while QQQ compounds at 10%-18%. Vellox is a concrete product suite, but no AI revenue, ARR, bookings or customer KPI was disclosed; it is optionality, not a modeled standalone revenue stream.
forecasts.falsifier: At each quarterly filing, calculate rolling-four-quarter revenue growth and operating margin from SEC GAAP statements, and read company backlog/book-to-bill disclosures. Re-underwrite immediately and assign zero weight to paths above 4% revenue growth or 11% terminal margin if either (a) rolling-four-quarter revenue growth is <=-3% at two consecutive quarter-ends, (b) rolling-four-quarter GAAP operating margin is <9% at two consecutive quarter-ends, or (c) quarterly book-to-bill is <0.9x twice within four quarters. From debt filings, also calculate post-Ultra net debt/LTM adjusted EBITDA; if it exceeds 4.0x at two consecutive quarter-ends, remove all terminal multiples above 15x until leverage returns below 3.5x. These are pre-breach relative to Q1's 1.5x book-to-bill, 11.9% adjusted margin and disclosed 2.7x June leverage; the latter predates the August financing/acquisition and therefore is not used as the post-close baseline.
forecasts.nextAction: Independent Evidence & Risk review must reperform the scenario arithmetic, verify the TTM tax normalization, post-August debt/cash bridge, Ultra purchase accounting and contribution, backlog/book-to-bill definitions, and whether any later filing disclosed Vellox economics. The North Star PM then decides ranking for both Core and AI sleeves; no roster, sizing or trade action is authorized here.

forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: At 2026-06-30 BAH had $540m cash, $19m current debt and $3,917m noncurrent debt; 120.284257m Class A shares were outstanding and Q1 diluted weighted-average shares were 120.185147m. The prospectus showed as-adjusted debt of $4,422m and cash of $1,015m before the acquisition; the source-based post-close bridge is cash=(1015-720) and net debt=4422-(1015-720), both USDm, but no post-close balance sheet had yet been filed. No preferred stock or noncontrolling-interest claim was identified. REPORTED-TO-NORMALIZED TTM BRIDGE, USDm except per share: revenue=(11217+2800-2924); operating income=(1033+279-257); reported net income=(205+200+175+198); pretax income=((205+21)+(200-13)+(175+58)+(198+53)); normalized net income=pretax*(1-0.215), using the midpoint of management's 20%-23% FY2027 tax guide. Normalized EPS=normalized net income/120.185147. forecasts.probabilityRationale: The nine probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated; none comes from a legacy score, hurdle, rank or target return. QQQ wins in the BAH fiscal-shock, execution-miss, index-outruns and solid-but-lag paths. All formulas use USD millions for revenue, operating income and interest, 120.185147 million diluted shares, no preferred/NCI deduction, zero assumed net share shrinkage, and terminal GAAP EPS times a P/E multiple. Interest scalars are author estimates that explicitly reflect the August debt refinancing and varying deleveraging; tax, margin, growth and multiple scalars are author assumptions, not source forecasts.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: AppFolio's 2026 Q2 10-Q identifies the Nasdaq-traded security as Class A common stock, reports Q2 revenue of $281.124 million (up 19% year over year), 9.6 million property-management units (up 8%), 22,751 property-management customers, and GAAP operating income of $52.977 million (18.8% margin). Value Added Services were $219.467 million of Q2 revenue versus $59.800 million of subscription revenue, so payments, screening, and risk-mitigation usage—not subscriptions alone—drives the model. The filing reports $217.401 million cash, no revolver borrowings, H1 operating cash flow of $121.902 million, and only $0.228 million H1 PP&E purchases; GuruFocus's source-provided TTM diluted EPS is $4.387. Model inference: start with $4.387 of TTM diluted EPS and model five-year net-income growth divided by explicit diluted-share growth, then apply a terminal P/E; this direct per-share framework avoids an irrelevant EV bridge but does not treat current net cash as incremental terminal value. Human judgment: durable system-of-record workflows, higher-value transaction adoption, and operating leverage can support mid-teens-or-better net-income growth, while payments concentration, regulation, AI competition, and multiple compression warrant severe lag cases.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: APPF can beat QQQ if unit growth plus deeper Value Added Services adoption sustains roughly 20% net-income growth in the central execution-win case while diluted-share growth stays near 0.5% and the terminal market still awards 35x earnings. Q2 2026 revenue grew 19%, units 8%, and GAAP operating income 31%, providing operating evidence for that path; however, the stock starts from a premium earnings multiple and QQQ is the better alternative whenever growth fades toward high single digits, dilution rises, or the terminal multiple falls into the mid-20s. The scenario weights are fresh subjective judgments, not calibrated frequencies or translations of any legacy score.
forecasts.falsifier: At each quarterly filing, test: (1) property-management units grow below 6% year over year for two consecutive quarters, or Value Added Services revenue grows below 12% year over year for two consecutive quarters—then remove the 20% central net-income-growth assumption and shift the base execution-win weight to the lag case; (2) GAAP operating margin is below 15% while revenue growth is below 15% for two consecutive quarters—then cap the central terminal multiple at 27x and re-underwrite; (3) diluted weighted-average shares grow above 2% year over year for two consecutive quarters absent a disclosed acquisition—then use at least 2% annual share growth in every case and recalculate; (4) a material payment-processor loss, adverse payments/tenant-screening regulation, or disclosed material cyber/chargeback loss occurs—then suspend the win cases pending quantified economics. Sources are the next two APPF 10-Q/10-K filings, especially revenue disaggregation, units, operating margin, EPS/share data, SBC, and repurchase notes. Consequence in every trigger is a full probability and valuation refresh, not an automatic trade.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies SPS Commerce, Inc., CIK 0001092699, one Nasdaq-listed common share under SPSC. The GuruFocus 2026-10-07 historical-price payload returned $81, although its MCP wrapper raised a list-versus-dictionary structured-content error; that failure remains part of provenance. FY2025 revenue was $751.505m; H1-2026/H1-2025 revenue was $389.936m/$368.949m, so reported TTM revenue is $772.492m. SPS sold its 3P Revenue Recovery business on 2026-06-30. The issuer says FY2026 guidance incorporates an approximately $10.5m reduction to H2 revenue and that the sale should be neutral to H2 adjusted EBITDA. The model therefore removes twice that explicitly quantified half-year amount from reported TTM revenue: $772.492m - 2 x $10.5m = a $751.492m continuing-revenue proxy. This is a transparent sensitivity, not a claim that $21m is the exact divested TTM revenue. Q2 revenue was $197.815m, GAAP operating income was $8.413m, and the separately disclosed 3P sale loss was $23.454m. The starting normalized operating bridge is therefore ($8.413m + $23.454m) / $197.815m = 16.109496246492935%. Its consistent quarterly after-tax per-share bridge is ($8.413m + $23.454m) x (1-24%) / 36.577m Q2 diluted shares = $0.6621352215873364. This definition excludes only the separately identified sale loss; it retains recurring SBC, acquired-intangible amortization, depreciation, and all ordinary operating costs. H1 SBC was $36.769m and unrecognized SBC was $115.2m over a 2.7-year weighted-average recognition period. Before repurchases, disclosed H1 share activity added 340,825 shares from awards/ESPP net of withholding, equal to 0.9084490465836252% of the 2025 year-end count in six months; H1 repurchases used $98.358m. MODEL INFERENCE: every scenario begins from the $751.492m proxy and 36.000174m July shares. Terminal price = [$751.492m x (1+revenue growth)^5 x terminal normalized operating margin x (1-24% tax)] / [36.000174m x (1+annual share growth)^5] x terminal P/E. Price CAGR = (terminal price / $81)^(1/5)-1. Because the margin retains SBC and all amortization and annual shares grow 1.8%-2.0%, no repurchase cash or SBC add-back is double-counted. Cash is deliberately omitted from terminal equity value, so no terminal-cash benefit funds repurchases. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the $751.492m proxy is the least-assertive bridge available from the issuer's quantified guidance; 1.8%-2.0% annual share growth is anchored to the disclosed six-month pre-repurchase issuance pace rather than net shares after cash-funded repurchases. Network effects, 96% recurring revenue, low concentration, and operating leverage could expand the sale-loss-normalized 16.1% Q2 operating margin, but the required 26%-29% execution margins in winning base/bull paths are demanding because they continue to charge SBC and amortization.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SPSC strictly beats QQQ in this authored distribution only in the QQQ-bear/resilient, QQQ-base/central, and QQQ-bull/upside paths, totaling 57%. The central case beats QQQ only narrowly: 10.308337205582441% versus 10%, so small deterioration in growth, dilution, margin, or multiple makes QQQ superior. The credible counter-thesis is that post-divestiture growth remains low single digit, short-cancel contracts or competition weaken retention, MAX/AI spending does not restore growth, acquisitions keep amortization and SBC elevated, gross equity issuance exceeds the modeled range, or valuation normalizes. Stress, base-lag, and bull-lag explicitly select QQQ as the better alternative. The 57% is subjective and uncalibrated, not investment approval.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if issuer-reported revenue growth, adjusted only for a separately quantified divestiture comparison, is <=2% y/y for two consecutive quarters, or if (GAAP operating income plus only separately quantified one-time disposal losses) / revenue is <=15% for two consecutive quarters, move all growth/margin assumptions to stress or base-lag until two subsequent quarters cure the breach. Pre-breach equity-economics trigger: if trailing-twelve-month pre-repurchase share issuance from awards and ESPP net of withholding exceeds 2.25% of the beginning share count, or SBC is >=10% of revenue for two consecutive quarters, use at least 2.5% annual share growth and cap terminal P/E at 20x until two subsequent quarters cure the breach; repurchases cannot cure this metric. Pre-breach capital trigger: if quarter-end cash less disclosed interest-bearing current/noncurrent borrowings becomes negative, or gross interest-bearing borrowing exceeds $250m, without a separately disclosed acquisition bridge covering first-year revenue, interest, tax, shares, and financing, remove all upside paths and default to QQQ. June 2026 cash was $173.167m and the filing presented no interest-bearing borrowing line; leases remain tracked separately. These are monitoring triggers, not evidence that a breach has occurred.
forecasts.nextAction: At the next filing, replace the $751.492m proxy with an issuer-disclosed exact continuing-operations revenue bridge if one becomes available; update reported revenue growth, the sale-loss-normalized operating margin under the unchanged SBC-and-amortization-inclusive definition, cash, interest-bearing borrowings, leases, diluted shares, pre-repurchase award/ESPP issuance, SBC/revenue, and repurchase cash. Evidence & Risk must reproduce the six formulas, confirm strict inequalities and the 57% aggregate, and challenge the 26%-29% terminal margins. North Star PM must decide whether a narrowly positive base-case spread and subjective 57% strict-beat weight justify inclusion versus simply owning QQQ.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: GuruFocus reports a USD53.49 consolidated regular-session close at 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT and TTM EPS of USD3.638 for the ADR. Tencent's 2026 interim report reports first-half revenue of RMB401.243 billion (+10% year over year), IFRS profit attributable to equity holders of RMB114.115 billion (+10%), diluted IFRS EPS of RMB12.417 (+12%), and Q2 gross margin of 58%. Q2 segment revenue growth was 8% for VAS, 22% for Marketing Services, and 9% for FinTech and Business Services. Model inference: Tencent can compound USD-translated attributable earnings through games, AI-improved ads, cloud and payments while repurchases partly offset awards/options, but elevated AI investment, China policy and currency/ADR risk warrant wide growth and terminal-P/E ranges. The model is direct source-provided TTM-EPS/P-E, not EV-derived; it therefore does not add investee value or net cash separately.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Tencent begins at about 14.7 times the source-provided USD3.638 TTM EPS versus the USD53.49 ADR price, while issuer evidence shows double-digit first-half revenue/profit growth, 22% Q2 Marketing Services growth, gross-margin expansion and ongoing repurchases. If AI-enhanced advertising, internally developed games and cloud sustain low-double-digit USD-translated attributable-profit growth and the diluted share base contracts, a mid-teens terminal P/E can produce price growth above the shared QQQ base case. QQQ remains the better default if AI capex suppresses cash conversion, China regulation/geopolitics or RMB depreciation imposes a lasting discount, or Tencent's earnings growth falls to mid-single digits while QQQ compounds at 10%-18%.
forecasts.falsifier: At each Tencent quarterly/interim/annual release, test: (1) if consolidated revenue growth is below 5% and non-IFRS operating margin is below 32% for two consecutive quarters, move base-case mass toward execution-lag and reduce operating-growth assumptions; (2) if both Marketing Services growth is below 10% and Domestic Games growth is below 5% for two consecutive quarters, remove the low-double-digit base growth premise; (3) if reported diluted weighted-average shares grow more than 2% year over year for two consecutive quarters despite repurchases, replace nonpositive share-count-growth assumptions with at least +2% and recalculate; (4) if period-end net cash is below zero or reported free cash flow remains negative for two consecutive half-years while capex exceeds 25% of revenue, reduce terminal multiples and reassess financing risk; and (5) any ADR ratio change, inability to convert/cancel the DR, trading restriction, sanctions exposure that impairs holders, or loss of reliable USD price evidence makes the row unrankable pending security reconciliation. Consequence: any one security/tradability event is an immediate hard gap; either operating pair triggers a re-underwrite rather than automatic removal.
forecasts.nextAction: The six outcomes already use the controller's full-precision deterministic results. Evidence & Risk must independently verify the USD53.49 close, GuruFocus USD3.638 TTM EPS translation against issuer RMB diluted EPS and applicable FX, the ADR ISIN and 1:1 terms across holder-relevant depositaries, current issued shares and the diluted option/award basis, debt/net cash, formula arithmetic and strict QQQ comparisons. forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Meta's 2026 Q2 filing identifies Nasdaq-traded Class A common stock as META and reports $60.801bn quarterly revenue (+28% year over year), 3.60bn Family daily active people (+3%), ad impressions +14%, average price per ad +12%, and Family of Apps operating income of $23.394bn, offset by a $4.619bn Reality Labs operating loss. The filing reports $6.18 diluted Q2 EPS; GuruFocus reports $26.548 TTM diluted GAAP EPS at the 2026-10-07 close. Primary-source normalization facts: Meta's Q3 2025 results say a one-time $15.93bn non-cash tax charge reduced diluted EPS by $6.20; Q1 2026 results say an $8.03bn tax benefit, which partially offset that charge, increased diluted EPS by $3.13; Q2 2026 results include $2.40bn of legal charges and $1.18bn of severance expense. Model inference: recommendation and advertising AI can sustain low-double-digit operating-earnings growth, but the $130bn-$145bn 2026 capex program, Reality Labs losses, no H1 2026 share repurchases, and very large disclosed infrastructure commitments make conversion to per-share value uncertain. Human judgment: the direct framework starts from reported TTM diluted GAAP EPS of 26.548. The normalization pressure test is starting EPS = 26.548 + 6.20 - 3.13 + 0.00 legal adjustment + 0.00 severance adjustment. The two issuer-quantified per-share tax effects are reversed in opposite directions. Legal and severance charges remain fully in the normalized denominator because the issuer did not publish item-specific after-tax per-share effects, legal exposure remains active, restructuring may recur, and assuming deductibility or nonrecurrence would be unsupported. No tax shield is imputed to either retained item.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Source facts: Q2 advertising volume and pricing both grew double digits while Family of Apps remained highly profitable, giving Meta a company-specific AI monetization path rather than only broad AI beta. Model inference: META beats QQQ only if net income compounds materially faster than the index while net share count becomes flat-to-down and the terminal P/E remains at least in the low-to-mid 20s despite the infrastructure obligation load. Counter-thesis and QQQ alternative: QQQ is preferable if Meta's infrastructure and Reality Labs spending absorb owner cash, regulation weakens targeting, SBC drives dilution, or the stock's reported-EPS valuation compresses; QQQ then diversifies AI upside across semiconductors, software, cloud and other platforms instead of relying on one ad-funded capital program. The normalized sensitivity removes only the issuer-quantified one-time Q3 tax charge and offsetting Q1 tax benefit; it is not used to erase legal or severance costs. Scenario weights are subjective conditional judgments, not calibrated frequencies or publisher targets.

This is a pre-breach capital-risk trigger and does not require a liquidity default. These are forecast consequences, not trade instructions.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies CIK 0001653482 and Nasdaq-traded Class A common stock GTLB. GuruFocus recorded the October 7, 2026 16:00 EDT close at $51.99. GitLab reported FY2026 revenue of $955.224m, 26% growth, 87% gross margin, $232.856m operating cash flow, a $70.481m GAAP operating loss and $55.956m attributable net loss. Latest H1 FY2027 revenue was $550.412m, up 22%; Q2 revenue was $286.254m, up 21%, with 84% GAAP gross margin, negative 20% GAAP operating margin, 15% non-GAAP operating margin, $42.1m non-GAAP net income and negative $36.844m GAAP attributable net income. Base customers rose 8% to 11,114, $100k-plus ARR customers rose 17% to 1,571, and dollar-based net retention was 117% versus 121%. FY2027 guidance was $1.129b-$1.133b revenue, $148m-$152m non-GAAP operating income and $0.85-$0.87 non-GAAP diluted EPS on about 172m diluted shares. MODEL INFERENCE: unified code, security, deployment, governance and audit context can make GitLab an enterprise control plane for heterogeneous software agents; seat add-ons plus usage credits create two monetization paths. HUMAN JUDGMENT: from $51.99, outperformance requires sustained high-teens-plus revenue growth and conversion to GAAP margins that absorb recurring SBC, not merely adjusted-profit growth.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: GitLab can beat QQQ if agentic software creation increases lifecycle throughput and governance demand, Duo/Flex/credits expand wallet share, and a unified DevSecOps platform consolidates point tools. The model's beating paths require 20%-27% five-year revenue CAGR, 26%-32% terminal GAAP operating margin including SBC, only 1%-1.5% annual diluted-share growth, and 32x-40x terminal earnings. Those are author assumptions, not company guidance. QQQ is superior if model vendors or hyperscalers own the interface, AI coding reduces paid seat economics, usage revenue carries lower gross margin, net retention fades, or SBC/share issuance prevents per-share conversion.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating falsifier: if reported dollar-based net retention is below 108% for two consecutive quarterly disclosures, or reported revenue growth is below 14% for two consecutive quarters while non-GAAP operating margin is below 12%, move all base-execution/breakout mass to lag/downside and refresh the model; the July 31, 2026 baselines were 117%, 21% Q2 revenue growth and 15% Q2 non-GAAP operating margin. Capital falsifier: if weighted-average diluted shares exceed 180m in any four-quarter window without a disclosed funded repurchase bridge, raise modeled share growth to the observed pace. Sources are the latest 10-Q and Q2 FY2027 earnings exhibit; these thresholds and consequences are author judgment and were not breached at the model date.
forecasts.nextAction: Independent Evidence & Risk review must verify the SEC TTM bridge, Q2 non-GAAP reconciliation, 172m diluted-share baseline, no-debt claim, 50m preferred-share authorization with none issued, repurchase/SBC cash bridge, and that terminal GAAP margins include recurring SBC. The controller has mechanically evaluated the disclosed formulas; the reviewer must independently reproduce them. forecasts.whyBeatQqq: AVGO can beat QQQ if custom XPU and Ethernet content plus VMware/private-cloud cash flow sustain mid-teens or better revenue growth, high-40s-or-better GAAP operating margins, controlled dilution and deleveraging. Exact outputs classify the resilient QQQ-bear outcome, AI-platform QQQ-base outcome and AI-supercycle QQQ-bull outcome as strict AVGO wins, totaling 0.48 probability. QQQ remains the better default when AI spending or customer financing breaks, hyperscalers insource, XPV claims consume capital, a funded acquisition resets debt/share economics, recurring SBC or amortization suppresses GAAP earnings, or AVGO's terminal multiple compresses faster than per-share earnings grow.
forecasts.falsifier: Test at every quarterly filing. Downside pre-breach triggers: (1) consolidated y/y revenue growth below 15% and AI semiconductor growth below 25% for two consecutive quarters; (2) trailing-four-quarter GAAP operating margin below 35% for two quarters while retaining SBC and acquisition amortization; (3) diluted weighted-average shares growing above 2% y/y for two quarters; or (4) gross debt above $70bn, any recognized XPV liability or cumulative XPV cash payment above $2bn, or any announced acquisition/funded issuance above $5bn. Any financing or acquisition trigger immediately suspends the stale model and requires rebuilt debt, cash, average rate, interest, shares, tax and terminal valuation before retaining probabilities. Upside re-underwrite trigger: two consecutive quarters with consolidated growth at least 30%, AI semiconductor growth at least 75%, trailing GAAP operating margin at least 50%, diluted-share growth no more than 0.5% and gross debt no more than $55bn. Meeting all upside thresholds forces a fresh scenario/debt/share bridge and recomputation of strict QQQ-beat probability rather than leaving upside mass capped by this draft.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus identifies GFS as GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. and supplied the frozen $48.07 regular-session close. Its accessible annual history is FY2019-FY2025, only seven years, not 15; quarterly history was also retrieved. FY2025 issuer results were revenue $6,791m, reported operating profit $797m, net income $888m and diluted EPS $1.59; management non-IFRS values were operating profit $1,066m, net income $965m and EPS $1.72. Q1/Q2 2025 reported revenue was $1,585m/$1,688m, operating profit $151m/$196m, net income $211m/$228m and EPS $0.38/$0.41; non-IFRS operating profit was $213m/$258m, net income $189m/$234m and EPS $0.34/$0.42. Q1/Q2 2026 reported revenue was $1,634m/$1,786m, operating profit $180m/$174m, net income $104m/$167m and EPS $0.18/$0.30; non-IFRS operating profit was $271m/$298m, net income $227m/$256m and EPS $0.40/$0.46. MODEL INFERENCE: the TTM bridge is FY2025-Q1'25-Q2'25+Q1'26+Q2'26: reported revenue 6791-1585-1688+1634+1786=6938; reported operating profit 797-151-196+180+174=804; reported net income 888-211-228+104+167=720; reported EPS 1.59-0.38-0.41+0.18+0.30=1.28, corroborating GuruFocus TTM EPS 1.281. Management-adjusted TTM operating profit is 1066-213-258+271+298=1164, net income 965-189-234+227+256=1025 and EPS 1.72-0.34-0.42+0.40+0.46=1.82. I do not use the $1.82 as normalized economic EPS: SBC is recurring and dilutive, and acquisition amortization, integration and structural-optimization costs may recur as GF expands. The terminal model therefore starts from the $6,938m reported TTM revenue bridge and uses IFRS operating margins that retain SBC, then explicitly applies net finance/other, tax, NCI, diluted-share growth and a P/E. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the opportunity is specialty foundry mix and utilization improvement, with silicon photonics/SiGe for AI optical networking, power delivery and technology-services/IP raising growth and margin; it is not a leading-edge GPU thesis.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: GFS can beat QQQ only if specialty demand changes its low-growth earnings profile: Q2 2026 revenue rose 6% YoY, non-IFRS operating margin reached 16.7%, and management highlighted optical networking in AI data centers. Q2 cash generation and $3.3b cash/marketable securities support investment, while the June ARC acquisition and July Photeon IVR acquisition broaden Physical-AI and data-center power offerings. The high cases require sustained 10%-14% revenue growth, 20%-22% IFRS operating margin and 27x-30x terminal P/E; these are author assumptions, not guidance. QQQ remains superior if handset/cycle weakness, utilization, China capacity, tariffs, grants, customer concentration, integration, recurring SBC or financial-reporting control weaknesses constrain GFS to 5%-6% growth and 14%-17% margins. Because the starting stock multiple embeds a recovery while reported TTM EPS is only about $1.28, plausible lag states are intentionally material.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger, observed in issuer quarterly 6-K earnings releases after the 2026-10-07 snapshot: move the working model to the slow/downcycle set (revenue CAGR no more than 5%, terminal IFRS operating margin no more than 14%, multiple no more than 18x) if either (a) Communications Infrastructure & Datacenter revenue growth is below 20% YoY in any of Q3 2026 or Q4 2026, versus the issuer's Q2 filing showing 62% YoY growth, or (b) IFRS operating margin is below 9% for two consecutive quarters; Q1/Q2 2026 were 11.0%/9.7%, so this was not breached at the model date. Legal-share trigger: at each SEC-filed quarter/annual period end or later dated prospectus share-capital disclosure, measure only ordinary shares legally issued and outstanding; exclude diluted weighted-average EPS shares, outstanding awards, plan reserves and registered-but-unissued shares. If that legal count exceeds 570,000,000, use at least 2% annual diluted-share growth and no buyback offset in every scenario at the next model refresh. The latest disclosed legal count was 557,418,603 at 2026-09-11, so this trigger was not breached at the model date. Debt trigger: at each filed period end, define debt solely as the statement-of-financial-position line items current borrowings plus non-current borrowings, excluding lease liabilities. If that sum exceeds $2.0b, set terminal net finance/other to no better than -$100m in every scenario at the next refresh and retain that penalty until a later filed period-end sum is at or below $2.0b; there is no acquisition-asset offset. Reporting-quality trigger: if the FY2026 auditor again gives an adverse ICFR opinion, or GF announces a financial-statement restatement before then, set the QQQ-base slow-execution probability to 0.35 and the QQQ-base mix-and-margin-execution probability to 0.20 at the next refresh, preserving the 0.55 QQQ-base marginal. These thresholds and consequences are author judgments; the cited SEC filings are the measurement sources.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Amazon's Q2 2026 10-Q identifies the traded security as AMZN common stock, reports 10.7863 billion shares outstanding on July 22, 2026, and shows Q2 net sales of $200.606 billion, operating income of $27.461 billion, and diluted shares of 10.903 billion. The model assigns beat outcomes to a resilient QQQ-bear path, the strong QQQ-base execution path, and the exceptional QQQ-bull path; the subjective joint mass is 0.43. It deliberately lets QQQ win when revenue remains strong but margin, financing cost or terminal valuation disappoint, including a credible strong-company/strong-index lag state.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if reported consolidated net-sales growth is below 8% year over year AND operating margin is below 10% in each of two consecutive quarters, move all strong/exceptional execution mass to lag/impaired paths until two quarters recover; Q2 2026 was $200.606B versus $167.702B and $27.461B operating income, so this conjunction was not breached at model date. Pre-breach financing trigger: if reported long-term debt exceeds $200B while trailing operating income is below $100B for two consecutive quarters, cap terminal P/E at 20 and use at least $10B terminal net interest; June 30 debt was $128.894B before the documented July $24.867B net USD and September £4.235B net sterling offerings, so the $200B threshold was not evidenced as breached. Dilution trigger: if quarterly diluted weighted-average shares rise more than 2% year over year for two quarters, use at least 2% annual share growth in every path; Q2 was 10.903B versus 10.806B. forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Credo's FY2026 10-K identifies Nasdaq-traded ordinary shares (not an ADR), describes copper and optical interconnect products spanning AECs, retimers, DSPs, chiplets and IP, and reports FY2026 revenue of $1.335 billion, GAAP net income of $472.279 million and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.51. The filing says the top ten customers represented about 90% of revenue and end-customer B, D and E represented 32%, 33% and 19%, respectively. The Q1 FY2027 10-Q reports $479.003 million revenue, 64.5% GAAP gross margin, $129.425 million GAAP net income and $0.67 GAAP diluted EPS; the issuer's Q1 results release guided Q2 revenue to $525-$535 million. Model inference: the direct per-share framework starts with FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.51 and values five-year terminal GAAP EPS after explicit net-income growth and diluted-share growth at a scenario P/E. The thesis requires Credo's low-power connectivity content to expand with AI cluster density while new optical products broaden the revenue base. Human judgment: the terminal multiples and outcome probabilities are subjective research assumptions, not issuer guidance or calibrated probabilities.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Credo beats QQQ only if unusually strong per-share earnings growth outruns dilution and offsets substantial valuation compression. The base execution-win case requires 32% annual net-income growth, 2% annual diluted-share growth and a 45x terminal P/E from $2.51 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS. The QQQ alternative is preferable if customer concentration, optical integration or competition reduces net-income growth to the 16% base-lag assumption while dilution reaches 4% and the terminal P/E contracts to 35x. Source facts support exceptional recent growth but do not establish its durability: Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 114.7% year over year, while FY2026 top-ten customer concentration was about 90%. This is price-only research, not a portfolio or trade instruction.
forecasts.falsifier: Review each 10-Q and 10-K through FY2029. Metric/threshold/window/source/consequence: (1) if year-over-year revenue growth is below 25% for two consecutive quarters, move probability from each execution-win branch to its paired lag branch and recompute; (2) if GAAP gross margin is below 60% for two consecutive quarters, cap the terminal P/E at 30x pending a new model; (3) if basic ordinary shares exceed 210 million by the FY2028 year end or quarterly diluted weighted-average shares exceed 225 million, replace all share-growth assumptions with the observed higher rate; (4) if rolling-four-quarter GAAP diluted EPS growth is below 20% in two consecutive reports, treat QQQ as the preferred default until re-underwritten; and (5) if top-ten customer concentration remains at least 80% in FY2028 and any disclosed at-least-10% end customer's annual revenue share falls by at least 20 percentage points year over year, mark the row temporarily unrankable. Use the issuer's quarterly and annual filings for revenue, margin, EPS, shares and customer concentration.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: These are fresh subjective conditional weights, not empirical or legacy-score translations. The bear state places most mass on execution lag because a $220.01 starting price against $2.51 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS leaves little tolerance for customer loss or multiple compression; only the smaller bear-win branch assumes sufficient earnings growth to offset contraction. The base state is also tilted to lag because FY2026 top-ten concentration was about 90%, Q1 SBC was large relative to GAAP income, and DustPhotonics introduces integration and contingent-share risk, despite reported Q1 revenue growth of 114.7% and Q2 revenue guidance of $525-$535 million. The bull state tilts to execution win because broad AI infrastructure spending, AEC and IC ramps and the issuer's greater-than-$500 million FY2027 optical-revenue expectation could create sustained operating leverage. The paired weights exactly reproduce the required QQQ marginals: 0.04+0.16 for bear, 0.24+0.31 for base, and 0.15+0.10 for bull. Using the supplied deterministic outputs, the strict-beat branches are bear/execution wins, base/execution wins and bull/execution wins, for a subjective 0.43 total probability of beating QQQ.

MODEL INFERENCE: use $4.40 normalized forward diluted EPS/share, the $1.10 Q3 midpoint annualized, rather than raw TTM GAAP EPS. This is a run-rate convention, not issuer FY guidance, and it is generous because SBC is recurring. Five-year outcomes grow total normalized earnings 10%-50% annually, separately apply 2%-3% annual diluted-share growth, then apply 24x-38x terminal P/E. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Marvell can beat QQQ only if AI custom silicon, optics, switching and scale-up connectivity sustain unusually high earnings growth; the price already requires substantial execution. Counter-thesis: hyperscaler concentration, discretionary Google purchase milestones, TSMC/supply dependence, integration risk and recurring excluded costs produce slower growth and multiple compression, making diversified QQQ the superior default.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MODEL INFERENCE: MRVL has more operating leverage to AI infrastructure than QQQ if data-center revenue remains broad across electro-optics, switching, storage and custom silicon and if current growth converts to normalized earnings faster than diluted shares rise. The base-execution and exceptional paths require 40% and 50% annual total normalized-earnings growth, respectively, while diluted shares grow 2.5%-3%; they do not assume buybacks. QQQ wins in the demand-setback, base-deceleration and bull-valuation-reset paths because MRVL's $284.68 starting price and adjusted-EPS exclusions leave little margin for merely good execution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: upside is concentrated, not QQQ-like; accepting this as a core candidate requires belief that Marvell's customer programs are durable enough to offset single-customer, dilution and valuation risk.

On 2026-08-18 Marvell issued Google a warrant for up to 58,970,907 common shares at $206.58 through 2033: 1,360,867 time-vest over one year and the balance vests in 240 equal tranches, one per $500M of discretionary Custom Products revenue through FY2033. At 2026-08-01 cash was $3.9328B and noncurrent debt $4.9629B. Six-month SBC was $533.8M and repurchases $400M; acquisitions of Celestial AI and XConn added goodwill and financing complexity. MODEL ASSUMPTION: annual diluted-share growth is 2%-3% across all paths, never negative; this bounds preferred conversion, awards/SBC, acquisition issuance and some Google warrant vesting without crediting a short authorization as a five-year offset. The >960M-share falsifier forces the upper bound.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: HUMAN JUDGMENT: probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated; none comes from a legacy score, rank, IRR or hurdle. QQQ masses are fixed at 0.20/0.55/0.25. Within QQQ bear, 0.12 goes to a customer/demand setback and 0.08 to resilient AI execution. Within QQQ base, 0.30 goes to deceleration and 0.25 to broad execution. Within QQQ bull, 0.15 goes to participation with valuation reset and 0.10 to exceptional execution. The heavier lag weights reflect the high starting price, adjusted-EPS exclusions, hyperscaler concentration and dilution instruments. The upside weights reflect verified 37% company and 46% data-center Q2 growth, Q3 acceleration guidance and broad product exposure. QQQ is explicitly preferred in credible lag states. The resulting strict five-year price-outperformance probability is 0.43.

scenarios.name: QQQ bear / customer-program setback
scenarios.rationale: SOURCE ANCHOR: $4.40 normalized forward diluted EPS/share is the annualized $1.10 Q3 issuer-adjusted midpoint on 921M guided diluted shares; the bridge excludes recurring SBC and amortization. MODEL: total normalized earnings +10%/yr, diluted shares +3%/yr, terminal P/E 24x. Formula: $4.40 x ((1+0.10)/(1+0.03))^5 x 24 = $146.7037517445498; five-year price CAGR from $284.68 is -12.417597827560367%. This assumes lost/delayed custom programs, slower data-center demand and full dilution pressure; it is a material downside against QQQ bear.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus historical-price output returns the Nasdaq Class A close at $237.15 on 2026-10-07, and its key-ratio payload is timestamped 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT. Nebius's Q2 2026 SEC-furnished results report revenue of $582.3m, +454% YoY; Nebius AI cloud supplied $574.9m and reached $3.0bn annualized run-rate revenue (last-month revenue x12). Q2 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $236.2m, but GAAP operating loss was $175.9m and GAAP continuing net loss was $190.4m, or $0.68 per diluted share. Q2 cost of revenue $133.6m + product development $191.0m + SG&A $173.9m + D&A $259.7m = $758.2m total operating costs versus $582.3m revenue; SBC was $102.5m. This is not normalized profitability: D&A, SBC and financing costs are economically material. The reported-to-model revenue bridge is Q3 2025 $146.1m + Q4 2025 $227.7m + Q1 2026 $399.0m + Q2 2026 $582.3m = $1,355.1m TTM; the model instead starts from $3.2bn FY2026E, the midpoint of issuer guidance of $3.0bn-$3.4bn, because capacity and contracted deployments make TTM revenue stale. MODEL INFERENCE: value the still-GAAP-loss-making company as enterprise value/revenue, then deduct terminal net debt and divide by a fully diluted share denominator. Five-year terminal revenue equals $3.2bn times the stated scenario growth for five years; terminal enterprise value equals terminal revenue times the stated EV/revenue multiple. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the current valuation embeds substantial execution; only paths with roughly 35%-50% five-year revenue growth and sustained 9x-13x terminal EV/revenue produce attractive per-share outcomes after financing dilution.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Nebius can beat QQQ if its $37.5bn of reported remaining performance obligations at June 30, Microsoft/Meta deployments, higher ACV per MW, customer prepayments and expanding power footprint convert into sustained revenue growth while AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA economics remain strong. Q2 management reported four landmark deals averaging >$1bn, 70% of deals with prepayments covering 50%-60% of related capex, a 1-year-10-month estimated payback for Q2 deals, and a 5 GW year-end contracted-power target. The counter-thesis is that $237.15 already prices a large share of this success: GAAP operating profit and FCF remain negative after D&A and capex, customer concentration is high, capacity requires repeated debt/equity issuance, and terminal multiple compression can overwhelm revenue growth. QQQ is the better default in the 59% joint probability assigned to the three lag paths; modeled beat probability is 41%, an uncalibrated author judgment.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: when FY2026 results are filed, revenue below $3.0bn OR year-end Nebius AI-cloud ARR below $6.5bn (versus issuer guidance $3.0bn-$3.4bn revenue and $7bn-$9bn ARR) moves all win paths to their same-benchmark lag path and caps any rerun terminal EV/revenue multiple at 6x. Pre-breach financing trigger: at each quarterly/annual filing through 2027, gross funded debt above $18bn before reported Nebius AI-cloud ARR reaches $7bn, or an economic diluted-share sensitivity above 440m before ARR reaches $7bn, forces at least the base-lag denominator/net-debt assumptions and removes the bull-win path. Quality trigger: two consecutive quarters with Nebius AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin below 30% after ARR exceeds $4bn forces revenue growth assumptions down by at least 10 percentage points. Sources are the issuer's SEC-furnished results, debt filings and outstanding-share/equity-award disclosures. None of these forward windows was observable as breached at 2026-10-07; Q2 ARR was $3.0bn, Q2 AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin was 49.7%, and disclosed debt components remained below the $18bn trigger. Consequence is an explicit probability/model reset, not an automatic trade.

forecasts.limitations: GuruFocus deep-source attempts were incomplete: summary and key-ratio payloads were available and the exact 2026-10-07 close was returned, but annual and quarterly financial arrays were empty; segment retrieval hit a provider schema error; operating-data fields were legacy internet metrics and not decision-useful. GuruFocus exposed only 10-year ratio extrema, not a valid 15-year current-company operating history. The post-2024 Nebius business is also not economically comparable with historical Yandex because the divested businesses represented >95% of 2023 revenue/assets. SEC/issuer filings therefore control the model. Q2 statements are unaudited and the latest full financial period at the cutoff; no Q3 2026 earnings were public. Inferize terms were undisclosed. FY2026 revenue/ARR, RPO conversion, payback and prepayment coverage are management statements, not guaranteed cash flows. EV/revenue ignores timing of customer prepayments, GPU obsolescence, maintenance capex, taxes and lease/deferred-revenue claims except through conservative terminal net-debt and multiple judgments. The full-precision outputs reproduce the controller's evaluation of the authored expressions and remain subject to independent evidence-and-arithmetic review.
forecasts.capitalStructure: The traded instrument is Nasdaq Class A ordinary shares, €0.01 par value; SEC CIK 0001513845 and CUSIP N97284108 are primary-evidenced. The 2025 20-F cover identifies Class A Ordinary Shares, trading symbol NBIS, on Nasdaq Global Select Market. Class B is not the traded ticker but is included in per-share denominators. There is no ADR ratio or local-currency bridge: shares trade in USD and Nebius reports in USD. At June 30, 2026, 271,855,218 legal shares were outstanding (238,400,165 Class A; 33,455,053 Class B), excluding 50,185,726 treasury Class A shares. Q2 basic and diluted weighted averages were both 280,381,615 because loss made incremental claims antidilutive. Separate economic claims included 21,065,936 NVIDIA pre-funded warrant shares treated in EPS from issuance, about 10.0m awards excluded as antidilutive, and 65.4m gross if-converted shares excluded; 12.3m ATM shares remained available after 12.7m were sold through June. June cash was $8.0421bn; current debt $46.7m and noncurrent debt $8.4990bn. After quarter-end Nebius added a ~$775m secured facility at SOFR+2.50% due 2030, closed $5.75bn of new convertibles, and exchanged $800m of old notes for ~15.8m Class A shares. New-note initial conversion prices are $313.46 and $324.65; gross conversion exposure is not ignored. No preferred stock claim was disclosed. Rather than assume cash settlement or unfinanced repurchases, scenario denominators of 400m-460m cover the disclosed legal/economic claims plus further SBC/financing; terminal net debt ranges from $15bn to $0, with $5bn net cash only in the extreme bull. The bounds are author judgments; exact post-quarter claim reconciliation is an independent-review item.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: Uncalibrated subjective joint weights are independent of any legacy rank, conviction score or hurdle. QQQ bear mass 0.20 splits 0.08 failure / 0.12 recovery because weak capital markets hurt funding but a lower QQQ hurdle lets a modest positive NBIS CAGR outperform. QQQ base mass 0.55 splits 0.33 lag / 0.22 win because the current valuation requires exceptional growth and valuation durability. QQQ bull mass 0.25 splits 0.18 lag / 0.07 win because broad AI prosperity benefits Nebius demand but makes QQQ's 18% hurdle difficult; only the extreme scale/valuation path wins. Total lag mass is 0.59 and beat mass is 0.41. All revenue growth, terminal multiples, terminal net debt and share counts are author-selected scenario assumptions, not issuer forecasts except the common $3.2bn starting midpoint.

scenarios.name: Funding stress and multiple reset
scenarios.rationale: Failure path. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.15)^5*4-15)*1000/460. Start with $3.2bn FY2026E revenue; compound 15% for five years; apply 4x terminal EV/revenue; deduct $15bn terminal net debt; divide by 460m diluted shares. The expression converts billions of equity value and millions of shares to USD/share. The result is $23.35950434782607 and a five-year price CAGR of -37.09457528477219%, below QQQ's -4%.

scenarios.name: Contract conversion recovery
scenarios.rationale: Recovery path. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.35)^5*9-5)*1000/400. Revenue grows 35% annually for five years; 9x terminal EV/revenue reflects scarce scaled AI cloud; deduct $5bn terminal net debt; divide by 400m diluted shares. The result is $310.35040750000013 and a 5.5275458248484455% five-year price CAGR, which beats a -4% QQQ state. The 400m denominator assumes no unsupported repurchase and covers disclosed equity-linked claims.

scenarios.name: Execution below embedded expectations
scenarios.rationale: Central lag path. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.28)^5*7-8)*1000/430. Revenue grows 28% annually for five years, but terminal EV/revenue compresses to 7x; deduct $8bn net debt and divide by 430m diluted shares. The result is $160.38561382400005 and a -7.524123498232149% five-year price CAGR, showing that strong operating growth can still lose badly to 10% QQQ when valuation, financing and dilution are recognized.

scenarios.name: Scaled AI cloud compounder
scenarios.rationale: Base-state win path. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.45)^5*11-0)*1000/400. Revenue grows 45% annually for five years on large contracts, inference and enterprise mix; apply 11x EV/revenue; assume zero terminal net debt after customer prepayments and retained operating cash offset funding; divide by 400m diluted shares. The result is $564.0565975 and an 18.921371954846666% five-year price CAGR, above QQQ's 10%. Zero net debt is not a repurchase assumption and requires funding discipline plus realized margins.

scenarios.name: AI boom but capital intensity wins
scenarios.rationale: Bull-market lag path. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.40)^5*9-5)*1000/420. Revenue grows 40% annually for five years and earns 9x EV/revenue, but $5bn terminal net debt and 420m diluted shares absorb much of enterprise value. The result is $356.888838095238 and an 8.51804652888215% five-year price CAGR, below QQQ's deliberately difficult 18% hurdle; sector growth alone does not establish relative outperformance.

scenarios.name: Global AI-cloud leader
scenarios.rationale: Extreme upside. Formula: (3.2*(1+0.50)^5*13+5)*1000/400. Revenue grows 50% annually for five years as the $37.5bn June RPO, 5 GW pipeline and production inference create a global scaled platform; apply 13x terminal EV/revenue, add $5bn terminal net cash, and divide by 400m diluted shares. The result is $802.2500000000001 and a 27.601952372858607% five-year price CAGR. This is the only bull-QQQ win path and requires exceptional execution and valuation durability; it is not a target price chosen to force a win.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Viant's SEC filing identifies a Nasdaq-listed, USD-traded Class A common share and a cloud-based advertising-technology demand-side platform. Q2 2026 revenue was $104.254m, contribution ex-TAC was $60.204m, and adjusted EBITDA was $14.208m; Q3 guidance was $107.5m-$110.5m revenue and $18.5m-$19.5m adjusted EBITDA. At June 30, 2026, Viant reported 21.052546m Class A units, 45.402216m exchangeable Class B units, 7.506m RSUs, 0.487m PSUs, and 4.182m NQSOs. MODEL INFERENCE: if ViantAI/Outcomes and CTV improve advertiser outcomes and win spend while platform investment yields GAAP-like operating leverage, revenue and per-share earnings can compound despite substantial dilution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the loop is promising but unproven because Viant discloses no ViantAI-specific revenue, adoption, retention, or ROAS uplift; all current awards and maximum modeled future LTIP capacity therefore enter the denominator without forfeiture or exercise-proceeds credit.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: DSP can beat QQQ only if share gains sustain mid-teens or better revenue growth and a GAAP-like terminal operating margin reaches roughly the mid-teens despite recurring SBC, while realized issuance stays within the explicit conservative award-capacity bound. QQQ is the better default if growth settles near 10%, terminal operating margin remains near 10% or lower, privacy or customer-switching pressure persists, TVision integration disappoints, or acquisition/funding issuance exceeds the modeled denominator. The low starting price does not itself establish outperformance.
forecasts.falsifier: After 2026-10-07, if contribution ex-TAC growth is below 12% year over year for two consecutive reported quarters, versus 24% in Q2 2026, cap the next model's five-year revenue growth at 8% and terminal P/E at 18x until reacceleration is evidenced. If adjusted EBITDA/contribution ex-TAC is below 15% for two consecutive quarters, versus 24% in Q2 2026, remove the execution and breakout paths and use at most the recovery-margin path. If cash less debt falls below $75m, annualized total economic-unit growth exceeds 5%, or equity is issued outside the modeled LTIP award stack for financing or acquisitions, suspend all beat classifications at the next refresh until an explicit funding and fully diluted unit bridge is rebuilt. If by the FY2027 10-K Viant still discloses no measurable Outcomes/ViantAI adoption, spend-share, retention, or efficiency KPI and contribution ex-TAC growth is below 15%, do not credit AI with above-market growth. These are next-refresh consequences, not claims that a trigger is already breached.

forecasts.theme: AI-powered programmatic advertising; autonomous campaign decisioning and CTV share gains
forecasts.limitations: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus returned annual financial observations only from 2019 through 2025 plus TTM, not 15 years, consistent with the 2021 listing. GuruFocus summary, annual and quarterly financials, and key ratios were retrieved; its segment endpoint failed adapter validation. The SEC filing identifies one reportable operating segment and does not provide decision-useful product or AI revenue. Customer relationships generally lack long-term or exclusive obligations, customers can use competitors without significant switching cost, and privacy/data access, agency concentration, long sales cycles, AI execution, and TVision integration remain material risks. The September secondary offering was withdrawn and no shares were sold. MODEL LIMITS: the gross terminal denominator assumes all current awards vest or exercise, no forfeitures, no treasury-stock credit for NQSO proceeds, all 4.1m currently available LTIP shares are granted and terminal-vested, and each maximum 5% annual reserve increase through January 2031 is granted and terminal-vested immediately. This is more conservative than normal three-year RSU/PSU vesting and ignores the board's ability to reduce an annual reserve increase, but it is not a legal cap on non-LTIP acquisition or financing equity. HUMAN JUDGMENT: growth, margins, interest, tax, P/E multiples, scenario probabilities, and QQQ returns are subjective and uncalibrated. Scenario output fields contain the controller-supplied full-precision evaluation of the explicit arithmetic expressions and require independent verification before publication.
forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE SHARE/AWARD ROLL-FORWARD, millions except prices: at June 30, 2026, 21.052546 Class A units plus 45.402216 exchangeable Class B units equaled 66.454762 economic units. Class B units exchange one-for-one into Class A, so exchanges do not create new economic units. Outstanding awards were 7.506 RSUs, 0.487 PSUs, and 4.182 NQSOs. RSUs and PSUs generally vest over three years; NQSOs generally vest over three to four years, have ten-year contractual terms, carried a $6.05 weighted-average exercise price and 6.2-year weighted-average remaining contractual term, and 4.032m were vested/exercisable. The LTIP had 4.1m shares available for grant. Its reserve may increase each January through 2031 by 5% of prior December 31 outstanding capital stock, although the board may approve a smaller or zero increase. MODEL DILUTION BOUND: terminal economic units = (66.454762+7.506+0.487+4.182+4.100)*(1.05^5), in millions. It assumes zero forfeiture, gross one-for-one NQSO exercise with no treasury-stock or exercise-proceeds offset, full use and terminal vesting of today's reserve, full use and terminal vesting of five maximum annual reserve increases on a recursively expanded base, no Class B exchange dilution, and no buyback. The 2025 RSU roll-forward was 4.459 opening + 2.732 granted - 2.775 vested - 0.463 forfeited = 3.953 closing; H1 2026 was 3.953 opening + 5.396 granted - 1.700 vested - 0.143 forfeited = 7.506 closing. SOURCE OPERATING BRIDGE: TTM revenue was $388.498m, TTM operating income $9.115m, TTM consolidated net income $21.590m, issuer non-GAAP TTM net income $45.800m, and TTM SBC $29.385m, using filed FY2025 and H1 2026/H1 2025 values. The $45.800m figure excludes recurring SBC and is only a non-comparable diagnostic; neither reported nor non-GAAP TTM income is divided by a point-in-time share denominator or anchors terminal EPS. At June 30 cash was $193.053m, long-term debt was zero, and current liabilities were $149.853m. Each scenario starts from sourced TTM revenue, applies a positive tax rate, and divides terminal net income by the same explicit terminal fully diluted economic-unit formula.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: The six subjective joint-state weights sum exactly to 1.00. Their grouped QQQ marginals are exactly 0.12+0.08=0.20 bear, 0.25+0.30=0.55 base, and 0.15+0.10=0.25 bull, preserving the shared QQQ state masses. Lower DSP paths reflect weak customer commitment, privacy/competition, recurring SBC, and TVision integration; higher paths reflect share gains, CTV growth, and autonomous campaign adoption. Controller-supplied arithmetic classifies only Base / autonomous-ad execution and Bull / AI decisioning breakout as strict QQQ beats, so probabilityBeatQqq is 0.30+0.10=0.40. These are author judgments, not empirically calibrated probabilities, and the arithmetic remains subject to independent verification.

forecasts.thesis: Source facts: Micron's September 30, 2026 8-K identifies the listed security as $0.10-par common stock trading as MU on Nasdaq Global Select Market. Its attached FY2026 release reports $133.188 billion revenue, $84.969 billion GAAP net income, $74.33 diluted EPS on 1.143 billion weighted-average diluted shares, $89.68 billion operating cash flow, $27.37 billion net capital expenditures, and $62.31 billion adjusted free cash flow; Q4 revenue was $54.229 billion and GAAP diluted EPS was $32.87. The issuer's Q4 prepared remarks say the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bit supply is covered by agreements at significant year-over-year price increases, while the Q3 10-Q describes multi-year take-or-pay strategic customer agreements and also warns that DRAM and NAND selling prices have historically been extremely volatile. Model inference: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $74.33 is the common direct-per-share starting metric; five-year aggregate net-income growth, dilution/buyback bounds, and terminal P/E—not a selected stock CAGR—determine every outcome. Human judgment: the contracts and HBM mix may improve durability, but 80.7% FY2026 GAAP gross margin and a $1,088 starting price embed an extraordinary shortage cycle, so most probability remains on execution-lag outcomes.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: MU beats QQQ only if contracted supply, HBM leadership, and disciplined industry capacity let aggregate earnings remain durable or compound from the record FY2026 base while dilution stays controlled. At $1,088, the trailing GAAP P/E implied by issuer EPS is not itself the hard problem; the hard problem is whether record shortage-era EPS persists through 2031. The modeled base-win path requires 12% annual aggregate net-income growth, 0.5% annual share shrinkage, and a 14x terminal P/E. The QQQ alternative is superior in the three execution-lag paths because it diversifies away Micron's memory-pricing, customer, technology-transition, capex, and China risks and does not require one producer's record margin to persist.
forecasts.falsifier: Move probability from each execution-win path to its paired lag path if either (1) Micron reports GAAP gross margin below 60% for two consecutive quarters within the next eight reported quarters, using 10-Q/10-K statements; (2) disclosed SCA remaining performance obligations or covered-volume expectations fall more than 20% year over year without an explained conversion to recognized revenue, using issuer prepared remarks/filings; (3) calendar-2027/2028 HBM qualification or shipment commitments are delayed by two quarters or more, using issuer releases/filings; or (4) diluted weighted-average shares rise more than 1% year over year for two consecutive fiscal years absent demonstrably accretive M&A, using 10-K EPS footnotes. If FY2028 GAAP diluted EPS is below $74.33 despite the issuer's FY2027 supply commentary, retire the positive aggregate-growth assumptions and re-underwrite from normalized trough earnings. Conversely, two fiscal years with gross margin above 65%, no material SCA cancellations, and diluted shares flat/down would support retaining—not automatically increasing—the win weights.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT close at $386.05 and identifies the security as Ordinary Shares-Class A; SEC CIK 0000877212 and the Q2 2026 10-Q identify NASDAQ-traded Class A common stock. SEC arithmetic for the TTM ended 2026-07-04 is revenue $5,847m = $5,396m FY2025 - $2,601m H1 2025 + $3,052m H1 2026; GAAP operating income $858m = $700m-$378m+$536m; GAAP net income $539m = $419m-$248m+$368m; and summed diluted EPS $10.91 = $8.18-$4.81+$7.54. NORMALIZATION/MODEL INFERENCE: add back H2 2025 exit/restructuring $76m and acquisition/integration $17m, H1 2026 purchase-accounting $5m, acquisition/integration $3m and exit costs $16m; subtract Q2's nonrecurring $73m tariff-refund benefit. That yields normalized operating income about $902m. Below operating income, add back only H1 investment losses net of sale/other gains ($15m-$5m-$3m=$7m), while retaining interest, FX and debt-issuance costs. Applying a 19% tax assumption to the $51m pretax adjustment gives normalized net income about $580m = $539m + $51m*(1-0.19), or about $12.1 per diluted share on the 48.0m model base; the SEC-reported Q2 diluted weighted-average count was 48.129m. All bridge arithmetic is author-calculated and requires independent verification. SBC and intangible amortization are retained because equity compensation recurs and acquisitions/intangible consumption are part of Zebra's operating model; company non-GAAP TTM EPS of $19.29 (FY2025 $15.84 less H1 2025 $7.63 plus H1 2026 $11.08) is therefore not used as economic EPS. HUMAN JUDGMENT: durable AIDC leadership, machine vision, RFID and AI-assisted frontline workflows can compound, but the $386.05 price demands substantial growth and margin expansion relative to this conservative earnings base.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Zebra can beat QQQ only if organic growth remains mid/high single digit or better, Elo integration and machine-vision/frontline-AI products lift consolidated margins, and cash generation reduces refinancing risk without relying on buybacks. Q2 organic sales grew 9.2% (CF 7.5%, AVA 11.4%); management guided FY2026 reported growth of 14%-16%, including about 8 points from acquisitions/dispositions/FX, 23.5%-24.0% adjusted EBITDA margin, $20.75-$21.25 non-GAAP EPS and greater than $1bn FCF. Those are source facts, not forecast assumptions. The counter-thesis is that recent growth is acquisition/FX-assisted, Q2 margin includes a $73m tariff refund, services/software grew only 1.3% in Q2, Elo increased debt and goodwill, and machine-vision/AI revenue and attach rates are undisclosed. At conservative normalized EPS near $12.1, valuation is demanding; QQQ is the better default in the central and lag paths unless Zebra achieves durable revenue/margin upside.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if SEC/issuer quarterly releases show rolling-four-quarter organic net-sales growth below 3% AND adjusted EBITDA margin below 20% for two consecutive reports through 2028, move all central/strong weights to lag/downside and cease claiming a QQQ-beating base case. Financing trigger: if quarter-end total debt divided by TTM adjusted EBITDA exceeds 3.0x at any report through 2028, especially around the Term Loan A and revolving-facility maturity on May 25, 2027, remove any flat-share assumption and use at least 1.5% annual dilution plus downside multiples until leverage falls below 2.5x. The 2026-07-04 source baseline is $2.776bn gross debt and $157m cash; author arithmetic estimates TTM adjusted EBITDA about $1.389bn, or debt/EBITDA about 2.0x, so the threshold is not already breached; the independent reviewer should reproduce the ratio. AI-specific trigger: if Zebra begins disclosing machine-vision/software attach metrics and they undergrow consolidated organic sales for four consecutive quarters, treat Physical-AI value as zero rather than a multiple premium. Sources: Q2 2026 10-Q/Exhibit 99.1 and FY2025 10-K.

GuruFocus summary, annual/quarterly financials and key ratios were pulled before valuation; its financial history runs from 2017 but pre-2020 per-share history is zero/non-comparable, and its segment endpoint failed response-schema validation, so the SEC filing is the segment source. REPORTED-TO-SELECTED STARTING-EPS BRIDGE: FY2025 diluted GAAP EPS $3.41 minus H1 2025 diluted GAAP EPS $1.25 plus H1 2026 diluted GAAP EPS $2.26 equals selected TTM diluted GAAP EPS $4.42; GuruFocus reports $4.419 TTM. The model deliberately makes no non-GAAP add-back. The TTM includes acquisition intangible amortization of $269.9 million, calculated from source amounts as FY2025 $211.5 million minus H1 2025 $92.9 million plus H1 2026 $151.3 million; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes the H1 2026 $62.0 million contingent-consideration fair-value loss; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes H1 2026 $29.6 million of swap-related interest income; selected adjustment $0.00. It includes the $6.2 million debt-extinguishment loss; selected adjustment $0.00. It also retains reported taxes: the filing gives a 16.1% H1 2026 effective rate versus 28.8% in H1 2025, with H1 2026 affected by stock-compensation benefits and the swap settlement; selected tax adjustment $0.00. This is a causal GAAP base, not a normalized claim. COMPUTED SENSITIVITY CONTRACT: using 392.511287 million H1 diluted shares, the conservative lower-start formula 4.42-(29.6/392.511287)-(((1058.3*0.235)-170.4)/392.511287) equals $4.145102172666948, removing all H1 swap income and recasting H1 tax to the 2025 full-year 23.5% effective rate. The operating-adjusted upper-start formula 4.42+((62.0*(1-0.235))/392.511287)+((269.9*(1-0.235))/392.511287)-((29.6*(1-0.235))/392.511287)-(((1058.3*0.235)-170.4)/392.511287) equals $4.809693252311493. These are author calculations, not source-reported EPS. Substituting the lower start in the three authored winning branches produces five-year price CAGRs of -0.03290734056665845 in bear/resilient, 0.12499771003852023 in base/strong and 0.18572187973668375 in bull/strong; each remains strictly above its respective -0.04, 0.10 and 0.18 QQQ return. Therefore all three main-case win classifications and the 0.36 strict-win mass survive the conservative lower-start sensitivity. MODEL INFERENCE: AI and high-density compute can sustain unusually high demand for power, cooling and deployment infrastructure, but a direct GAAP-EPS model must absorb acquisition amortization, financing, cyclicality and dilution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: retain reported $4.42 rather than claim a normalized result; use aggregate post-financing, post-amortization GAAP earnings growth and terminal P/E, with no buyback benefit.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Vertiv can beat QQQ only if power-density, liquid-cooling, service and modular-deployment demand converts backlog into earnings growth far above aggregate Nasdaq-100 earnings while margins remain structurally higher. The cited filing supplies current evidence for that possibility: H1 2026 sales grew 26.7%, operating profit 47.0% and net income 81.7%, with strong Americas and APAC operating leverage. The offset is severe starting-valuation risk: $246.49 divided by selected SEC-derived $4.42 trailing diluted GAAP EPS is 55.76696832579186x. QQQ is the better default in the lag branches, where growth normalizes, acquisitions dilute GAAP earnings or terminal P/E compresses to 20x-32x. The deterministic main-case results show strict VRT wins only in bear/resilient, base/strong and bull/strong, for authored aggregate outperformance probability 0.36; the economic assumptions were selected independently rather than reverse-engineered from a desired rank. The computed lower-start sensitivity preserves those classifications, but its bull/strong CAGR of 0.18572187973668375 remains only narrowly above the 0.18 QQQ bull assumption.

The September 1 agreement requires approximately $1.45 billion upfront cash, subject to customary adjustments, plus up to $1.15 billion contingent cash and says existing resources will fund it.
