MODEL INFERENCE AND HUMAN-JUDGMENT FINANCING BOUNDS: Every 12%-29% aggregate earnings-growth input is after lost interest income, incremental interest, GAAP acquisition amortization, transaction/integration fees, earnout remeasurement and King; none is an unfinanced operating-growth rate. For the $1.45 billion upfront payment, resilient/strong branches assume a 4%-6% annual pretax cash/debt opportunity-cost range and lag branches 6%-8%. At a 23.5% tax rate and 392.511287 million diluted shares, the computed annual after-tax EPS costs are $0.11304133529286255-$0.16956200293929385 for 4%-6% and $0.16956200293929385-$0.2260826705857251 for 6%-8%. The model assumes the full earnout is paid in resilient/strong branches by the end of 2029 and zero earnout in lag branches when targets are missed; any fair-value remeasurement still flows through GAAP earnings. forecasts.probabilityRationale: These are subjective joint probabilities, not empirical or publisher-supplied odds. Each QQQ state's pair exactly preserves the shared 0.20/0.55/0.25 marginal. In QQQ bear, 0.08 goes to resilient execution because backlog and service demand may cushion a downturn, versus 0.12 to a simultaneous capex, integration and valuation shock. In QQQ base, 0.20 goes to strong execution because current sales, profit and margin evidence is exceptional, but 0.35 goes to lag because the starting mid-50s GAAP P/E leaves little room for merely good growth. In QQQ bull, 0.08 goes to execution strong enough to clear an 18% QQQ hurdle and 0.17 to company lag because broad AI prosperity can still favor the diversified index while VRT's multiple compresses. Main-case deterministic arithmetic identifies bear/resilient, base/strong and bull/strong as strict wins; aggregate authored mass is 0.36. The computed conservative lower-start sensitivity preserves all three classifications and 0.36 mass. Reweighting is exact if any sales/margin/backlog/acquisition-funding/leverage/King trigger trips: transfer 0.08 bear/resilient to bear/lag, 0.20 base/strong to base/lag and 0.08 bull/strong to bull/lag, preserving benchmark marginals and reducing strict-win mass from 0.36 to 0.00.

forecasts.whyBeatQqq: VEEV beats QQQ only if durable product expansion, Vault CRM migration and monetizable agentic workflows keep total revenue compounding near the high teens, GAAP operating margin reaches the mid-30s, dilution stays contained and the terminal multiple remains premium. A resilient Veeva path can beat a QQQ bear case; a 17% growth breakout can beat the QQQ base case; only a 20% category-creator path beats the QQQ bull case. forecasts.falsifier: Apply, do not merely observe, these pre-breach triggers using SEC/issuer quarterly reports: (1) if TTM total-revenue growth or subscription growth is below 10% for two consecutive reported quarters, cap remaining revenue CAGR at 8% and terminal P/E at 25x; latest Q2 growth was 18%/16%, so not breached. (2) If GAAP operating margin is below 25% for two consecutive quarters, use no more than 25% terminal operating margin; latest Q2 was 29.6%. (3) If diluted weighted-average shares grow above 2% YoY for two consecutive quarters, set forecast share growth to at least 2%; Q2 diluted shares fell to 165.057m from 167.685m. (4) Q2 disclosed one top-20 biopharma production deployment of Agentic Call Report. If by FY2028 Veeva has neither disclosed production AI deployment at at least three customers nor provided measurable AI-linked revenue, attach, or retention evidence, remove the 17%-20% AI breakout paths and reassign their mass to lag states. (5) A material security/privacy failure, failed Vault CRM migration causing disclosed customer losses, or funded debt above 1x TTM GAAP operating income forces a fresh model before use.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus identifies the quoted instrument as Mobileye Global Class A and supplied the $7.15 regular-session close at 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT. The Q2 2026 SEC filing identifies two operating segments: Mobileye is reportable and Moovit is within Other; Mentee Robotics is allocated to Mobileye. TTM consolidated GAAP revenue is $2,016m, operating loss is $4,175m, pretax loss is $4,116m and net loss is $4,062m; operating loss includes a $3,788m non-cash goodwill impairment in Q1 2026. Issuer Q3-2025/Q4-2025/Q1-2026/Q2-2026 adjusted operating income was $74m/$41m/$95m/$155m, totaling $365m; adjusted net income was $76m/$45m/$96m/$155m, totaling $372m; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.09/$0.06/$0.12/$0.19, totaling $0.46. Adjustments remove acquired-intangible amortization, SBC, goodwill impairment, acquisition expense and tax effects; Q2 also removes the R&D-law grant related to ordinary income from sold RSUs. Q2 customer concentration was 28%/16%/15%/14% and H1 was 27%/16%/16%/15%; China was $122m of Q2's $508m revenue. Mobileye purchases every EyeQ SoC from one supplier and describes substantial reliance on STMicroelectronics and Quanta. Mentee was a related-party acquisition: CEO Amnon Shashua was chairman, co-founder and a significant shareholder and received 37.83% of consideration, about $341m; CTO Shai Shalev-Shwartz was a co-founder and significant shareholder and received 13.07%, about $118m. Shashua's son and son-in-law were Mentee employees and received option consideration. Shashua recused himself; a four-member disinterested committee recommended the transaction, the Board approved it, and the Audit Committee approved it under the Related Persons Transaction Policy. MODEL INFERENCE: amortization and goodwill impairment are non-cash acquisition-accounting items, but SBC and Mentee retention consideration are recurring economic dilution, so scenarios do not treat adjusted EPS as distributable owner earnings and explicitly grow shares. The R&D-law benefit is only partly recurring because Q2 recognition covered H1. Concentration increases the chance that an OEM production change, ordering reset, China weakness or component constraint interrupts operating leverage. The Mentee conflict does not change disclosed cash/share arithmetic but weakens the capital-allocation prior and lowers Mentee-dependent breakout weight. HUMAN JUDGMENT: Mobileye beats QQQ only if higher-content Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur, Drive and robotaxi programs convert its installed base and nonbinding $24.5bn eight-year expected automotive pipeline into revenue growth and operating leverage; Mentee remains optionality, not required base revenue.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Mobileye starts from a depressed $7.15 price while retaining a scaled edge-AI platform: more than 258m vehicles had deployed its SoCs by 2026-06-27, it works with more than 50 OEMs, and it shipped 20.9m systems in H1 2026 versus 18.1m a year earlier. EyeQ volume growth, content per vehicle and production scaling of Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur and Drive could compound revenue faster than QQQ. Counter-thesis: four customers represented 73% of Q2 revenue and 74% of H1 revenue; China represented $122m of Q2 revenue; every EyeQ SoC came from one supplier; STMicroelectronics and Quanta are important dependencies; design wins are not purchase commitments; Q4-2025 revenue fell 9%; Q2-2026 revenue was approximately flat; high-content launches can slip; Intel controls voting power; and SBC/Mentee dilution can consume operating progress. Related-party Mentee economics add governance and capital-allocation risk to uncertain humanoid commercialization. QQQ is preferable if revenue remains low-single-digit, adjusted margin fails to hold above the mid-teens, concentration causes a material interruption, or premium-autonomy evidence does not arrive before valuation support fades.
forecasts.falsifier: Post-snapshot tests: (1) if any two consecutive subsequently reported quarters show year-over-year revenue growth at or below 0% AND issuer-defined adjusted operating margin below 15%, move all execution/breakout conditional weight to miss/severe assumptions and cap terminal P/E at 15x; Q2-2026 was approximately flat but margin was 31%, so the conjunction was not breached at the snapshot. (2) By 2027-12-31, qualifying launch proof must exist for at least two distinct programs among Surround ADAS, SuperVision, Chauffeur, Drive and robotaxi without a safety driver. Each must have post-snapshot issuer disclosure naming an OEM or paid fleet customer and either at least 50,000 cumulative paid production units or at least $25m trailing-12-month attributable revenue; SuperVision counts only once. If unmet, cap revenue CAGR at 5% and remove breakout. (3) If total A+B legal shares reach at least 1.12 times the matched-date 839.973490m baseline by 2028-12-31 without TTM adjusted net income at least 20% above the $372m Q3-2025-through-Q2-2026 aggregate, use at least 4% annual share growth and remove breakout. (4) If unrestricted cash plus marketable securities falls below $750m while TTM operating cash flow is negative, assume external financing and use the severe-execution share path. (5) If an EyeQ/ECU supply constraint or loss/material reduction of a greater-than-10% customer causes year-over-year revenue contraction in two consecutive reports through 2028-12-31, transfer all base-execution weight to launch slippage and cap terminal P/E at 15x. Sources are subsequent 10-Q/10-K filings and issuer reconciliations; consequences require a fresh forecast and are not automatic trading actions.

SEC identity is CIK 0001562088; the filing cover identifies DUOL as the Nasdaq-traded Class A common stock. FY2025 revenue/operating income/pretax income/net income were $1,037.589m/$135.570m/$182.410m/$414.065m. H1 2026 was $590.421m/$78.472m/$100.918m/$76.618m versus H1 2025 $483.008m/$56.957m/$81.460m/$79.916m. TTM line items use FY2025 plus H1 2026 minus H1 2025. Reported TTM net income is unusable because FY2025 included a $256.7m one-time valuation-allowance release. The source-to-model normalized common-earnings expression is ((182.410+100.918-81.460-5.766+5.000)*(1-0.24)); divide by 50.7m estimated diluted shares for normalized EPS. The -$5.766m reverses the nonrecurring H1 2026 Founder Award SBC benefit; +$5.000m removes the proposed legal-settlement charge. Ordinary SBC is retained as recurring economic compensation; acquisition/integration/earn-out and software-impairment items were individually small and are retained. Q2 2026 DAUs grew 23%, paid subscribers 17%, subscription bookings 10%, total bookings 8%, revenue 18%; GAAP operating margin was 11.4%. Q2 gross margin was 72.6%, with the company citing measured AI-feature rollout and AI cost efficiencies. MODEL INFERENCE: engagement and paid conversion can sustain a global subscription flywheel, while AI may improve teaching/content velocity; however bookings growth and heavy SBC show that user growth does not automatically become per-share earnings. HUMAN JUDGMENT: use a revenue-to-GAAP-operating-margin-to-tax-to-diluted-share EPS model, not reported provider EPS or adjusted EBITDA. The controller mechanically evaluated the disclosed formulas; Evidence & Risk must independently verify the arithmetic and source mapping.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: DUOL can beat QQQ only if its brand, experimentation dataset and AI-enabled learning features sustain high-teens revenue growth while GAAP operating leverage expands despite broader access to compute-intensive Video Call. The upside path requires 19% five-year revenue CAGR, 27% terminal GAAP operating margin and 36x terminal P/E even while shares grow 3% annually; this is demanding but causally tied to higher engagement, paid conversion and content efficiency. The central path deliberately assumes 15% growth, 22% margin, 25% tax, 3.5% share growth and 28x P/E, so QQQ can win through valuation compression or weaker monetization. QQQ is the better default if 8%-10% bookings growth becomes the durable revenue ceiling, AI lowers differentiation or gross margin, or equity compensation absorbs the operating gains.
forecasts.falsifier: All triggers are pre-breach at the 2026-10-07 snapshot. Trigger 1: if reported DAU growth is below 15% and paid-subscriber growth is below 12% year over year in the same two consecutive quarters (Q2 baselines 23% and 17%), cap forward revenue growth at the 8% downside path. Trigger 2: if subscription-bookings growth is below 8% in two consecutive quarters (Q2 baseline 10%), also move central probability to downside because cash demand is failing to follow engagement. Trigger 3: if GAAP gross margin is below 68% and GAAP operating margin below 10% in two consecutive quarters (Q2 baselines 72.6% and 11.4%), use the 14% terminal-margin downside case because AI/product costs are not scaling. Trigger 4: if company-reported pre-buyback dilution exceeds 4% for a full-year outlook or actual period (current guidance 3.5%-4.0%), use at least 4% annual share growth in every path and do not assume repurchases offset it. Sources are the subsequent 10-Q/10-K and shareholder letter; consequence is mechanical scenario reassignment, not a trade instruction.

forecasts.thesis: Lam is a high-quality but highly valued wafer-fabrication-equipment compounder. Its deposition, etch and clean leadership, growing installed base, CSBG, 3D NAND, HBM and advanced-packaging exposure can make revenue and margins outgrow semiconductor units. The latest TTM baseline is FY2026 GAAP: $23.232690bn revenue, $8.199795bn operating income, $7.265396bn net income and $5.76 diluted EPS. Normalized EPS is also $5.76: the model retains $0.386381bn SBC and all issuer non-GAAP exclusions rather than treating recurring compensation, acquired-intangible, financing, restructuring/optimization or tax volatility as free. The central risk is paying roughly 57x that baseline at $329.51 after a cyclical acceleration.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: LRCX narrowly beats a -4% QQQ bear return in the resilient 10%-growth path, and it beats positive-return QQQ states only where process intensity and installed-base service drive 18%-24% five-year revenue growth, GAAP operating margin reaches 40%-42%, dilution is contained without requiring buybacks, and a 40x-42x terminal P/E survives. Those higher-return paths reflect continued AI/HBM/3D scaling plus share gains, not merely semiconductor beta. In ordinary 12% growth/37% margin execution, multiple normalization leaves LRCX behind a 10% QQQ base return; QQQ is the superior default unless Lam converts record demand into durable per-share earnings at an exceptional rate.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: from the 2026-10-07 baseline (FY revenue $23.232690bn; June-quarter GAAP operating margin 37.4%; June-quarter CSBG $2.472390bn), if GAAP operating margin is below 30% for two consecutive reported quarters within the next eight quarters, or CSBG declines year over year in two consecutive quarters while systems revenue also declines more than 10% year over year, remove the 18%-24% growth paths and use at most the demand-digestion case. Severe trigger: if any subsequently reported TTM period has revenue below $20bn and GAAP operating margin below 30%, apply the deep-cycle case and a 20x cap. Financing trigger: if gross current plus noncurrent debt exceeds $7.5bn while cash is below $4bn, or diluted shares rise more than 2% year over year for two quarters, use at least +0.8% annual share growth and cap the multiple at 25x. Sources are quarterly SEC filings/earnings exhibits; consequences apply at the next refresh, not retroactively. None was breached by the latest public FY2026/June-quarter data.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies the Nasdaq-traded security as Class A common stock, RXRX. GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT close at $4.27. FY2025 revenue was $74.681m; H1 2025 and H1 2026 revenue were $33.968m and $14.143m, so the mechanical TTM baseline is $74.681m-$33.968m+$14.143m=$54.856m. Revenue is primarily collaboration revenue, not approved-product revenue. H1 2026 operating loss was $263.472m, net loss $248.509m, and operating cash use $187.048m. The stock-compensation note classifies $41.300m of H1 option/RSU expense; the cash-flow reconciliation separately reports a $41.713m stock-based-compensation adjustment. At 2026-06-30 cash plus restricted cash was $556.820m, notes and finance leases were $14.196m, and issued common-equivalent shares were 534.120235m. The detailed Q2 release says full-year 2026 cash operating expense guidance was lowered by $15m to $375m and runway without financing extended only into early 2028. MODEL INFERENCE: the five-year horizon therefore requires an explicit financing bridge. The model does not normalize milestone revenue or use EV/revenue. HUMAN JUDGMENT: RXRX beats QQQ only if clinical and partner validation creates large recurring product/royalty cash generation before dilution absorbs the value; current evidence does not establish that outcome.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: Recursion reported the first Genentech neuroscience target option, positive early REC-4881 FAP evidence, more than $500m of historical upfront/progress-based partner payments in the FY2025 filing, and potential future milestones that remain contingent and constrained from the accounting transaction price. REC-4881 had no approved medicine comparator in FAP and the company estimated more than 50,000 diagnosed US/EU5 patients, but these issuer estimates are not treated as realized sales. MODEL INFERENCE: only the program-validation and multi-program paths include product/royalty revenue and positive terminal FCF; the other four paths assign no going-concern platform EV beyond terminal net cash. HUMAN JUDGMENT: focused clinical successes can create convex value not replicated one-for-one in QQQ, but QQQ is the default when trials fail, commercialization slips, partner cash underdelivers, or financing occurs below modeled prices.
forecasts.falsifier: Review every 10-Q/10-K and material financing or clinical 8-K. SHARE TRIGGER, independent of partnership cash: if reported issued common-equivalent shares plus then-outstanding RSUs exceed the applicable calculated path by more than 5%, replace the denominator with the higher actual amount, replace future issue prices with the lower of the modeled price or actual trailing financing price, and move 5 percentage points from each positive-FCF path to the same-QQQ-state lag path; non-equity partner receipts cannot cure this breach. If an affected path would exceed then-available authorized-and-unreserved share capacity, set that path to zero until stockholder authorization or sufficient non-equity capital is evidenced. LIQUIDITY/PARTNER TRIGGER, tested separately: if cash plus restricted cash is below that path's next scheduled minimum, cumulative non-equity partner/product cash is below 50% of schedule at two consecutive quarter-ends, or required follow-on capital is unavailable at the modeled price, set unsourced future partner cash to zero until contracted, rerun the equity funding rule, and move 5 points from each positive-FCF path to financing-heavy progress or competitive lag. CLINICAL TRIGGER: if no issuer/SEC update by 2027-06-30 discloses an FDA-aligned registrational-development path for REC-4881, set both positive-FCF paths to zero probability and reassign their mass pro rata within their QQQ states to financing-heavy progress and competitive lag. forecasts.capitalStructure: SOURCE FACTS: 534.120235m Class A/Class B/exchangeable shares were issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, against 2.0bn authorized common shares. The company reported 27.468075m RSUs outstanding, $142.6m unrecognized RSU compensation over about three years, 29.3m shares available under the 2021 plan, 8.5m under the 2024 plan, and an unused $300m ATM. MODEL DEFINITION: terminal fully diluted shares equal 534.120235m starting issued common-equivalents + all 27.468075m existing RSUs at zero forfeiture and zero net-share withholding + scenario future plan awards + 5m author allowance for option exercise/other common equivalents + Tempus shares + funding shares. Existing RSUs and future awards are included once whether vested or unvested; ungranted pool capacity above the scenario award assumption is excluded, so no pool is double counted. The $142.6m is compensation-expense evidence, not an additional share line. Tempus stock shares equal stock dollars divided by that event-period issue price. Each period pre-financing cash equals prior cash minus cash operating/capex outflow plus non-equity partner/product cash plus Tempus license cash minus Tempus fee cash plus debt proceeds minus debt repayment; equity proceeds equal the positive amount needed to reach that period's minimum liquidity. The first $300m cumulative equity proceeds use the filed ATM and excess is a finite, scenario-derived follow-on assumption; funding shares equal proceeds divided by the stated issue price. The authorized-share ceiling is a legal cap, not evidence that follow-on financing will be available. No buyback or negative share growth is assumed.

Model inference: the direct per-share bridge removes all other income from normalized operations, values after-tax terminal GAAP operating profit, then adds scenario net financial assets and divides by diluted shares; this avoids treating volatile investment gains as recurring earnings while retaining the investment assets separately. Human judgment: NVIDIA can beat QQQ only if accelerated-computing demand broadens, CUDA/networking/system advantages preserve margins, disclosed infrastructure commitments earn acceptable returns, and growth offsets a demanding starting valuation.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: The differentiated upside is Data Center scale, CUDA/networking lock-in, rapid architecture cadence, and expansion from training into inference, sovereign AI, robotics and enterprise workloads. The direct bridge requires high-teens or better revenue compounding, durable 62%-65% GAAP operating margins and 30x-34x terminal after-tax operating-profit multiples in the strongest paths. The calculated distribution assigns a 0.26 strict-beat probability: strong AI platform execution beats 10% base-case QQQ and exceptional AI infrastructure expansion beats 18% bull-case QQQ. Q2 FY27 revenue grew 58%, ISG revenue grew 89% to $31.782B, ISG operating income reached $4.781B/15.0%, and FY27 guidance was $192B revenue and $24.37 GAAP diluted EPS. NORMALIZATION: TTM interest-and-other is -$0.433B before normalization: FY26 -$0.886B less H1 FY26 -$0.415B less Q3 FY26 -$0.178B leaves Q4 -$0.293B, then Q1 FY27 +$0.292B and Q2 -$0.254B. Dell disclosed $0.254B FY26 and $0.704B H1 FY27 fair-value gains on equity investments; removing the approximately $0.937B TTM gain makes normalized interest-and-other approximately -$1.370B. Applying a judgmental 19% recurring tax rate to $14.252B-$1.370B gives roughly $10.4B normalized common earnings, or roughly $15.8 per diluted share on the TTM implied share base. I retain all $0.727B estimated TTM SBC, intangible amortization, severance/payroll-tax/transaction/impairment charges and ordinary FX/hedging effects as economic recurring costs; no acquisition add-back is made. MODEL INFERENCE: Dell can compound if AI infrastructure volume persists and ISG margin remains well above its prior high-single-digit level, but the quote capitalizes much of the FY27 surge. HUMAN JUDGMENT: a direct GAAP earnings bridge, not provider non-GAAP EPS, is appropriate; scenarios therefore start from $151.197B TTM revenue and rebuild terminal common EPS from revenue growth, GAAP operating margin, interest/other, tax and diluted shares.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus supplied the $218.00 October 7, 2026 regular-session close, $3.073 billion TTM revenue, 1.655 GAAP TTM diluted EPS, 78.13% gross margin, 7.68% GAAP operating margin and 31.86% FCF margin. Okta's August 26 Q2 release reported $805 million revenue, 11% revenue growth, 12% subscription growth, 14% cRPO growth, 17% RPO growth, $107 million GAAP operating income, and $227 million FCF. It guided FY27 revenue to $3.216-$3.226 billion, FCF to $910-$930 million, and non-GAAP diluted weighted-average shares to approximately 184 million; Q2 actual non-GAAP diluted weighted-average shares were 184.448 million. The release defines FCF as operating cash flow less property/equipment purchases net of proceeds and capitalized software, and warns that FCF is volatile and working-capital sensitive. MODEL INFERENCE: identity remains a durable control point and AI agents can expand non-human identities, but no disclosed KPI quantifies incremental AI economics. HUMAN JUDGMENT: use the $3.216 billion low-end FY27 revenue guidance as a fiscal-period-end run-rate at January 31, 2027, then compound over the 1,710-day ACT/365.2425 interval to October 7, 2031. Value OKTA directly on acquisition-adjusted terminal FCF per diluted share. The model uses a 190 million normalized starting denominator and subtracts a $125 million recurring acquisition/capital reserve from terminal FCF in every path. No balance-sheet cash, discretionary repurchase, or acquisition synergy is credited.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: Q2 growth and cash conversion improved, and the issuer says Permiso adds identity threat detection and response capabilities, but primary sources through the cutoff do not disclose Permiso consideration, financing, seller equity, assumed awards, or post-combination costs. Okta for AI Agents is a separate subscription, while Agent SSO is included in core SSO at no extra charge; no paid AI-agent adoption, ARR, bookings, revenue, attach-rate, pricing or margin KPI was found. MODEL INFERENCE: if core identity sustains high-single- or low-double-digit growth while cash conversion expands, acquisition-adjusted FCF per diluted share can compound faster than QQQ; verified paid AI-agent adoption could add a second demand vector. HUMAN JUDGMENT: at $218, outperformance requires durable growth plus a premium terminal P/FCF multiple. The explicit acquisition reserve and dilution bridge make the stock carry its own Permiso uncertainty rather than deferring it. QQQ is the better alternative in mature-core, security-incident, integration-cost, or hyperscaler-bundling outcomes. This is a price-only comparison and does not include QQQ distributions.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply these pre-breach rules at every quarterly filing. (1) If cRPO growth is below 8% year over year for two consecutive quarters, rerun every path with revenue growth no higher than 7%, terminal FCF margin no higher than 28%, and terminal P/FCF no higher than 25x, retaining any already-lower input. (2) If TTM FCF margin is below 22% for two consecutive quarters, cap every terminal FCF-margin input at the lower of 22% or the then-observed TTM margin, cap terminal P/FCF at 25x, and perform a full margin re-underwrite; the prior 34%-38% margin cases may not survive unchanged. (3) If the next primary filing discloses Permiso cash consideration above $500 million, acquisition-related debt above $500 million, seller shares or assumed awards above 5 million shares, or annualized cash integration/post-combination costs above $75 million, replace the relevant $500 million cash/$500 million debt/5 million share/$75 million cost bound and rerun all paths before reliance. (4) If reported non-GAAP diluted shares exceed 190 million before January 31, 2028, replace the normalized base and retain at least 3% annual share growth in every path. (5) Assign no AI uplift until the issuer reports paid adoption, bookings, ARR, revenue, or another auditable monetization KPI for the separate AI-agent subscription. (6) A confirmed material compromise involving Okta's platform or a customer tenant, a regulator's enforcement finding tied to security/control failure, or issuer evidence of material customer-retention damage immediately triggers a full re-underwrite, a terminal multiple no higher than 20x, and no AI uplift pending auditable retention and remediation evidence.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Schrodinger licenses a physics-based molecular-design platform and runs collaboration and proprietary drug-discovery programs. FY2025 revenue was $255.869m: $199.500m software and $56.369m drug discovery. All top-20 pharma customers licensed its software and their 2025 ACV was $80.8m. The SEC-filed Q2 2026 release reported Q2 ACV of $29.6m, up 27%, and trailing-four-quarter ACV of $208m; excluding contribution ACV, Q2 ACV was $22.6m, up 23%, and trailing-four-quarter ACV was $196m. The issuer presents contribution separately because those arrangements are non-exchange grants rather than commercial software contracts. Q2 software revenue fell 10% as hosted licensing shifted recognition ratably; reported overall software gross margin was 71%, hosted revenue was 47% of Q2 software revenue and 30% on a trailing-four-quarter basis, and no hosted-only gross margin was disclosed. Bunsen launched in early access with an announced BMS deployment, but no Bunsen revenue, bookings, ACV or paid-user KPI was disclosed. MODEL INFERENCE: physics plus agentic workflow orchestration can increase user reach, calculation volume and commercial ACV, while collaborations provide lumpy optionality. COUNTER-THESIS: hosted migration depresses near-term revenue and overall software gross margin, competition and biopharma budgets can cap ACV, milestones are irregular, and clinical prediction has not eliminated failures. HUMAN JUDGMENT: value only the $196m ex-contribution commercial ACV base; assign no value to the $12m contribution-ACV difference, grants, clinical candidates, collaborator equity, royalties or unearned milestones. The framework assigns most mass to contraction or ordinary execution, not breakout; QQQ remains the default unless commercial ACV growth, software economics and cash-loss compression are demonstrated.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SDGR beats QQQ only if ex-contribution commercial software ACV compounds well above the 2026 10%-15% guide range for long enough, Bunsen broadens paid adoption without permanently impairing reported overall software gross margin, and R&D/collaboration economics reduce cash burn before dilution overwhelms per-share value. The breakout path applies 20% annual growth and a 9x terminal multiple only to the $196m commercial ACV base; contribution ACV is excluded rather than receiving an unsupported commercial multiple. The existing option, maximum RSU/PRSU and amended-plan pools are counted in full on top of the later legal-share base, with no option-exercise proceeds, forfeitures or buyback offset. This intentionally conservative dilution treatment makes ordinary execution less likely to beat QQQ. Drug milestones and clinical assets receive no separate pipeline NPV, preventing milestone double counting. QQQ is superior if commercial ACV growth remains near or below guidance, hosted/Bunsen economics fail to support margin, cash use persists, or disclosed equity overhang converts into still more shares.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply these source-linked pre-breach rules at each subsequent quarterly filing or annual proxy. (1) If trailing-four-quarter ACV excluding contribution ACV grows less than 15% year over year in any two consecutive quarterly reports through 2028-12-31, eliminate breakout in every QQQ state and transfer its probability to contraction in the same QQQ state. (2) If by 2027-12-31 the issuer has not disclosed an auditable Bunsen paid-production KPI such as revenue, bookings, commercial ACV, paid seats or paid calculation volume, eliminate breakout and transfer its weight to contraction; an announced deployment without a monetization KPI does not qualify. (3) If cash, restricted cash and marketable securities fall below $250m before positive trailing-12-month operating cash flow, use at least the contraction financing and dilution inputs and rerun all paths. (4) If reported overall software gross margin is below 65% in two consecutive quarterly reports through 2028-12-31, cap every commercial-ACV terminal multiple at 3x, retaining any already-lower multiple, and rerun. (5) At each proxy or 10-K, recompute same-date participating legal shares plus outstanding options plus maximum-performance RSUs/PRSUs plus shares available for new awards. If that disclosed sum exceeds the applicable modeled pre-financing bound of 74.805628+12.395566+3.932521+5.364521+3 for breakout, the same expression plus 6 for execution, or plus 9 for contraction, replace the denominator with the higher disclosed sum and rerun; contraction financing shares remain additional. (6) If common plus limited-common legal shares exceed 90m by 2029-12-31 without at least $200m of incremental net financing cash retained, reject breakout and execution dilution assumptions and rerun with contraction financing. Each consequence requires a fresh forecast; none is an automatic trading action.

forecasts.limitations: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus quote and ratios reported $27.29 at 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT in USD. Its current annual-financial window exposed only 2019-2025 plus TTM, while a prior source run exposed 2017-2025; no 15-year claim is made. GuruFocus segments failed schema validation, so exact SEC segment facts replace that endpoint. GuruFocus reported TTM diluted EPS of negative $0.737 and EBIT per share of negative $2.06; neither is used because reported earnings contain volatile equity gains and the core remains loss-making. Q2 10-Q/release facts include H1 revenue $117.476m, operating loss $90.341m, net loss $54.051m, SBC $17.867m and operating cash use $48.904m. Q2 net income was dominated by the $57.2m Ajax payment, consisting of $47.2m equity proceeds and a $10m collaboration milestone. HUMAN JUDGMENT: the model excludes the equity gain and uses $55m drug-discovery revenue, equal to the $65m FY2026 guidance floor less the disclosed $10m Ajax milestone, as a transparent normalized base. It excludes all $12m of contribution ACV from terminal value rather than assuming non-exchange grants receive commercial growth or multiples. MODEL INFERENCE: ACV is an operating metric, not GAAP revenue; all growth rates, multiples, cash-use amounts, future-award buffers, financing price and probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated. The full-count award method is intentionally more dilutive than treasury-stock accounting: every April 1 option is counted one-for-one, no exercise proceeds are credited, maximum RSUs/PRSUs and the full amended pool are counted, and any awards settled between April 1 and the July 29 legal-share date may be double counted. The controller mechanically evaluated the authored formulas into the stated terminal prices and annualized returns; independent arithmetic reproduction remains required. Research only; no rank, publication, approval, sizing or trade action is claimed.

The proxy's same-date participating legal-share count was 74.547503m. Stockholders approved the 3.0m plan increase in June and the August S-8 registered the amended plan. H1 SBC was $17.867m and remains an economic cost. HUMAN-JUDGMENT SHARE BRIDGE: start from the later 74.805628m legal count; add all 12.395566m options one-for-one with zero exercise proceeds; add all 3.932521m maximum RSUs/PRSUs; add the entire 5.364521m available pool; then add scenario-specific future awards beyond currently approved pools of 3m breakout, 6m execution or 9m contraction. Because the July legal count postdates the April proxy, the model deliberately does not subtract April-to-July exercises or vesting from the April pools; any overlap is double counted rather than risking understatement. Contraction additionally adds exactly 16m financing shares for $200m issued at the author-assumed $12.50 average price. Execution and breakout assume no external financing. No forfeiture, net settlement, treasury-stock option offset, option proceeds, buyback, acquisition, preferred/NCI claim, ADR or FX bridge is credited. Formula units are USD millions and millions of shares, yielding USD per share.

QQQ bear totals exactly 0.20 from 0.08 contraction, 0.08 execution and 0.04 breakout; QQQ base totals exactly 0.55 from 0.22 contraction, 0.24 execution and 0.09 breakout; QQQ bull totals exactly 0.25 from 0.12 contraction, 0.10 execution and 0.03 breakout. The heavier contraction weight in stronger QQQ states reflects idiosyncratic biotech/software execution and the possibility that SDGR lags a concentrated AI index. These are subjective, uncalibrated judgments rather than frequencies, scores or translated legacy ranks. The same economic path has the identical authored formula, terminal price and stock annualized return across benchmark states. On the controller's strict comparisons, only bear/execution, bear/breakout and base/breakout beat QQQ, producing a 0.21 aggregate beat probability.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies Alibaba Group Holding Limited, CIK 0001577552, and BABA on NYSE. GuruFocus' 2026-10-07 quote returned a $107 USD regular-session price. The retrieved GuruFocus financial payload exposed FY2017-FY2026 annual columns plus quarterly data (10 annual years, so this draft makes no 15-year coverage claim); its segment endpoint failed schema validation, so exact segment facts come from SEC-filed issuer releases. FY2026 revenue was RMB1,023,670m, operating income RMB50,150m, net income attributable to ordinary shareholders RMB105,904m, and diluted EPS per ADS RMB44.00/US$6.38. June-2026-quarter revenue was RMB268,953m; China e-commerce revenue was RMB110,900m; AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue was RMB48,437m, external cloud revenue grew 45%, and the segment reached 12% adjusted EBITA margin. TTM Jun-2026 GuruFocus facts in USD were revenue $150,234m, operating income $6,070m, net income $10,113m, diluted EPS $4.25 (more precise summary value $4.246), and provider-calculated EPS without NRI $4.82. REPORTED-TO-NORMALIZED BRIDGE: $150,234m revenue -> $6,070m reported operating income -> $10,113m reported net income -> $4.25 reported diluted ADS EPS -> $4.82 GuruFocus EPS without NRI, a +$0.57/ADS provider normalization. The provider page does not itemize that $0.57, so it is corroboration rather than a silently accepted model scalar. The issuer's June quarter provides the item-level check: RMB10,537m GAAP net income attributable/RMB3.71 diluted ADS (US$0.55) versus RMB20,715m non-GAAP net income/RMB8.52 diluted ADS (US$1.26); exclusions include non-cash SBC, investment gains/losses, goodwill/intangible impairments and other items, while Q1 SBC itself was RMB3,304m. MODEL INFERENCE: volatile mark-to-market/disposal gains and impairments should not be capitalized; ordinary commerce/cloud operating costs recur; SBC is economically retained through nonnegative share growth; and recurring treasury/equity-method income is bounded explicitly, not treated as mark-to-market upside. Each terminal formula independently rebuilds common earnings from reported-USD revenue growth x operating margin, minus interest plus a capped recurring non-operating/equity-method contribution, tax, NCI, diluted ADS growth and a P/E. This is a fresh direct per-ADS model, not an EV model or an unfinanced buyback assumption.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Alibaba can beat QQQ if AI-cloud growth remains materially above consolidated growth, cloud operating leverage and lower quick-commerce losses restore consolidated margins, and the August equity-funded AI build earns returns above its dilution. The starting $107 price is modest relative to normalized earnings only if the investment trough is temporary. QQQ is the superior default if capex and equity issuance continue without durable common-earnings conversion, China commerce weakens, RMB depreciation offsets local growth, or policy/VIE/geopolitical risk keeps the terminal multiple compressed. The draft deliberately includes credible QQQ-win paths in all QQQ states; no rank, prior score or hurdle informed the probabilities.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: starting with results for the quarter ending 2026-12-31, if AI Cloud and Compute Services external revenue growth is below 20% year over year for two consecutive reported quarters OR segment adjusted EBITA margin is below 8% for two consecutive quarters, replace every scenario with at most 5% reported-USD revenue growth, at most 5% consolidated operating margin and at most 14x. Funding/dilution trigger: if reported issued ordinary shares exceed 21.2bn (2.65bn ADS-equivalent at 8:1) at any month-end through 2027-10-31, absent a split, use at least 2.5% annual share growth in every remaining case. Cash-return trigger: if trailing-twelve-month FCF remains below negative RMB50bn at both 2027-06-30 and 2027-09-30 while gross debt rises above the Mar-2026 $37.724bn current-plus-long-term baseline, remove the 18x-plus paths. Sources are the SEC-filed quarterly release, HK monthly returns and GuruFocus debt pages; consequence is a mandatory rerun, not an automatic trade.
forecasts.nextAction: Evidence & Risk must independently reconcile GuruFocus's $4.25-to-$4.82 TTM normalization by item; verify June-2026 current and noncurrent debt, all convertible/exchangeable-note dilution, the September monthly return and award exercises; stress RMB/USD translation; and reperform all seven scenario calculations from the disclosed formulas and $107 starting price. North Star PM must then decide whether the reviewed beat probability merits either Core or AI-theme ranking; no portfolio action is authorized here.
forecasts.theme: China commerce plus full-stack AI cloud/compute; AI infrastructure investment and Qwen monetization with VIE, FX and dilution risk.
forecasts.limitations: Source/model boundary: GuruFocus supplied summary, annual/quarterly financials and ratios, but the segments call returned malformed structured content; segment facts were therefore replaced with exact SEC-filed issuer disclosures. Only 10 annual columns were exposed in the retrieved financial payload, not 15. The $4.82 TTM EPS-without-NRI is source-provided, but its +$0.57/ADS bridge from reported EPS is not itemized on the extracted page; independent verification is required before publication. The terminal recurring non-operating/equity-method contribution is author judgment and may overstate Ant/treasury income; it explicitly excludes mark-to-market and disposal gains. Scenario USD growth is a reported-USD assumption combining local operating growth and RMB/USD translation; no local-currency return is compared directly with QQQ, but the implied FX split remains judgment rather than a forward FX quote. June balance-sheet debt details were only partially extractable. China VIE enforceability, regulation, export controls, audit/listing risk, data rules, competition, AI-chip access, model economics and state-policy priorities can overwhelm the numerical cases. Dividends are excluded because the common comparison is price-only.
forecasts.capitalStructure: The NYSE security is an ADS; each ADS represents eight ordinary shares. The SEC/HK September-2026 monthly return reported 19,901,959,514 issued ordinary shares and zero treasury shares at month-end, equal to 2,487.744939m ADS-equivalent; this is the model denominator. June-end GuruFocus showed 2,401m ADS-equivalent before the August placement. Alibaba completed a 710m-ordinary-share placement (88.75m ADS-equivalent), 3.57% of post-deal shares, at HK$112.70, raising about HK$79.7bn net for full-stack AI; no repurchase offset is assumed. May awards covered 61,716,712 ordinary shares and August awards 1,932,300, both to be satisfied with new shares; June-quarter SBC was RMB3,304m. GuruFocus Mar-2026 debt was $4,095m current plus $33,629m long-term; June filing separately showed $8,092m noncurrent convertible notes and $1,369m exchangeable bonds within liabilities. June cash and other liquid investments were $69,933m, but Q1 FCF was negative $6,584m after $9,975m capex. Model interest remains $1.5-$1.8bn and share growth 0.5%-2.5%; no preferred claim is modeled, NCI is explicitly deducted, and convert/award dilution is bounded via positive share growth rather than ignored.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: Human judgment, not a calibrated frequency: probabilities are conditional execution weights chosen after observing 45% external cloud growth, 12% cloud adjusted EBITA margin, weak consolidated operating conversion, negative FCF and the 3.57% placement dilution. QQQ bear mass 0.20 is split 0.08 failure/0.12 stabilization; QQQ base 0.55 is split 0.20 investment trap/0.25 recovery/0.10 AI upside; QQQ bull 0.25 is split 0.15 index outruns/0.10 platform breakout. The asymmetry recognizes that strong cloud evidence is real but consolidated earnings, financing and FX can reverse the result. The full-precision evaluated paths imply a 0.20 strict probability of beating the matched QQQ states; the probabilities and all operating, financing, dilution and valuation assumptions remain author judgment subject to independent review.

scenarios.name: Investment failure in QQQ bear
scenarios.rationale: Author assumptions: $150,234m TTM reported-USD revenue is flat annually as local gains are offset by RMB weakness/disposals; 3% terminal operating margin; $1,600m interest; $2,500m recurring pre-tax treasury/equity-method income excluding marks/disposals; 22% tax; $500m NCI; 2.5% annual ADS growth for awards/funding; 12x terminal P/E. The expression returns USD per ADS. QQQ can still win if BABA destroys value despite a weak index.

scenarios.name: Stabilization in QQQ bear
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 6% annually after RMB translation; terminal operating margin recovers to 7%; interest $1,500m; recurring non-operating/equity-method income $4,000m; 20% tax; $500m NCI; ADS count grows 1.5%; 16x. This requires cloud leverage but not a return to FY2025 consolidated margins.

scenarios.name: Investment trap in QQQ base
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 3%; terminal operating margin only 5%; interest $1,800m after continued financing; recurring non-operating/equity-method income $3,000m; 22% tax; $600m NCI; 2.5% ADS growth; 13x. QQQ wins because AI capex and dilution fail to create consolidated common earnings.

scenarios.name: Core recovery in QQQ base
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 8%; terminal operating margin reaches 9% as cloud and quick-commerce unit economics improve; interest $1,500m; recurring non-operating/equity-method income $5,000m; 20% tax; $500m NCI; 1% ADS growth; 18x. This is the central path but remains below Alibaba's historical peak consolidated margin.

scenarios.name: AI cloud upside in QQQ base
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 12%; terminal operating margin 12%; interest $1,600m; recurring non-operating/equity-method income $6,000m; 20% tax; $600m NCI; 0.5% ADS growth; 22x. It requires AI-cloud growth to broaden into consolidated operating leverage and equity funding to reduce later debt needs.

scenarios.name: Good company but QQQ outruns
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 8% and terminal operating margin reaches 9%, but policy/FX risk holds recurring non-operating income to $4,000m and the multiple to 16x; interest $1,600m, tax 21%, NCI $600m and ADS growth 1.5%. Business execution is respectable while QQQ's 18% CAGR wins.

scenarios.name: AI platform breakout in QQQ bull
scenarios.rationale: Reported-USD revenue grows 15%; terminal operating margin reaches 15%; interest $1,800m despite the compute build; recurring non-operating/equity-method income $7,000m; 20% tax; $700m NCI; 0.5% ADS growth; 24x. This demanding path requires durable full-stack AI monetization and still charges for dilution, financing, tax, FX and NCI.

forecasts.thesis: SentinelOne sells a subscription cybersecurity platform built around endpoint/cloud telemetry, autonomous response and an expanding data/AI security layer. Source facts are 21% Q2 revenue growth, 22% ARR growth, expansionary but undisclosed NRR, and 13% growth in customers above $100k ARR. The investable thesis is that platform consolidation, machine-speed threats and security labor scarcity sustain mid-teens or better growth while sales efficiency improves. The counter-thesis is that Microsoft/CrowdStrike/Palo Alto bundle comparable functionality, AI features commoditize, cloud/inference costs suppress the 72% GAAP gross margin, acquisitions fail, and SBC keeps per-share value from tracking revenue. FY2026/H1 losses, Q2 negative FCF and 60.5m anti-dilutive securities make a revenue-to-EV model with explicit claims and dilution more honest than normalized EPS.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SentinelOne beats QQQ in this distribution only in the 22% base-upside and 24% bull-winner revenue paths, where durable strategic multiples and dilution falling to 3% overcome the starting valuation. The 16% central path produces only a 3.24% annualized price return and does not beat the 10% QQQ base case. AI for Security and Security for AI can expand the addressable workload, but no separate Purple AI/AI-SIEM ARR proves monetization. At $25.31, upside is operationally leveraged but highly valuation- and dilution-sensitive; QQQ is the better default if revenue settles near single digits, gross margin stays under pressure, or recurring SBC prevents per-share operating leverage.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: if reported ARR growth is below 12% year over year for two consecutive reported quarters through FY2028, cap forward revenue growth at 8% and terminal EV/revenue at 3.5x. Margin trigger: if GAAP gross margin is below 68% for two consecutive quarters through FY2028, remove all 7.5x-8.0x outcomes and use at most 4.0x. Dilution trigger: if issuer-guided or reported diluted shares exceed 390m before annual revenue exceeds $1.5bn, use at least 6% annual share growth. Cash-quality trigger: if trailing-four-quarter adjusted FCF after ITA payments is negative at Jan. 31, 2028, do not credit terminal net cash above $300m. Sources are each 10-Q/10-K and earnings release; consequence is immediate scenario repair and lower QQQ-beat probability, not a sell order.
forecasts.nextAction: Evidence & Risk must independently verify the 2026-10-07 close, TTM arithmetic, no-funded-debt conclusion, $345.7m claims bridge, treatment of the signed $150m commitment, full-precision controller arithmetic, and diluted-share paths; then North Star PM may compare the accepted 20% QQQ-beat probability with the QQQ alternative. Obtain Purple AI/AI-SIEM attach, inference-cost and cohort evidence before any conviction upgrade. This is an author draft, not portfolio or trade authority.
forecasts.theme: AI-native cybersecurity platform; endpoint, cloud, data/SIEM and AI-workload protection
forecasts.limitations: The issuer discloses no Purple AI/AI-SIEM ARR, attach rate, inference cost, module cohort economics or numeric NRR. Only FY2022-FY2026 plus TTM GuruFocus history exists, not 15 years. GuruFocus segment retrieval failed; SEC evidence establishes one reportable segment and geographic mix only. The $25.31 current price is the GuruFocus 2026-10-07 16:00:02 EDT close and still requires reviewer cross-check to an independent exchange-aligned source. Terminal EV/revenue multiples, growth, terminal cash and probabilities are author judgments, not company guidance. Strategic investments may be illiquid or impaired; the ITA liability is ILS-denominated and accrues 7% interest; the signed $150m investment is subject to closing conditions. SBC is recurring, award vesting is performance-sensitive, and share growth can exceed the modeled paths. Controller-supplied terminal values and CAGRs require independent arithmetic verification before acceptance.
forecasts.capitalStructure: NYSE:S is exchange-registered Class A common stock; Class B has identical economic rights but superior voting/conversion rights. July 31 issued/outstanding was 340.152m Class A plus 5.884m Class B; Aug. 21 was 342.184m plus 5.865m. The model uses FY2027 issuer guidance of 361m diluted weighted-average shares, then positive annual dilution. Potential dilution at July 31 included 43.218m RSUs, 2.174m PSUs, 8.469m options, 2.364m unvested restricted shares already legally outstanding and 0.876m ESPP. No preferred shares or funded debt were reported. $658.0m liquid/marketable assets less $162.3m ITA liability and the signed $150m strategic-investment commitment gives $345.7m conservative excess liquidity; $155.2m non-marketable strategic investments receive no credit. Acquisitions consumed $263.811m cash and issued 6.818m shares plus options. The exhausted repurchase authorization supplies no offset.
forecasts.probabilityRationale: Joint masses exactly preserve QQQ bear 0.20, base 0.55 and bull 0.25. Conditional stock execution weights are subjective and uncalibrated, derived from disclosed 21% revenue/22% ARR growth versus 13% large-customer growth, unquantified NRR, 72% GAAP gross margin, acquisition integration, negative Q2 FCF and heavy award overhang. Bear-Q: 60% severe/40% recovery. Base-Q: 36.36% bear/45.45% central/18.18% upside. Bull-Q: 60% lag/40% win. These are not inferred from legacy ranks or hurdle rates. Only the 0.10 base-upside and 0.10 bull-winner outcomes strictly beat their QQQ states, so the modeled QQQ-beat probability is 0.20. QQQ wins the other 0.80 of joint probability mass.

scenarios.name: QQQ bear / S severe commoditization
scenarios.rationale: Revenue contracts 5% annually as bundled suites win; 2.0x terminal EV/revenue reflects persistent losses. All current excess liquidity is consumed by ITA payments, the signed investment, integration and operations, so terminal net cash is $0. Diluted shares grow 6% from 361m with no repurchase offset. Formula in USD millions and USD/share: ((1098.704*(1-0.05)^5*2.0)+0)/(361*(1+0.06)^5)=3.519591008301467; CAGR=(3.519591008301467/25.31)^(1/5)-1=-0.3260308606982487. QQQ bear at -4% wins.

scenarios.name: QQQ bear / S resilient recovery
scenarios.rationale: Cybersecurity demand persists despite a weak index: revenue grows 8%, terminal EV/revenue is 3.5x, terminal net cash is $300m after claims, and diluted shares grow 5%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.08)^5*3.5)+300)/(361*(1+0.05)^5)=12.914612687294273; CAGR=(12.914612687294273/25.31)^(1/5)-1=-0.12590658559316037. Despite recovery, S loses to QQQ bear at -4%.

scenarios.name: QQQ base / S suite-pressure bear
scenarios.rationale: Revenue slows to 8%, 3.0x EV/revenue reflects margin and competitive disappointment, only $100m terminal net cash survives, and diluted shares grow 5%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.08)^5*3.0)+100)/(361*(1+0.05)^5)=10.728600038608661; CAGR=(10.728600038608661/25.31)^(1/5)-1=-0.15773223080601384. QQQ base at 10% wins.

scenarios.name: QQQ base / S platform central
scenarios.rationale: Land-and-expand and adjacent modules support 16% revenue growth, operating leverage earns 5.5x EV/revenue, current conservatively bridged $345.7m net liquidity is maintained, and diluted shares grow 4%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.16)^5*5.5)+345.7)/(361*(1+0.04)^5)=29.684536772239905; CAGR=(29.684536772239905/25.31)^(1/5)-1=0.03239912121256627. QQQ base at 10% wins.

scenarios.name: QQQ base / S AI-security upside
scenarios.rationale: AI security, data/SIEM and cloud expansion sustain 22% growth; profitable scale earns 7.5x EV/revenue, cash generation lifts terminal net cash to $700m, and dilution slows to 3%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.22)^5*7.5)+700)/(361*(1+0.03)^5)=54.889331063178446; CAGR=(54.889331063178446/25.31)^(1/5)-1=0.16745233621274602. S beats QQQ base at 10%, but this path lacks isolated AI ARR evidence.

scenarios.name: QQQ bull / S execution lag
scenarios.rationale: Revenue grows 14% but platform economics disappoint versus a powerful QQQ tape; terminal EV/revenue is 4.0x, terminal net cash is $300m, and diluted shares grow 4%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.14)^5*4.0)+300)/(361*(1+0.04)^5)=19.949019704900785; CAGR=(19.949019704900785/25.31)^(1/5)-1=-0.04648861520288439. QQQ bull at 18% wins.

scenarios.name: QQQ bull / S category winner
scenarios.rationale: SentinelOne captures AI-security workloads and compounds revenue 24%; durable platform quality supports 8.0x EV/revenue, terminal net cash reaches $900m after claims, and dilution falls to 3%. Formula: ((1098.704*(1+0.24)^5*8.0)+900)/(361*(1+0.03)^5)=63.722907233602356; CAGR=(63.722907233602356/25.31)^(1/5)-1=0.2028201287661. S narrowly beats QQQ bull at 18%; this is the demanding category-winner path.

forecasts.thesis: Gartner combines recurring, mostly subscription Insights revenue, proprietary decision data and executive distribution. forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: GuruFocus identified NAS:PANW as Palo Alto Networks and returned a split-adjusted 2026-10-07 close of $405.57. The FY2026 SEC filing and issuer supplement report $11.480bn revenue (+24.5%), including $9.200bn subscription/support; NGS ARR was $9.10bn (+63%) and RPO $21.2bn (+34%). CyberArk and Chronosphere materially changed the perimeter, so trailing growth is not purely organic. MODEL INFERENCE: platformization can sustain double-digit growth, but the starting price requires extraordinary earnings growth and/or a persistently exceptional multiple. This is a direct adjusted-earnings-per-share framework: terminal revenue times adjusted operating margin, plus normalized other income, less tax, divided by diluted shares, times an adjusted P/E. HUMAN JUDGMENT: most credible outcomes lag QQQ; only the extreme execution case supports QQQ-like or better returns from $405.57.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: PANW beats QQQ in this matrix in the bear-QQQ/upside-PANW branch and in all three extreme PANW branches; it clears base and bull QQQ only in the extreme branch. The bear/upside win reflects weak QQQ (-4%) rather than a high absolute PANW return (3.59%). The extreme path requires roughly 28% five-year revenue compounding, adjusted operating margin near 38%, minimal net dilution and a 65x terminal adjusted P/E, plus unusually strong CyberArk/Chronosphere integration and AI-security demand. In the author's downside and central operating cases, and in the upside case against base or bull QQQ, even healthy execution does not overcome the initial valuation; QQQ is the superior default alternative.
forecasts.falsifier: Pre-breach operating trigger: beginning with the first two fiscal quarters reported after 2026-10-07, if NGS ARR growth is below 18% year over year in two consecutive quarters, or RPO growth is below 18% year over year in two consecutive quarters, use at most the central branch and eliminate upside/extreme branches; the 2026-07 baselines were 63% and 34%, respectively. Margin/dilution triggers: if FY2027 adjusted operating margin is below 27%, shift every non-downside execution branch down one tier; if issuer-guided or realized diluted shares exceed 870m before FY2027 year-end, independently shift every non-downside execution branch down one additional tier. Each breached condition causes one tier shift, simultaneous margin and share-count breaches cause two tier shifts, and the downside branch remains floored at downside. The issuer's then-current FY2027 guide was 29.5% margin and 844m-847m shares. Financing trigger: if cash plus short- and long-term investments less current and noncurrent notes is below negative $5bn at two consecutive fiscal quarter ends, and adjusted diluted EPS for the trailing four quarters ended at each of those same quarter ends has grown less than 15% year over year versus the comparable prior-year trailing-four-quarter period, use the downside branch. Sources are subsequent SEC 10-Q/10-K filings and issuer earnings exhibits. Forecast consequences are mechanical branch elimination, tier shifts, or downside selection, not trade instructions.

The full-precision outputs make QQQ the winner in every downside and central outcome and in the base/bull upside outcomes; the strict-beat mass is 0.11 from bear-upside plus all three extreme outcomes.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: Camtek's 2025 Form 20-F identifies Nasdaq ticker CAMT as ordinary shares, NIS 0.01 par value, not an ADR; SEC CIK is 0001109138. GuruFocus reports the 2026-10-07 16:00 EDT close at $152.20 and TTM diluted EPS of $0.604. The SEC-filed Q2 2026 release reports H1 revenue $254.902m, GAAP operating income $54.493m, financial income $15.126m, pretax income $69.619m, tax expense $14.669m, net income $54.950m, diluted shares 51.433m and diluted EPS $1.09. Q2 revenue was $133.243m, GAAP operating margin 20.4%, financial income $6.977m and diluted shares 51.520m. It labels $7.7m of Q2 tax expense one-time; its non-GAAP reconciliation also excludes acquisition-related expense and SBC, but this model does not add those back. Management guided Q3 revenue to $158m-$160m and H2 revenue to grow more than 30% from H1. MODEL INFERENCE: normalized forecast 2026 GAAP diluted EPS is ((54.950+7.700)+(((335.0*0.22)+14.0)*(1-0.12)))/52.0 = $2.688961538461539. The $335m H2 revenue assumption is modestly above the greater-than-30% H2/H1 guidance floor; 22% H2 GAAP operating margin is near Q1's 22.4% and above Q2's acquisition-affected 20.4%; $14m H2 financial income is below H1's $15.126m; 12% tax is deliberately above the roughly 10% H1 rate after subtracting only the issuer-labeled one-time tax amount; and 52m diluted shares exceed Q2's 51.520m. The 22% GAAP operating margin retains ordinary SBC, recurring acquired-intangible amortization, inventory step-up/purchase accounting and transaction costs; no acquisition-cost normalization is claimed. HUMAN JUDGMENT: apply a terminal P/E to this direct normalized forecast diluted EPS. Scenario operating growth means aggregate normalized-net-income growth; share-count growth separately captures future dilution. COUNTER-THESIS: $152.20 already requires durable AI/advanced-packaging growth. Cyclicality, China/export exposure, customer/order timing, Israeli operating risk, competition, SBC, converts and valuation de-rating can make QQQ superior even if Camtek grows.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: Camtek can beat QQQ only if advanced-packaging, HBM and 2.5D/3D inspection demand converts its more-than-$600m 2026 year-to-date order intake into durable high-teens-or-better normalized-net-income growth, dilution stays controlled and a premium terminal multiple survives. The issuer presentation said about 75% of revenue was from advanced-packaging applications, mostly AI products, creating focused upside and concentration. QQQ is the better default if AI capex broadens away from Camtek, export controls or Israeli disruption impair shipments, margins weaken, converts and awards dilute owners, or valuation de-rates. Under the explicit bridge and six authored cases, only the 10% breakout path strictly beats its paired QQQ return.
forecasts.falsifier: Review each quarterly SEC-filed 6-K/issuer release and each annual 20-F through 2031. If rolling four-quarter revenue growth is below 10% AND non-GAAP operating margin is below 25% for two consecutive reported quarters, cap all central/upside normalized-net-income growth at 9% and terminal P/E at 25x and rerun. If advanced-packaging revenue is below 60% of total for two consecutive quarters without an offsetting disclosed growth category, or disclosed orders/backlog no longer support next-twelve-month revenue growth above 10%, remove the 20%-27% growth paths. If diluted weighted-average shares exceed 55m before 2029, or any SEC filing adds equity-linked financing beyond the disclosed 2030 notes and 2018 Plan, use at least 3% annual share growth in every path and rerun; there is no EPS-accretion exception. Because the 2025 20-F reports China at 49% of revenue, suspend ranking and rebuild after the first 6-K, 20-F or issuer earnings release that (a) quantifies newly blocked, delayed or license-dependent China deliveries/orders at at least 10% of prior-year company revenue, or (b) reports a China-revenue decline of at least 25% year over year for a disclosed quarter or fiscal year and attributes most of it to export restrictions. Also suspend after any Israeli disruption prevents production or shipment for one full reported quarter.

forecasts.thesis: Forgent is a newly public Up-C electrical-distribution manufacturer whose FY2026 revenue was 59% data-center exposed and whose $3.0bn backlog plus stated $5.8bn post-expansion capacity can support several years of growth if data-center and grid projects convert on time. The stock nevertheless embeds substantial success: conservative FY2026 fully exchanged normalized income is about $144.9m, or $0.476 per 304.699m diluted equivalent shares, after retaining recurring amortization, SBC and sponsor costs. Five-year upside therefore requires both backlog conversion and durable operating-margin expansion without financing or equity dilution overwhelming per-share earnings.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: A beat requires Forgent's scarce engineered-to-order powertrain capacity to turn a $2.4-$2.6bn FY2027 revenue guide into sustained growth toward the stated $5.8bn capacity, while operating margin rises and share growth stays low. QQQ is the better default in ordinary execution because FPS begins at a very high multiple of normalized earnings, is concentrated in project/capacity execution, and carries variable-rate debt plus a material TRA liability. The draft's credible lag states therefore lose to QQQ; only exceptional AI-infrastructure demand, margin, dilution, and terminal-valuation persistence plausibly beats the QQQ bull case.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply the downside framework, not the base/bull paths, if either (a) reported backlog falls below $2.0bn or aggregate book-to-bill is below 0.8x over any two consecutive reported quarters through fiscal 2027, versus $3.0bn backlog and 3.3x Q4 FY2026 book-to-bill, or (b) the Powertrain expansion is not online by fiscal Q4 2027 while adjusted EBITDA margin is below 20%. Apply at least the 5%-6% dilution/high-interest paths if, by the FY2027 10-K, total economic diluted equivalents exceed 330m or gross debt exceeds $750m while trailing CFO less capex is negative. These are pre-breach thresholds at the model date; consequence is removal of the strong/AI-supercycle paths until two subsequent quarters restore the KPI.

forecasts.probabilityRationale: Six joint outcomes preserve exact QQQ masses: bear 0.12+0.08=0.20, base 0.25+0.30=0.55, bull 0.15+0.10=0.25; total 1.00. Conditional weights are subjective, uncalibrated judgments based on the short history, $3.0bn backlog, FY2027 step-up, $5.8bn stated capacity, high starting valuation, debt/TRA, and execution/dilution risks. They are not derived from a prior rank, conviction score, expected IRR, or hurdle. Each formula starts with FY2026 revenue $1,420.059m, subtracts scenario cash interest after applying an operating margin that retains D&A/SBC/sponsor costs, applies a full-C-corp tax rate, divides by 304.699m diluted economic equivalents grown at the stated positive rate, and applies a terminal P/E. QQQ wins in all ordinary paths by design of the economics, not by forcing a target beat probability.

This requires sustained AI/data-center and grid scarcity, successful expansion, cash-funded working capital and valuation persistence; it is the only path intended to have a plausible chance to beat a QQQ bull case.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies GE Vernova Inc., CIK 0001996810, with one NYSE-traded GEV common-stock class; 266,333,581 shares were outstanding at 2026-06-30.[1] GuruFocus reports $997.09 USD at 2026-10-07 16:00:02 EDT.[6][8] The 2Q26 SEC tables report 1H26 segment revenue/EBITDA of $10,449m/$1,842m Power, $6,597m/$1,200m Electrification and $3,459m/negative $657m Wind; 2Q reported segment EBITDA margins were 18.8% Power and 18.4% Electrification, correcting the rejected draft's unsupported 19.1% figures.[2][3] The reconciliation separately reports 1H26 Other EBITDA of negative $239m, D&A of $760m, non-operating benefit income of $253m, net interest and other financial income of $100m, $4,445m of gains on purchases/sales of business interests, and $623m tax provision.[4] MODEL INFERENCE: this revision does not use or claim an exact normalization of GuruFocus's $34.935 TTM GAAP diluted EPS to its $19.41 EPS-without-NRI. Instead every terminal price is rebuilt directly from twice the sourced 1H26 segment-revenue bases, independently assumed five-year segment revenue growth and terminal EBITDA margins, explicit corporate/Other cost and D&A percentages, net financial cost/income, tax, common-attributable deduction, diluted-share roll-forward and terminal P/E. The transparent starting operating schedule is the source formula 1H26 segment EBITDA $2,384m less Other EBITDA $239m less D&A $760m, before separately disclosed restructuring, business-interest gains, separation, non-operating, interest and tax items; no normalized starting EPS is asserted.[3][4] HUMAN JUDGMENT: Power and Electrification can compound through equipment scarcity and services while Wind can recover, but the $997.09 entry valuation requires unusually strong execution and exposes holders to large multiple compression.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: SOURCE FACTS: 2Q26 revenue was $11.104B, organic revenue grew 12%, adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.3%, Power organic revenue grew 14%, Electrification organic revenue grew 29%, and Wind lost $275m of segment EBITDA.[1][3][10] RPO was $176.284B: $87.821B equipment and $88.463B services, with 97% and 54%, respectively, expected within five years.[1] MODEL INFERENCE: GEV beats QQQ only if Power and Electrification sustain high-single- to mid-teens growth, retain or expand high-teens EBITDA margins, Wind approaches profitability, and terminal earnings remain valuable despite a P/E below the current price divided by GuruFocus's unreconciled $19.41 metric. COUNTER-THESIS/QQQ ALTERNATIVE: QQQ is superior if backlog conversion, capacity, tariffs, service estimates or product quality hold segment growth/margins below the execution cases; if Wind remains structurally loss-making; if Prolec integration raises D&A/capital needs; or if GEV's terminal P/E compresses to the 20s. HUMAN JUDGMENT: probabilities are subjective and uncalibrated; controller-calculated outcomes, a new exact-hash author confirmation, independent Evidence & Risk review and North Star PM judgment are still required. This is research, not sizing or trade authority.

forecasts.thesis: SOURCE FACTS: SEC identifies Argan, Inc., CIK 0000100591, and its $0.15-par common stock as AGX on NYSE. GuruFocus reported the 2026-10-07 16:00:03 EDT close at $404.39. The FY2026 10-K reported $944.606m revenue, $134.701m operating income, $160.509m pretax income, $22.735m tax, $137.774m net income and $9.74 diluted EPS. The Q2 FY2027 10-Q reported six-month revenue $674.930m, operating income $102.200m, pretax income $120.657m, tax $21.292m, net income $99.365m and diluted EPS $7.01, versus prior-year six-month $431.403m/$54.397m/$65.422m/$7.597m/$57.825m/$4.09. The reported TTM bridges are revenue=$1,188.133m (944.606+674.930-431.403), operating income=$182.504m (134.701+102.200-54.397), pretax=$215.744m (160.509+120.657-65.422), reported tax=$36.430m (22.735+21.292-7.597), and net income=$179.314m (137.774+99.365-57.825). GuruFocus independently reports TTM EPS of $12.649. NORMALIZATION: use the 10-Q-disclosed 21% U.S. statutory rate rather than reported tax because option exercises and award settlements created favorable tax benefits (Q2 FY2026 tax was only $0.361m); normalized starting EPS is ((160.509+120.657-65.422)*(1-0.21))/14.181, approximately $12.019. Retain recurring SBC inside operating expense: FY2026 SBC $7.867m and six-month FY2027/prior-year SBC $4.458m/$3.453m; do not add it back. Retain recurring investment income in pretax earnings but reset terminal other income by scenario because rates and liquid balances vary. ValCor closed 2026-07-31 for $9.4m and contributed no H1 revenue/earnings; transaction costs were immaterial, so no adjustment. FX translation remained OCI, not net income. MODEL INFERENCE: the $2.5b backlog, active power projects, and data-center cooling-vessel award can sustain revenue, but the current earnings surge and valuation embed strong execution. HUMAN JUDGMENT: a revenue-growth × terminal operating-margin + other-income → normalized tax → diluted-share → P/E model is more decision-useful than carrying reported EPS growth forward.
forecasts.whyBeatQqq: AGX can beat QQQ if its $2.5b backlog converts on schedule, constrained power-EPC supply and AI/data-center load growth replenish awards, Power margins remain disciplined, and Industrial data-center work scales without repeating the Q2 margin decline. The balance sheet has no borrowings and substantial liquidity, supporting bonding capacity and selective growth without required debt issuance. The counter-thesis is that $404.39 already capitalizes unusually strong margins, favorable tax benefits in reported results, investment income and backlog visibility: fixed-price cost overruns, project delays/cancellations, declining backlog, customer concentration, falling interest rates or multiple compression can make QQQ the superior default. The model therefore includes several credible lag states and does not count dividends because the shared benchmark basis is price-only.
forecasts.falsifier: Apply prospectively from the 2026-10-07 snapshot. Primary threshold: if consolidated backlog is below $1.75b at two consecutive reported quarter-ends (latest sourced baseline $2.5b at 2026-07-31; $2.9b at 2026-01-31), shift all Base/Bull execution weight to the Reset/Severe paths and prefer QQQ pending a new award bridge. Execution threshold: if trailing-four-quarter GAAP operating income divided by revenue is below 10% at any two consecutive quarterly filings, remove terminal margins above 12%; latest reported TTM values are $182.504m/$1,188.133m. Dilution threshold: if diluted weighted-average shares exceed 15.0m before 2028-07-31 without at least proportionate acquired normalized earnings, raise modeled share growth to the observed rate and re-underwrite. Financing/claims threshold: any funded debt above $250m, or a probable project/legal loss above $100m, requires explicit interest/claims deductions before retaining a QQQ-beating path. Sources are each future 10-Q/10-K and related 8-K; consequence is model refresh, not an order.
forecasts.nextAction: Evidence & Risk should independently verify the TTM bridge, 21% normalized tax, recurring SBC treatment, ValCor consideration and deferred compensation, current/noncurrent debt, bonding and claim exposures, share ledger, backlog, $404.39 close, every expanded formula, and every full-precision controller result. It should also verify the proposed security identity from the SEC filing cover. forecasts.limitations: GuruFocus Deep Source Pack attempts covered summary, exact-date quote/OHLC, annual and quarterly financials, key ratios, operating data and segment data. The returned annual series exposed FY2017-FY2026 plus TTM, not 15 years, so no 15-year claim is made. GuruFocus operating fields were zero/unusable and its OHLC and segment endpoints failed response-shape validation; SEC segment disclosures control, while GuruFocus summary/key-ratio output corroborates the exact-date close. The SEC model uses $m and consolidated USD reporting; it does not isolate project-level AI revenue, backlog profitability or exact foreign-currency sensitivity. Backlog is not guaranteed revenue and is concentrated in Power. Q2 disclosed four customers at 15%, 15%, 13% and 13% of revenue. Percentage-of-completion estimates, fixed-price execution, tariffs, turbine/labor availability, $0.9b bonded obligations, $104.3m other bonds and the disputed U.K. project can create nonlinear losses. Contract liabilities of $627.020m mean gross cash/investments are not all distributable. Terminal other income, growth, margin, tax, share growth and P/E are author assumptions, not company guidance. Future acquisitions/financing are not fully bounded; scenarios allow dilution but no assumed buyback offset. Price return excludes the $0.70 quarterly dividend declared after Q2. The controller mechanically evaluated the disclosed formulas and price CAGRs at full precision; independent Evidence & Risk review must reperform the arithmetic and verify the source inputs before acceptance.
